title.zh: 卷九十七 列傳第八十五: 西域
title.raw: 卷九十七 列傳第八十五: 西域 Volume 97 Biographies 85: Western Region

sentences.zh: 列傳第八十五西域

translations.literal: Biography 85: The Western Regions
translations.idiomatic: Biography 85: The Western Regions

sentences.zh: 《夏書》稱：「西戎即序。」

translations.literal: The Book of Xia says: "The Western Rong were brought to order."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Xia records: "The Western Rong were brought into order."

sentences.zh: 班固云：「就而序之，非盛威武致其貢物也。」

translations.literal: Ban Gu said: "To bring them to order by going to them—that is not to display overwhelming might and thereby obtain their tribute goods."
translations.idiomatic: Ban Gu wrote: "To bring them into order by going among them is not to display overwhelming might merely to extract their tribute."

sentences.zh: 漢氏初開西域，有三十六國。

translations.literal: When the Han first opened the Western Regions, there were thirty-six states.
translations.idiomatic: When the Han dynasty first opened the Western Regions, there were thirty-six states.

sentences.zh: 其後，分立五十五王，置校尉、都護以撫之。

translations.literal: Later they were divided into fifty-five kingships, and colonels and protectors-general were installed to pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: Later the region was split among fifty-five rulers, and colonels and protectors-general were appointed to keep them in hand.

sentences.zh: 王莽篡位，西域遂絕。

translations.literal: When Wang Mang usurped the throne, contact with the Western Regions ceased.
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Mang seized the throne, ties with the Western Regions were cut off.

sentences.zh: 至於後漢班超所通者五十餘國，西至西海，東西萬里，皆來朝貢。

translations.literal: As for the Later Han, the more than fifty states opened by Ban Chao extended west to the Western Sea; for ten thousand li east and west, all came to court with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Later Han, Ban Chao reconnected more than fifty states westward to the Western Sea; for ten thousand li east and west, all sent envoys to pay tribute.

sentences.zh: 復置都護、校尉，以相統攝。

translations.literal: Protectors-general and colonels were again installed to oversee them jointly.
translations.idiomatic: Protectors-general and colonels were reinstated to supervise them.

sentences.zh: 其後或絕或通，漢朝以為勞弊中國，其官時置時廢。

translations.literal: Thereafter contact was sometimes broken and sometimes restored; the Han court considered it a drain that exhausted China, and these offices were at times established and at times abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward ties were severed and restored by turns; the Han court judged the effort a burden that wore down the empire, and the frontier offices were created and abolished intermittently.

sentences.zh: 暨魏、晉之後，互相吞滅，不可復詳記焉。

translations.literal: From Wei and Jin onward the states swallowed one another, and they can no longer be recorded in full detail.
translations.idiomatic: From the Wei and Jin periods on, the states devoured one another until they could no longer be traced in any detail.

sentences.zh: 道武初，經營中原，未暇及於四表。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Daowu's reign, he was consolidating the Central Plain and had no leisure to attend to the four quarters.
translations.idiomatic: In the early years of Emperor Daowu, he was busy securing the Central Plain and had no time for the outlying regions.

sentences.zh: 既而西戎之貢不至，有司奏依漢氏故事，請通西域，可以振威德於荒外，又可致奇貨於天府。

translations.literal: Before long tribute from the Western Rong ceased to arrive; the responsible officials memorialized that, following Han precedent, the Western Regions should be opened, whereby imperial prestige might be displayed beyond the wilds and rare goods brought into the imperial treasury.
translations.idiomatic: When tribute from the western peoples stopped arriving, officials urged reopening the Western Regions along Han lines, arguing that this would extend imperial prestige into distant lands and bring rare goods into the state treasury.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「漢氏不保境安人，乃遠開西域，使海內虛耗，何利之有？

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The Han did not secure their borders and settle their people, yet opened the Western Regions far away, draining the realm within—what profit was there in that?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied: "The Han failed to secure their borders and protect their people, yet opened the Western Regions at vast distance and emptied the empire—what good did that do?

sentences.zh: 今若通之，前弊復加百姓矣！」

translations.literal: If we open them now, the former evils will again be laid upon the common people!"
translations.idiomatic: If we open them now, the same harms will fall on the people again!"

sentences.zh: 遂不從。

translations.literal: He therefore did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: He refused.

sentences.zh: 曆明元世，竟不招納。

translations.literal: Throughout the Mingyuan era they were never courted or received.
translations.idiomatic: Through the entire Mingyuan reign the court never sought or accepted their overtures.

sentences.zh: 太延中，魏德益以遠聞，西域龜茲、疏勒、烏孫、悅般、渴槃陀、鄯善、焉耆、車師、粟特諸國王始遣使來獻。

translations.literal: In the Taiyan period Wei virtue was heard ever farther abroad; the kings of Kucha, Kashgar, Wusun, Yueban, Khotan, Shanshan, Karashahr, Cheshi, and Sogdiana in the Western Regions first sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: During Taiyan, Wei prestige spread ever farther; kings of Kucha, Kashgar, Wusun, Yueban, Khotan, Shanshan, Karashahr, Cheshi, and Sogdiana in the Western Regions sent their first embassies with tribute.

sentences.zh: 太武以西域漢世雖通，有求則卑辭而來，無欲則驕慢王命，此其自知絕遠，大兵不可至故也。

translations.literal: Emperor Taiwu held that although the Western Regions had been in contact with Han, when they had requests they came with humble words, and when they had no desire they were arrogant toward royal commands—this was because they knew themselves to be utterly remote and that great armies could not reach them.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taiwu reasoned that in Han times the Western Regions had come with humble words when they wanted something and treated imperial orders with arrogance when they did not—knowing how remote they were and that no great army could reach them.

sentences.zh: 若報使往來，終無所益，欲不遣使。

translations.literal: If envoys were exchanged in return, in the end there would be no benefit; he wished not to send envoys.
translations.idiomatic: Exchanging envoys would bring no lasting gain, he thought, and he meant to send none.

sentences.zh: 有司奏：「九國不憚遐險，遠貢方物，當與其進，安可豫抑後來？」

translations.literal: The responsible officials memorialized: "The nine states did not fear distant hardship and sent regional products from afar; we should advance with them—how can we beforehand restrain those who come later?"
translations.idiomatic: Officials argued: "These nine states braved vast distances to offer tribute; we should meet them halfway—how can we discourage others who may follow?"

sentences.zh: 乃從之。

translations.literal: He thereupon consented.
translations.idiomatic: He agreed.

sentences.zh: 於是始遣行人王恩生、許綱等西使。

translations.literal: Thereupon he first dispatched the envoys Wang Ensheng, Xu Gang, and others on a western mission.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent envoys Wang Ensheng, Xu Gang, and others westward—the court's first such mission.

sentences.zh: 恩生出流沙，為蠕蠕所執，竟不果達。

translations.literal: Ensheng went out beyond the shifting sands and was seized by the Rouran; in the end he did not reach his destination.
translations.idiomatic: Ensheng crossed the shifting sands but was captured by the Rouran and never completed the journey.

sentences.zh: 又遣散騎侍郎董琬、高明等多齎錦帛，出鄯善，招撫九國，厚賜之。

translations.literal: He again sent the Attendant Gentleman of the Scattered Riders Dong Wan, Gao Ming, and others bearing much silk and brocade; they went out through Shanshan to win over and comfort the nine states and richly rewarded them.
translations.idiomatic: The court next sent Attendant Gentleman Dong Wan, Gao Ming, and others laden with silk and brocade through Shanshan to win over the nine states with generous gifts.

sentences.zh: 初，琬等受詔：便道之國，可往赴之。

translations.literal: At first Wan and the others received the edict: any state along the convenient route might be visited.
translations.idiomatic: Wan and his party had orders to call on any state that lay conveniently along their route.

sentences.zh: 琬過九國，北行至烏孫國。

translations.literal: Wan passed through the nine states and traveled north to the state of Wusun.
translations.idiomatic: Wan passed through the nine states and went north to Wusun.

sentences.zh: 其王得魏賜，拜受甚悅。

translations.literal: Its king received Wei's gifts, bowed in acceptance, and was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The Wusun king received Wei's gifts with a bow and was delighted.

sentences.zh: 謂琬等曰：「傳聞破洛那、者舌皆思魏德，欲稱臣致貢，但患其路無由耳。

translations.literal: He said to Wan and the others: "I have heard that Poluona and Zheshe both admire Wei's virtue and wish to submit and send tribute, but only fear that they have no route.
translations.idiomatic: He told Wan's party: "I hear that Bactria and Zheshe both admire Wei and wish to submit and send tribute, but they have no road by which to reach you.

sentences.zh: 今使君等既到此，可往二國，副其慕仰之誠。」

translations.literal: Now that you envoys have come here, you may go to the two states and fulfill their longing admiration."
translations.idiomatic: Since you have come this far, you might visit those two states and answer their desire to pay court."

sentences.zh: 琬於是自向破洛那，遣明使者舌。

translations.literal: Wan thereupon went himself toward Poluona and sent Ming as envoy to Zheshe.
translations.idiomatic: Wan went on to Bactria himself and sent Ming as envoy to Zheshe.

sentences.zh: 烏孫王為發導譯，達二國，琬等宣詔慰賜之。

translations.literal: The king of Wusun provided guides and interpreters; reaching the two states, Wan and the others proclaimed the edict, comforted them, and bestowed gifts.
translations.idiomatic: The Wusun king furnished guides and interpreters; reaching both states, Wan and his colleagues announced the imperial edict, offered reassurance, and distributed gifts.

sentences.zh: 已而琬、明東還，烏孫、破洛那之屬遣使與琬俱來貢獻者，十有六國。

translations.literal: Before long Wan and Ming returned east; Wusun, Poluona, and their kindred sent envoys who came with Wan to offer tribute—sixteen states in all.
translations.idiomatic: When Wan and Ming returned east, envoys from Wusun, Bactria, and related states accompanied them with tribute—sixteen states in all.

sentences.zh: 自後相繼而來，不間于城，國使亦數十輩矣。

translations.literal: From then on they came in succession without pause at the capital; foreign envoys numbered several tens of missions.
translations.idiomatic: After that embassies arrived in an unbroken stream at the capital, until foreign missions numbered in the dozens.

sentences.zh: 初，太武每遣使西域，常詔河西王沮渠牧犍，令護送。

translations.literal: At first, whenever Emperor Taiwu sent envoys to the Western Regions, he regularly ordered the King of Hexi, Juqu Mujian, to escort them.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Emperor Taiwu sent missions westward, he routinely ordered Juqu Mujian, king of Hexi, to provide escort.

sentences.zh: 至姑臧，牧犍恆發使導路，出於流沙。

translations.literal: When they reached Guzang, Mujian always dispatched guides to lead the way out through the shifting sands.
translations.idiomatic: At Guzang, Mujian always sent guides to lead them out across the shifting sands.

sentences.zh: 後使者自西域還至武威，牧犍左右謂使者曰：「我君承蠕蠕吳提妄說，云：'去歲魏天子自來伐我，士馬疫死，大敗而還，我擒其長弟樂平王丕。

translations.literal: Later, when envoys returning from the Western Regions reached Wuwei, those about Mujian said to the envoys: "Our lord has received the false tale of the Rouran chief Wuti, who says: 'Last year the Wei Son of Heaven came in person to attack me; men and horses died of pestilence; he was utterly defeated and retreated; I captured his elder younger brother, the Prince of Leiping, Pi.
translations.idiomatic: When envoys returning from the west reached Wuwei, Mujian's attendants told them: "Our lord has heard the Rouran chief Wuti's boast that last year the Wei emperor marched against him in person, that men and horses died of plague, that Wei was routed, and that he captured the emperor's younger brother, Prince Leiping Pi.

sentences.zh: '我君大喜，宣言國中。

translations.literal: Our lord was greatly pleased and proclaimed it throughout the state.
translations.idiomatic: Our lord was overjoyed and proclaimed it throughout his realm.

sentences.zh: 又聞吳提遣使告西域諸國：'魏已削弱，今天下唯我為強。

translations.literal: We have also heard that Wuti sent envoys to tell the states of the Western Regions: 'Wei has been weakened; now under Heaven only I am strong.
translations.idiomatic: We also hear that Wuti has told the Western Regions: "Wei is weakened; I alone am strong under Heaven now.

sentences.zh: 若更有魏使，勿復恭奉。

translations.literal: If there should again be Wei envoys, do not again show respectful submission.
translations.idiomatic: If more Wei envoys come, do not treat them with respect again.

sentences.zh: '西域諸國，亦有貳。」

translations.literal: Some of the Western Region states have also wavered in loyalty."
translations.idiomatic: Some states in the Western Regions have already turned away."

sentences.zh: 且牧犍事主，稍以慢墮。

translations.literal: Moreover, in serving his sovereign, Mujian had gradually become slack and remiss.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Mujian had grown increasingly negligent in his duties toward the throne.

sentences.zh: 使還，具以狀聞。

translations.literal: When the envoys returned, they reported the full circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: The envoys reported everything on their return.

sentences.zh: 太武遂議討牧犍。

translations.literal: Emperor Taiwu thereupon deliberated on punishing Mujian.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taiwu then resolved to campaign against Mujian.

sentences.zh: 涼州既平，鄯善國以為辱亡齒寒，自然之道也。

translations.literal: Once Liang province was pacified, the state of Shanshan reasoned that when the lips are gone the teeth grow cold—this is the natural course of things.
translations.idiomatic: After Liang province fell, Shanshan judged that when the lips are gone the teeth grow cold—a natural law of survival.

sentences.zh: 今武威為魏所滅。

translations.literal: Now Wuwei has been destroyed by Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Wuwei has now been destroyed by Wei.

sentences.zh: 次及我矣。

translations.literal: Next it will reach us.
translations.idiomatic: We will be next.

sentences.zh: 若通其使人，知我國事，取亡必近；

translations.literal: If we allow their envoys passage and they learn our state's affairs, our destruction will surely be near;
translations.idiomatic: If we let their envoys through and they learn our affairs, our fall will come soon;

sentences.zh: 不如絕之，可以支久。

translations.literal: it would be better to cut them off; thus we may endure long.
translations.idiomatic: better to cut them off and hold out longer.

sentences.zh: 乃斷塞行路，西域貢獻，歷年不入。

translations.literal: They therefore blocked and sealed the routes; tribute from the Western Regions did not enter for many years.
translations.idiomatic: They blocked the routes, and Western Region tribute ceased for years.

sentences.zh: 後平鄯善，行人復通。

translations.literal: Later, when Shanshan was pacified, traveling envoys were again able to pass.
translations.idiomatic: After Shanshan was subdued, envoys could travel the routes again.

sentences.zh: 始，琬等使還京師，具言凡所經見及傳聞傍國，云：西域自漢武時五十餘國，後稍相並，至太延中為十六國。

translations.literal: When Wan and the others first returned to the capital, they reported in full everything they had seen and heard of neighboring states, saying: from Emperor Wu of Han's time there were more than fifty states in the Western Regions; later they gradually merged, until in the Taiyan period there were sixteen states.
translations.idiomatic: On their return to the capital, Wan and his party described everything they had seen and heard abroad: in Han Wudi's day there were more than fifty Western Region states; by the Taiyan era mergers had reduced them to sixteen.

sentences.zh: 分其地為四域：自蔥嶺以東，流沙以西為一域；

translations.literal: Their territory was divided into four regions: from the Pamirs east and west of the shifting sands was one region;
translations.idiomatic: They divided the region into four zones: east of the Pamirs and west of the shifting sands formed one zone;

sentences.zh: 蔥嶺以西，海曲以東為一域；

translations.literal: west of the Pamirs and east of the sea's bend was one region;
translations.idiomatic: west of the Pamirs and east of the sea's bend formed another;

sentences.zh: 者舌以南，月氏以北為一域；

translations.literal: south of Zheshe and north of the Yuezhi was one region;
translations.idiomatic: south of Zheshe and north of the Yuezhi formed a third;

sentences.zh: 兩海之間，水澤以南為一域。

translations.literal: between the two seas, south of the marshes and waters, was one region.
translations.idiomatic: between the two seas, south of the lakes and marshes, formed the fourth.

sentences.zh: 內諸小渠長，蓋以百數。

translations.literal: The petty chieftains within them numbered on the order of a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Petty chiefs within these zones numbered roughly a hundred.

sentences.zh: 其出西域，本有二道，後更為四：出自玉門，度流沙，西行二千里至鄯善，為一道；

translations.literal: Routes out of the Western Regions were originally two, later becoming four: from Yumen Pass, crossing the shifting sands, west two thousand li to Shanshan was one route;
translations.idiomatic: Routes westward had originally been two, later four: from Yumen Pass across the shifting sands, two thousand li west to Shanshan, was one;

sentences.zh: 自玉門度流沙，北行二千二百里至車師，為一道；

translations.literal: from Yumen crossing the shifting sands, north two thousand two hundred li to Cheshi was one route;
translations.idiomatic: from Yumen across the sands, twenty-two hundred li north to Cheshi, was another;

sentences.zh: 從莎車西行一百里至蔥嶺，蔥嶺西一千三百里至伽倍，為一道；

translations.literal: from Shache west one hundred li to the Pamirs, and west of the Pamirs one thousand three hundred li to Jiabei, was one route;
translations.idiomatic: from Shache one hundred li west to the Pamirs, then thirteen hundred li west of the Pamirs to Jiabei, was a third;

sentences.zh: 自莎車西南五百里，蔥嶺西南一千三百里至波路，為一道焉。

translations.literal: from Shache southwest five hundred li, and southwest of the Pamirs one thousand three hundred li to Bolu, was one route.
translations.idiomatic: from Shache five hundred li southwest, then thirteen hundred li southwest of the Pamirs to Bolu, was the fourth.

sentences.zh: 自琬所不傳而更有朝貢者，紀其名，不能具國俗也。

translations.literal: As for states that sent tribute though not mentioned in Wan's report, their names are recorded, but their customs cannot be given in full.
translations.idiomatic: States that paid tribute but were not covered in Wan's account are named here, though their customs cannot be described in full.

sentences.zh: 東西魏時，中國方擾，及于齊、周，不聞有事西域，故二代書並不立記錄。

translations.literal: In the Eastern and Western Wei, China was in turmoil; through Qi and Zhou nothing was heard of affairs in the Western Regions, so the histories of both dynasties established no record.
translations.idiomatic: During Eastern and Western Wei China was torn by strife; under Qi and Zhou nothing was heard from the Western Regions, so neither dynasty's history records them.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇、仁壽之間，尚未雲經略。

translations.literal: Between Sui's Kaihuang and Renshou reigns, there was as yet no talk of frontier management.
translations.idiomatic: Through Sui's Kaihuang and Renshou reigns the court had not yet turned its attention westward.

sentences.zh: 煬帝時，乃遣侍御史韋節、司隸從事杜行滿使于西籓諸國，至罽賓得瑪瑙杯，王舍城得佛經，史國得十舞女、師子皮、火鼠毛而還。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Yang, Attendant Censor Wei Jie and Retainer of the Metropolitan Commandant Du Xingman were sent to the western tributary states; reaching Kasmira they obtained an agate cup, at Wangshecheng Buddhist scriptures, and at the state of Shi ten dancing girls, lion skins, and fire-rat fur, then returned.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Yang, Wei Jie and Du Xingman were dispatched to the western realms; in Kasmira they acquired an agate cup, at Wangshe Buddhist scriptures, and at Shi ten dancing girls, lion pelts, and fire-rat fur before returning.

sentences.zh: 帝復令聞喜公裴矩于武威、張掖間往來以引致之。

translations.literal: The emperor again ordered Duke of Wenxi Pei Ju to travel back and forth between Wuwei and Zhangye to draw them in.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also sent Duke Pei Ju to shuttle between Wuwei and Zhangye to entice further embassies.

sentences.zh: 其有君長者四十四國，矩因其使者入朝，啖以厚利，令其轉相諷諭。

translations.literal: Of states with rulers there were forty-four; when their envoys came to court, Ju tempted them with rich profit and had them persuade one another in turn.
translations.idiomatic: Forty-four states had recognized rulers; Ju lavished gifts on their envoys at court and set them to persuade one another to come.

sentences.zh: 大業中，相率而來朝者四十餘國，帝因置西戎校尉以應接之。

translations.literal: In the Daye period more than forty states came to court in succession; the emperor therefore installed a Colonel of the Western Rong to receive them.
translations.idiomatic: During Daye more than forty states came in succession; the emperor appointed a Colonel of the Western Rong to receive them.

sentences.zh: 尋屬中國大亂，朝貢遂絕。

translations.literal: Soon China fell into great disorder and tribute missions ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Soon civil war engulfed China and tribute missions ceased.

sentences.zh: 然事亡失，書所存錄者二十國焉。

translations.literal: Yet affairs were lost; what the books preserve records twenty states.
translations.idiomatic: Much was lost in the turmoil; only twenty states survive in the written record.

sentences.zh: 魏時所來者，在隋亦有不至，今總而編次，以備前書之《西域傳》云。

translations.literal: States that came in Wei times and some that did not come in Sui are now gathered and arranged in order, to supplement the "Treatise on the Western Regions" of earlier books.
translations.idiomatic: States that sent envoys under Wei and some that did not under Sui are here compiled in order, supplementing earlier histories' treatises on the Western Regions.

sentences.zh: 至於道路遠近，物產風俗，詳諸前史，或有不同。

translations.literal: As for distances along the roads, products, and customs, earlier histories give detail, though there may be differences.
translations.idiomatic: Distances, products, and customs are treated at length in earlier histories, though accounts sometimes differ.

sentences.zh: 斯皆錄其當時，蓋以備其遺闕爾。

translations.literal: These are all recorded as they were at the time, intending to supply what was lost or omitted.
translations.idiomatic: What follows records conditions as they were then, to fill gaps left by earlier works.

sentences.zh: 鄯善國，都扞泥城，古樓蘭國也。

translations.literal: The state of Shanshan had its capital at Gannicheng; it was the ancient state of Loulan.
translations.idiomatic: Shanshan, capital at Gannicheng, was the ancient kingdom of Loulan.

sentences.zh: 去代七千六百里。

translations.literal: It was seven thousand six hundred li from Dai.
translations.idiomatic: It lay seven thousand six hundred li from the Wei capital.

sentences.zh: 所都城方一里。

translations.literal: Its walled capital was one li square.
translations.idiomatic: The capital walls measured one li square.

sentences.zh: 地多沙鹵，少水草，北即白龍堆路。

translations.literal: The land had much salty sand and little water and grass; to the north lay the route of the White Dragon Mounds.
translations.idiomatic: The land was mostly salty desert with little water or pasture; to the north ran the route past the White Dragon Mounds.

sentences.zh: 至太延初，始遣其弟素延耆入侍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taiyan, they first sent the king's younger brother Suyanqi to attend court.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taiyan the king sent his younger brother Suyanqi to court.

sentences.zh: 及太武平涼州，沮渠牧犍弟無諱走保敦煌。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taiwu pacified Liang province, Juqu Mujian's younger brother Wuhui fled to hold Dunhuang.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taiwu conquered Liang province, Juqu Mujian's brother Wuhui fled to Dunhuang.

sentences.zh: 無諱後謀渡流沙，遣其弟安周擊鄯善，王比龍恐懼欲降。

translations.literal: Later Wuhui planned to cross the shifting sands and sent his younger brother Anzhou to attack Shanshan; King Bilong was afraid and wished to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Wuhui later planned to cross the sands and sent his brother Anzhou against Shanshan; King Bilong, terrified, was ready to submit.

sentences.zh: 會魏使者自天竺、罽賓還，俱會鄯善，勸比龍拒之，遂與連戰。

translations.literal: It happened that Wei envoys returning from India and Kasmira all met at Shanshan and urged Bilong to resist; they then fought in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Wei envoys returning from India and Kasmira happened to meet at Shanshan and urged Bilong to resist; fighting followed.

sentences.zh: 安周不能克，退保東城。

translations.literal: Anzhou could not overcome them and withdrew to hold the eastern city.
translations.idiomatic: Anzhou failed to take the city and withdrew to the eastern quarter.

sentences.zh: 後比龍懼，率眾西奔且末，其世子乃應安周。

translations.literal: Later Bilong grew afraid, led his people west in flight to Qiemo, and his heir then yielded to Anzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Bilong later fled west to Qiemo with his followers; his heir then submitted to Anzhou.

sentences.zh: 鄯善人頗剽劫之，令不得通，太武詔散騎常侍、成周公萬度歸乘傳發涼州兵討之。

translations.literal: The people of Shanshan frequently plundered and robbed, so that passage was impossible; Emperor Taiwu ordered the Regular Attendant of the Scattered Riders, Duke of Cheng Wu Wan Duigui, to travel post-haste and mobilize Liang province troops to punish them.
translations.idiomatic: Shanshan bandits blocked the routes; Emperor Taiwu ordered Attendant Wan Duigui, Duke of Cheng, to rush Liang troops against them.

sentences.zh: 度歸到敦煌，留輜重，以輕騎五千度流沙，至其境。

translations.literal: Duigui reached Dunhuang, left the baggage train, and with five thousand light cavalry crossed the shifting sands into their territory.
translations.idiomatic: Duigui reached Dunhuang, left the baggage train behind, and crossed the sands with five thousand light cavalry.

sentences.zh: 時鄯善人眾布野，度歸敕吏卒不得有所侵掠。

translations.literal: At the time the people of Shanshan were scattered in the fields; Duigui ordered officers and soldiers not to plunder in any way.
translations.idiomatic: The Shanshan people were scattered across the countryside; Duigui forbade his men any looting.

sentences.zh: 邊守感之，皆望旗稽服。

translations.literal: The frontier guards were moved by this and all, seeing the banners, bowed in submission.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier peoples were moved and submitted at sight of his banners.

sentences.zh: 其王真達面縛出降，度歸釋其縛，留軍屯守，與真達詣京都。

translations.literal: Their king Zhenda came out bound in person to surrender; Duigui released his bonds, left troops to garrison, and went with Zhenda to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: King Zhenda came out with bound hands; Duigui freed him, left a garrison, and escorted him to the capital.

sentences.zh: 太武大悅，厚待之。

translations.literal: Emperor Taiwu was greatly pleased and treated him generously.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taiwu was delighted and received him with great honor.

sentences.zh: 是歲，拜交趾公韓拔為假節、征西將軍、領護西戎校尉、鄯善王以鎮之，賦役其人，比之郡縣。

translations.literal: That year Han Ba, Duke of Jiaozhi, was appointed with provisional credentials as General Who Pacifies the West, Colonel Protecting the Western Rong, and King of Shanshan to garrison it; the people were taxed and levied for labor as in commanderies and counties.
translations.idiomatic: That year Han Ba was made acting General Who Pacifies the West, Colonel Protecting the Western Rong, and King of Shanshan to hold the region; its people were taxed and levied like subjects of interior commanderies.

sentences.zh: 且末國，都且末城，在鄯善四，去代八千三百二十里。

translations.literal: The state of Qiemo had its capital at Qiemo city; it was four [units of measure] from Shanshan and eight thousand three hundred twenty li from Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Qiemo, capital at Qiemo city, lay four days' travel from Shanshan and eight thousand three hundred twenty li from the Wei capital.

sentences.zh: 真君三年，鄯善王比龍避沮渠安周之難，率國人之半奔且末。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenjun, King Bilong of Shanshan, fleeing the trouble from Juqu Anzhou, led half his people in flight to Qiemo.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenjun 3, King Bilong of Shanshan fled Juqu Anzhou's attack with half his people to Qiemo.

sentences.zh: 後役屬鄯善。

translations.literal: Later it was made subject and attached to Shanshan.
translations.idiomatic: It later became a dependency of Shanshan.

sentences.zh: 且末西北有流沙數百里，夏日有熱風，為行旅之患。

translations.literal: Northwest of Qiemo were shifting sands extending several hundred li; in summer there were hot winds, a peril to travelers.
translations.idiomatic: Several hundred li northwest of Qiemo lay shifting sands where summer hot winds were a deadly hazard to travelers.

sentences.zh: 風之所至，唯老駝預知之，即嗔而聚立，埋其口鼻于沙中。

translations.literal: Where the wind was about to strike, only old camels foreknew it; they would snort and gather standing, burying their muzzles in the sand.
translations.idiomatic: Only veteran camels sensed the wind's approach; they would snort, cluster together, and bury their muzzles in the sand.

sentences.zh: 人每以為候，亦即將氈擁蔽鼻口。

translations.literal: People always took this as a sign and likewise wrapped felt about their noses and mouths.
translations.idiomatic: Travelers took this as their signal and wrapped felt over nose and mouth.

sentences.zh: 其風迅駃，斯須過盡，若不防者，必至危斃。

translations.literal: The wind was swift and sudden; in an instant it passed—but those who did not guard against it would surely come to peril and death.
translations.idiomatic: The wind struck swiftly and passed in moments; anyone unprepared faced certain death.

sentences.zh: 大統八年，其兄鄯善米率眾內附。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Datong, his elder brother, the Shanshan chief Mi, led his people to submit inward.
translations.idiomatic: In Datong 8, his elder brother Mi of Shanshan led his people to submit to the court.

sentences.zh: 于闐國，在且末西北，蔥嶺之北二百餘里。

translations.literal: The state of Khotan was northwest of Qiemo, more than two hundred li north of the Pamirs.
translations.idiomatic: Khotan lay northwest of Qiemo, more than two hundred li north of the Pamirs.

sentences.zh: 東去鄯善千五百里，南去女國三千里，去硃俱波千里，北去龜茲千四百里，去代九千八百里。

translations.literal: East to Shanshan was one thousand five hundred li; south to the Women's Kingdom three thousand li; to Zhujubo one thousand li; north to Kucha one thousand four hundred li; to Dai nine thousand eight hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: It was fifteen hundred li east of Shanshan, three thousand li south of the Women's Kingdom, a thousand li from Zhujubo, fourteen hundred li north of Kucha, and nine thousand eight hundred li from the Wei capital.

sentences.zh: 其地方亙千里，連山相次，所都城方八九里。

translations.literal: Its territory extended a thousand li square; ranges of mountains followed one upon another; its walled capital was eight or nine li square.
translations.idiomatic: Its territory stretched a thousand li on a side, with ranges of mountains in succession; the capital walls measured eight or nine li square.

sentences.zh: 部內有大城五，小城數十。

translations.literal: Within the territory there were five large cities and several tens of small cities.
translations.idiomatic: Within its domain were five large cities and several dozen smaller ones.

sentences.zh: 于闐城東三十里有首拔河，中出玉石。

translations.literal: Thirty li east of Khotan city was the Shouba River, from which jade and stone issued.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty li east of Khotan stood the Shouba River, which yielded jade and stone.

sentences.zh: 土宜五穀並桑、麻。

translations.literal: The soil was suited to the five grains, together with mulberry and hemp.
translations.idiomatic: The soil supported the five grains as well as mulberry and hemp.

sentences.zh: 山多美玉。

translations.literal: The mountains had much fine jade.
translations.idiomatic: The mountains abounded in fine jade.

sentences.zh: 有好馬、駝、騾。

translations.literal: There were good horses, camels, and mules.
translations.idiomatic: It had fine horses, camels, and mules.

sentences.zh: 其刑法，殺人者死，餘罪各隨輕重懲罰之。

translations.literal: Its penal code: killers were put to death; remaining crimes were each punished according to severity.
translations.idiomatic: Under its penal code, murder was punishable by death; lesser offenses were penalized according to their severity.

sentences.zh: 自外風俗物產，與龜茲略同。

translations.literal: Apart from these, customs and products were roughly the same as Kucha.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise, its customs and products closely resembled those of Kucha.

sentences.zh: 俗重佛法，寺塔、僧尼甚眾。

translations.literal: The people valued Buddhist law; temples, pagodas, monks, and nuns were very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: The people held Buddhism in high regard; temples, pagodas, monks, and nuns were exceedingly numerous.

sentences.zh: 王尤信尚，每設齋日，必親自灑掃饋食焉。

translations.literal: The king especially believed in and honored it; on each day of fasting offerings, he personally swept, cleaned, and presented food.
translations.idiomatic: The king was especially devout; on each fasting day he personally swept the grounds and provided offerings of food.

sentences.zh: 城南五十里有贊摩寺，即昔羅漢比丘盧旃為其王造覆盆浮圖之所。

translations.literal: Fifty li south of the city was Zanmo Temple, the place where in former times the arhat bhikṣu Lu Zhan built an inverted-bowl stūpa for its king.
translations.idiomatic: Fifty li south of the city stood Zanmo Temple, where the arhat Lu Zhan had once built an inverted-bowl pagoda for the king.

sentences.zh: 石上有辟支佛跣處，雙跡猶存。

translations.literal: On the stone was the barefoot place of a pratyekabuddha; the pair of footprints still remained.
translations.idiomatic: On the stone was a spot where a pratyekabuddha had walked barefoot; the twin footprints could still be seen.

sentences.zh: 于闐西五百里有比摩寺，雲是老子化胡成佛之所。

translations.literal: Five hundred li west of Khotan was Bimo Temple; it was said to be the place where Laozi transformed a barbarian into a Buddha.
translations.idiomatic: Five hundred li west of Khotan lay Bimo Temple, said to mark the spot where Laozi transformed himself into the Buddha among the barbarians.

sentences.zh: 俗無禮義，多盜賊淫縱。

translations.literal: The customs lacked ritual and propriety; there were many thieves, robbers, and lewd excesses.
translations.idiomatic: The people observed little ritual or propriety; thievery and licentious behavior were common.

sentences.zh: 自高昌以西諸國人等，深目高鼻，唯此一國，貌不甚胡，頗類華夏。

translations.literal: From Gaochang westward, the people of the various states had deep eyes and high noses; only this one state was not very barbarian in appearance and rather resembled Huaxia.
translations.idiomatic: West of Gaochang the peoples of the various states typically had deep-set eyes and high noses; Khotan alone was not notably foreign in appearance and resembled China in many respects.

sentences.zh: 城東二十里有大水北流，號樹枝水，即黃河也，一名計式水。

translations.literal: Twenty li east of the city was a great river flowing north, called Branch Water; it was the Yellow River, also named Jishi Water.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty li east of the city a great river flowed northward, known as Branch Water—the Yellow River, also called Jishi Water.

sentences.zh: 城西十五里亦有大水名達利水，與樹枝水會，俱北流。

translations.literal: Fifteen li west of the city was also a great river named Dali Water; it joined Branch Water, and both flowed north.
translations.idiomatic: Fifteen li west of the city another great river, the Dali, joined the Branch Water, and both flowed north together.

sentences.zh: 真君中，太武詔高涼王那擊吐谷渾慕利延，慕利延懼，驅其部落渡流沙。

translations.literal: In the Zhenjun era, Emperor Taiwu ordered the Prince of Gaoliang Na to attack Tuyuhun Muli; Muli was afraid and drove his clans across the shifting sands.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenjun reign, Emperor Taiwu commanded Prince Na of Gaoliang to strike Tuyuhun Muli; fearing defeat, Muli drove his tribes across the desert sands.

sentences.zh: 那進軍急追之，慕利延遂西入于闐，殺其王，死者甚眾。

translations.literal: Na advanced his army in hot pursuit; Muli then entered Khotan from the west, killed its king, and many died.
translations.idiomatic: Na pressed the pursuit hard; Muli fled west into Khotan, slew its king, and left great numbers dead.

sentences.zh: 獻文末，蠕蠕寇于闐。

translations.literal: At the end of the Xianwen reign, Rouran raided Khotan.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of Emperor Xianwen's reign, the Rouran attacked Khotan.

sentences.zh: 于闐患之，遣使素目伽上表曰：「西方諸國，今皆已屬蠕蠕。

translations.literal: Khotan was troubled by this and sent the envoy Sumoga to submit a memorial, saying: "The western states are now all subject to Rouran.
translations.idiomatic: Distressed, Khotan sent the envoy Sumoga with a memorial stating, "The western states have all now fallen under Rouran control.

sentences.zh: 奴世奉大國，至今無異。

translations.literal: Your servant has for generations served the great state and to this day remains unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: We have served the great empire for generations and remain loyal to this day.

sentences.zh: 今蠕蠕軍馬到城下，奴聚兵自固，故遣使奉獻，遙望救援。」

translations.literal: Now Rouran's army and horses have reached below the walls; your servant has gathered troops to hold firm, and therefore sends this envoy with tribute, looking from afar for rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Now Rouran forces have reached our walls; we have mustered troops to defend ourselves and send this envoy with tribute, hoping from afar for relief.

sentences.zh: 帝詔公卿議之。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the chief and lesser ministers to deliberate on it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered his ministers to deliberate.

sentences.zh: 公卿奏曰：「于闐去京師幾萬里，蠕蠕之性，唯習野掠，不能攻城。

translations.literal: The ministers memorialized, saying: "Khotan is tens of thousands of li from the capital; Rouran's nature is only practiced in wild raiding and cannot besiege cities.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers replied, "Khotan lies many thousands of li from the capital; the Rouran are accustomed only to wild raiding and cannot take walled cities.

sentences.zh: 若為害，當時已旋矣，雖欲遣師，勢無所及。」

translations.literal: If they were doing harm, they would already have withdrawn; even if troops were sent, circumstances would not allow reaching them.
translations.idiomatic: If they meant real harm, they would already have withdrawn; even if we sent troops, we could not arrive in time.

sentences.zh: 帝以公卿議示其使者，亦以為然。

translations.literal: The emperor showed the ministers' deliberation to their envoy, who also considered it so.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor showed the deliberation to the envoy, who agreed.

sentences.zh: 於是詔之曰：「朕承天理物，欲令萬方各安其所，應敕諸軍，以拯汝難。

translations.literal: Thereupon he issued an edict to them, saying: "We receive Heaven's principle and govern things, wishing to let the ten thousand regions each rest in their place; we should order the armies to rescue your difficulty.
translations.idiomatic: He then issued an edict: "We bear Heaven's mandate and govern all things, wishing every realm peace; we ought to command our armies to deliver you from peril.

sentences.zh: 但去汝遐阻，政復遣援，不救當時之急，是以停師不行，汝宜知之。

translations.literal: But distance from you is far and obstructed; even if aid were sent again, it would not save the urgency of the moment; therefore the army was halted and did not go—you should know this.
translations.idiomatic: But you are too distant and the routes too difficult; even if we sent aid, it could not meet your immediate need. We therefore halt our armies and do not march. You should understand this.

sentences.zh: 朕今練甲養卒，一二歲間，當躬率猛將，為汝除患。

translations.literal: We now drill armor and nurture soldiers; within one or two years we shall personally lead fierce generals to remove your affliction for you.
translations.idiomatic: We are now training troops; within a year or two we shall personally lead brave generals to eliminate your enemies.

sentences.zh: 汝其謹敬候，以待大舉。」

translations.literal: You should respectfully and reverently wait, awaiting the great campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Remain vigilant and await our grand campaign.

sentences.zh: 先是，朝廷遣使者韓羊皮使波斯，波斯王遣使獻馴象及珍物。

translations.literal: Earlier, the court had sent the envoy Han Yangpi as envoy to Persia; the Persian king sent envoys presenting tame elephants and precious things.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the court had dispatched Han Yangpi as envoy to Persia; the Persian king sent envoys with tame elephants and rare goods.

sentences.zh: 經于闐，于闐中于王秋仁輒留之，假言慮有寇不達。

translations.literal: Passing through Khotan, Khotan's vice-king Qiuren detained them, falsely saying he feared raiders and they could not pass through.
translations.idiomatic: Passing through Khotan, Vice-King Qiuren detained them, claiming he feared bandits and that they could not pass safely.

sentences.zh: 羊皮言狀，帝怒，又遣羊皮奉詔責讓之。

translations.literal: Yangpi reported the circumstances; the emperor was angry and again sent Yangpi bearing an edict to reproach them.
translations.idiomatic: Yangpi reported what had happened; the emperor was furious and again sent him with an edict of rebuke.

sentences.zh: 自後每使朝貢。

translations.literal: From then on, on each mission they presented tribute at court.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter they sent tribute with every envoy mission.

sentences.zh: 周建德三年，其王遣使獻名馬。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jiande of Zhou, its king sent envoys presenting famous horses.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiande 3 of Northern Zhou, its king sent envoys with prized horses.

sentences.zh: 隋大業中，頻使朝貢。

translations.literal: In the Daye era of Sui, envoys frequently came to court with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: During the Sui Daye reign, envoys came frequently with tribute.

sentences.zh: 其王姓王，字早示門。

translations.literal: Its king's surname was Wang, and his style-name was Zaoshimen.
translations.idiomatic: The king's surname was Wang; his courtesy name was Zaoshimen.

sentences.zh: 練錦帽，金鼠冠，妻戴金花。

translations.literal: He wore a hat of refined brocade and a golden-rat crown; his wife wore golden flowers.
translations.idiomatic: He wore a brocade cap and a golden mouse crown; his queen wore golden flowers in her hair.

sentences.zh: 其王髮不令人見，俗言若見王髮，其年必儉云。

translations.literal: The king's hair was not shown to people; by custom it was said that if one saw the king's hair, that year would surely be scarce.
translations.idiomatic: No one was permitted to see the king's hair; the people believed that whoever saw it would bring famine upon the land that year.

sentences.zh: 蒲山國，故皮山國也。

translations.literal: The state of Pishan was the former state of Pishan.
translations.idiomatic: Pishan was formerly known as the state of Pishan (Mount Pi).

sentences.zh: 居皮城，在于闐南，去代一萬二千里。

translations.literal: It dwelt at Pishan city, south of Khotan, twelve thousand li from Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Its seat was Pishan city, south of Khotan, twelve thousand li from the Wei capital.

sentences.zh: 其國西南三里有凍淩山。

translations.literal: Three li southwest of its state was Mount Dongling.
translations.idiomatic: Three li southwest of the state stood Mount Dongling.

sentences.zh: 後役屬于闐。

translations.literal: Later it was subjected and became tributary to Khotan.
translations.idiomatic: Later it became a dependency of Khotan.

sentences.zh: 悉居半國，故西夜國也，一名子合。

translations.literal: The state of Xijuban was formerly the state of Xiye, also called Zihe.
translations.idiomatic: Xijuban was formerly Xiye, also known as Zihe.

sentences.zh: 其王號子。

translations.literal: Its king was titled Zi.
translations.idiomatic: Its ruler bore the title Zi.

sentences.zh: 治呼犍。

translations.literal: It was governed from Hujian.
translations.idiomatic: Its capital was Hujian.

sentences.zh: 在于闐西，去代萬二千九百七十里。

translations.literal: It was west of Khotan, twelve thousand nine hundred seventy li from Dai.
translations.idiomatic: It lay west of Khotan, twelve thousand nine hundred seventy li from the Wei capital.

sentences.zh: 太延初，遣使來獻，自後貢使不絕。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taiyan, it sent envoys to come with tribute; from then on tribute missions did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Taiyan reign it sent tribute envoys; thereafter tribute missions continued without interruption.

sentences.zh: 權于摩國，故烏秅國也。

translations.literal: The state of Quyusa was formerly the state of Wuno.
translations.idiomatic: Quyusa was formerly the state of Wuno.

sentences.zh: 其王居烏秅城。

translations.literal: Its king dwelt at Wuno city.
translations.idiomatic: Its king resided at Wuno city.

sentences.zh: 在悉居半西南，去代一萬二千九百七十里。

translations.literal: It was southwest of Xijuban, twelve thousand nine hundred seventy li from Dai.
translations.idiomatic: It lay southwest of Xijuban, twelve thousand nine hundred seventy li from the Wei capital.

sentences.zh: 渠莎國，居故莎車城，在子合西北，去代一萬二千九百八十里。

translations.literal: The state of Qusha dwelt at the former Shache city, northwest of Zihe, twelve thousand nine hundred eighty li from Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Qusha occupied old Shache city, northwest of Zihe, twelve thousand nine hundred eighty li from the Wei capital.

sentences.zh: 車師國，一名前部，其王居交河城。

translations.literal: The state of Cheshi, also called the Front Kingdom; its king dwelt at Jiaohe city.
translations.idiomatic: Cheshi, also known as the Front Kingdom, had its seat at Jiaohe.

sentences.zh: 去代萬五十里。

translations.literal: It was ten thousand fifty li from Dai.
translations.idiomatic: It was ten thousand and fifty li from the Wei capital.

sentences.zh: 其地北接蠕蠕，本通使交易。

translations.literal: Its territory bordered Rouran to the north; originally it exchanged envoys and conducted trade.
translations.idiomatic: Its territory bordered the Rouran on the north; it had long exchanged envoys and conducted trade.

sentences.zh: 太武初，始遣使朝獻，詔行人王恩生、許綱等出使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taiwu, it first sent envoys to court with tribute; the emperor ordered the messenger Wang Ensheng, Xu Gang, and others to go as envoys.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taiwu's reign it first sent tribute envoys; the emperor dispatched Wang Ensheng, Xu Gang, and others as envoys.

sentences.zh: 恩生等始度流沙，為蠕蠕所執。

translations.literal: Ensheng and the others had just crossed the shifting sands when they were seized by Rouran.
translations.idiomatic: Ensheng and his party had scarcely crossed the desert when the Rouran captured them.

sentences.zh: 恩生見蠕蠕吳提，持魏節不為之屈。

translations.literal: Ensheng saw Rouran's Wuti; holding the Wei credential of office, he did not yield to him.
translations.idiomatic: Brought before the Rouran khan Wuti, Ensheng held the Wei envoy's staff and refused to submit.

sentences.zh: 後太武切讓吳提，吳提懼，乃遣恩生等歸。

translations.literal: Later Emperor Taiwu sternly reproached Wuti; Wuti was afraid and then sent Ensheng and the others back.
translations.idiomatic: Later Emperor Taiwu sternly rebuked Wuti; fearing consequences, Wuti released Ensheng and his companions.

sentences.zh: 許綱到敦煌病死，朝廷壯其節，賜諡曰貞。

translations.literal: Xu Gang reached Dunhuang and died of illness; the court admired his integrity and posthumously conferred the title Zhen ("Upright").
translations.idiomatic: Xu Gang died of illness at Dunhuang; the court honored his steadfastness and granted him the posthumous name Zhen.

sentences.zh: 初，沮渠無諱兄弟之渡流沙也，鳩集遺人，破車師國。

translations.literal: At first, when Juqu Wuhui and his brothers crossed the shifting sands, they gathered scattered people and broke the state of Cheshi.
translations.idiomatic: When Juqu Wuhui and his brothers first crossed the desert, they gathered survivors and overthrew Cheshi.

sentences.zh: 真君十一年，車師王車夷落遣使琢進薛直上書曰：「臣亡父僻處塞外，仰慕天子威德，遣使奉獻，不空於歲。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Zhenjun, the Cheshi king Che Yiluo sent the envoy Zhuo Jinxue to submit a memorial, saying: "Your servant's deceased father dwelt remote in the outer frontier, admiring the Son of Heaven's august virtue; he sent envoys with tribute, never missing a year.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenjun 11, King Che Yiluo of Cheshi sent Zhuo Jinxue with a memorial: "My late father, dwelling far beyond the frontier, admired the Son of Heaven's majesty and sent tribute envoys every year without fail.

sentences.zh: 天子降念，賜遣甚厚。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven lowered his regard and bestowed gifts with great generosity.
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven graciously received him and sent rich gifts in return.

sentences.zh: 及臣繼立，亦不闕常貢，天子垂矜，亦不異前世。

translations.literal: When your servant succeeded to the throne, regular tribute was not lacking; the Son of Heaven showed compassion, no different from previous generations.
translations.idiomatic: When I succeeded him, I continued the regular tribute; the Son of Heaven showed the same favor as before.

sentences.zh: 敢緣至恩，輒陳私懇。

translations.literal: Daring to follow upon supreme grace, I rashly state a private plea.
translations.idiomatic: Presuming on this great kindness, I venture to state a personal plea.

sentences.zh: 臣國自無諱所攻擊，經今八歲，人民饑荒，無以存活。

translations.literal: Your servant's state, since Wuhui's attack, has now gone eight years; the people are famine-stricken and have no means to survive.
translations.idiomatic: Since Wuhui's attack eight years ago, my people have suffered famine and cannot survive.

sentences.zh: 賊今攻臣甚急，臣不能自全，遂舍國東奔，三分免一。

translations.literal: The brigands now attack your servant very urgently; your servant could not preserve himself and therefore abandoned the state and fled east; one in three escaped.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy presses hard; unable to defend my realm, I fled eastward—only one in three of my people escaped.

sentences.zh: 即日已到焉耆東界，思歸天闕，幸垂賑救。」

translations.literal: On this very day we have reached the eastern border of Yanqi; we think of returning to the celestial court—may you grant relief and rescue.
translations.idiomatic: We have now reached the eastern border of Yanqi; longing to return to the imperial court, we beg for your aid.

sentences.zh: 於是下詔撫慰之，開焉耆倉給之。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict was issued to console them; Yanqi's granaries were opened to supply them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then issued an edict of consolation and opened the Yanqi granaries to provide for them.

sentences.zh: 正平初，遣子入侍，自後每使朝貢不絕。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhengping, he sent his son to serve at court; from then on tribute missions at each court visit did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhengping reign he sent his son as hostage; thereafter tribute missions continued without interruption.

sentences.zh: 高昌者，車師前王之故地，漢之前部地也。

translations.literal: Gaochang was the former territory of the front king of Cheshi, the territory of the Former Kingdom under Han.
translations.idiomatic: Gaochang occupied the former territory of the Cheshi Front Kingdom, the Han-era Former Kingdom.

sentences.zh: 東西二百里，南北五百里，四面多大山。

translations.literal: East-west two hundred li, north-south five hundred li; on all four sides were many great mountains.
translations.idiomatic: It measured two hundred li east to west and five hundred li north to south, with great mountains on every side.

sentences.zh: 或云：昔漢武遣兵西討，師旅頓弊，其中尤困者因住焉。

translations.literal: Some say: In former times Emperor Wu of Han sent troops west to campaign; the army was exhausted and worn, and among them the most distressed consequently stayed there.
translations.idiomatic: Some say that when Emperor Wu of Han marched west, his army grew exhausted, and the most weary soldiers simply remained there.

sentences.zh: 地勢高敞，人庶昌盛，因名高昌。

translations.literal: The terrain was high and open, the people prosperous and flourishing; therefore it was named Gaochang ("Lofty and Flourishing").
translations.idiomatic: The land was elevated and open, its population thriving—hence the name Gaochang, "Lofty and Flourishing."

sentences.zh: 亦云：其地有漢時高昌壘，故以為國號。

translations.literal: It is also said: The place had a Han-era Gaochang fort, and therefore this was taken as the state's name.
translations.idiomatic: Others say it took its name from a Han-era Gaochang garrison fortress on the site.

sentences.zh: 東去長安四千九百里。

translations.literal: East to Chang'an was four thousand nine hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: It lay four thousand nine hundred li east of Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 漢西域長史及戊巳校尉並居於此。

translations.literal: The Han Western Regions Chief Commandant and the Wuji Colonel both dwelt here.
translations.idiomatic: The Han Western Regions Chief Commandant and the Wuji Colonel had both been stationed there.

sentences.zh: 晉以其地為高昌郡。

translations.literal: Jin made its territory Gaochang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin dynasty organized the region as Gaochang commandery.

sentences.zh: 張軌、呂光、沮渠蒙遜據河西，皆置太守以統之。

translations.literal: Zhang Gui, Lü Guang, and Juqu Mengxun held Hexi; each appointed grand administrators to govern it.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Gui, Lü Guang, and Juqu Mengxun held the Hexi region, each appointed governors to administer Gaochang.

sentences.zh: 敦煌十三日行。

translations.literal: Thirteen days' travel from Dunhuang.
translations.idiomatic: It was thirteen days' journey from Dunhuang.

sentences.zh: 國有八城，皆有華人。

translations.literal: The state had eight cities; all had Chinese people.
translations.idiomatic: The kingdom had eight cities, all with Chinese inhabitants.

sentences.zh: 地多石磧，氣候溫暖，厥土良沃，穀麥一歲再熟，宜蠶，多五果，又饒漆。

translations.literal: The land had much stony desert; the climate was warm; its soil was fine and fertile; grain and wheat ripened twice in a year; silkworms were suited; there were many of the five fruits; and lacquer was abundant.
translations.idiomatic: Much of the land was stony desert, but the climate was mild and the soil fertile; grain ripened twice yearly, silkworms thrived, fruit trees flourished, and lacquer was plentiful.

sentences.zh: 有草名羊刺，其上生蜜。

translations.literal: There was a grass named sheep-thorn; on it honey grew.
translations.idiomatic: A plant called sheep-thorn bore honey on its stalks.

sentences.zh: 而味甚佳。

translations.literal: And its flavor was very fine.
translations.idiomatic: Its flavor was exceptionally fine.

sentences.zh: 引水溉田。

translations.literal: Water was drawn to irrigate fields.
translations.idiomatic: Irrigation channels watered the fields.

sentences.zh: 出赤鹽，其味甚美，復有白鹽，其形如玉，高昌人取以為枕，貢之中國。

translations.literal: It produced red salt, whose flavor was very fine; there was also white salt, whose form was like jade; Gaochang people took it to make pillows and presented it as tribute to China.
translations.idiomatic: It produced red salt of excellent flavor and white salt shaped like jade; the people of Gaochang fashioned the latter into pillows and sent them as tribute to China.

sentences.zh: 多蒲桃酒。

translations.literal: There was much grape wine.
translations.idiomatic: Grape wine was abundant.

sentences.zh: 俗事天神，兼信佛法。

translations.literal: The customs served the heavenly god and also believed in Buddhist law.
translations.idiomatic: The people worshipped heaven and also practiced Buddhism.

sentences.zh: 國中羊、馬，牧在隱僻處以避寇，非貴人不知其處。

translations.literal: Within the state, sheep and horses were pastured in hidden secluded places to avoid raiders; except for nobles, none knew the locations.
translations.idiomatic: Sheep and horses were grazed in hidden pastures to escape raiders; only nobles knew where they were kept.

sentences.zh: 北有赤石山，山北七十里有貪汗山，夏有積雪。

translations.literal: To the north was Red Stone Mountain; seventy li north of the mountain was Greedy-Sweat Mountain, which had accumulated snow in summer.
translations.idiomatic: To the north stood Red Stone Mountain; seventy li beyond it rose Mount Gehan, which retained snow even in summer.

sentences.zh: 此山北，鐵勒界也。

translations.literal: North of this mountain was the territory of the Tiele.
translations.idiomatic: North of that mountain lay Tiele territory.

sentences.zh: 太武時有闞爽者，自為高昌太守。

translations.literal: In the Taiwu era there was Kan Shuang, who installed himself as grand administrator of Gaochang.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Taiwu's reign, Kan Shuang proclaimed himself governor of Gaochang.

sentences.zh: 太延中，遣散騎侍郎王恩生等使高昌，為蠕蠕所執。

translations.literal: In Taiyan, Attendant Gentleman of the Dispersed Cavalry Wang Ensheng and others were sent as envoys to Gaochang and were seized by Rouran.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taiyan reign, Wang Ensheng and others were dispatched as envoys to Gaochang but were captured by the Rouran.

sentences.zh: 真君中，爽為沮渠無諱所襲，奪據之。

translations.literal: In Zhenjun, Shuang was attacked by Juqu Wuhui, who seized and occupied it.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenjun reign, Juqu Wuhui attacked Shuang and seized Gaochang.

sentences.zh: 無諱死，弟安周代立。

translations.literal: Wuhui died; his younger brother Anzhou succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: After Wuhui's death, his brother Anzhou succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 和平元年，為蠕蠕所並。

translations.literal: In the first year of Heping, it was annexed by Rouran.
translations.idiomatic: In Heping 1, Rouran annexed the state.

sentences.zh: 蠕蠕以闞伯周為高昌王，其稱王自此始也。

translations.literal: Rouran made Kan Bozhou king of Gaochang; the title of king began from this time.
translations.idiomatic: The Rouran installed Kan Bozhou as king of Gaochang—the first time the region had a king of its own.

sentences.zh: 太和初，伯周死，子義成立。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taihe, Bozhou died; his son Yicheng succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Taihe reign, Bozhou died and his son Yicheng succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，為從兄首歸所殺，自立為高昌王。

translations.literal: After a little more than a year, he was killed by his cousin Shougui, who installed himself as king of Gaochang.
translations.idiomatic: A little over a year later, his cousin Shougui killed him and proclaimed himself king of Gaochang.

sentences.zh: 五年，高車王阿至羅殺首歸兄弟，以敦煌人張孟明為王。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, the Gaoche king Azheluo killed Shougui and his brothers and made Zhang Mengming of Dunhuang king.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, the Gaoche king Azheluo killed Shougui and his brothers and installed Zhang Mengming of Dunhuang as king.

sentences.zh: 後為國人所殺，立馬儒為王，以鞏顧禮、麴嘉為左右長史。

translations.literal: Later he was killed by men of the state; they installed Ma Ru as king and appointed Gong Guli and Qu Jia as left and right chief secretaries.
translations.idiomatic: Later the people of the state killed him and made Ma Ru king, appointing Gong Guli and Qu Jia as his left and right chief secretaries.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，遣司馬王體玄奉表朝貢，請師逆接，求舉國內徙。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year, they sent the Marshal Wang TiXuan bearing a memorial with tribute to court, requesting troops to meet and escort them, and asking to move the entire state inward.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year, Ma Ru sent Marshal Wang Tixuan with a memorial and tribute to court, requesting an army to meet and escort him and asking to relocate the entire kingdom into Wei territory.

sentences.zh: 孝文納之，遣明威將軍韓安保率騎千餘赴之，割伊吾五百里，以儒居之。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen accepted; he sent the General of Manifest Might Han Anbao leading more than a thousand horsemen to go to them, carved out five hundred li of Yiwu, and had Ru dwell there.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen agreed and sent General of Manifest Might Han Anbao with more than a thousand cavalry to meet him, allotting five hundred li of Yiwu for Ma Ru to settle.

sentences.zh: 至羊榛水，儒遣嘉、禮率步騎一千五百迎安保。

translations.literal: Reaching Yangzhen Water, Ru sent Jia and Guli leading one thousand five hundred infantry and cavalry to welcome Anbao.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Yangzhen Water, Ma Ru sent Qu Jia and Guli with fifteen hundred foot and horse to welcome Han Anbao.

sentences.zh: 去高昌四百里而安保不至。

translations.literal: Four hundred li from Gaochang, and Anbao did not arrive.
translations.idiomatic: They were four hundred li from Gaochang, but Han Anbao never came.

sentences.zh: 禮等還高昌，安保亦還伊吾。

translations.literal: Guli and the others returned to Gaochang; Anbao also returned to Yiwu.
translations.idiomatic: Guli and his party returned to Gaochang, and Han Anbao went back to Yiwu.

sentences.zh: 安保遣使韓興安等十二人使高昌，儒復遣顧禮將其世子義舒迎安保。

translations.literal: Anbao sent the envoys Han Xing'an and eleven others as envoys to Gaochang; Ru again sent Guli leading his heir Yishu to welcome Anbao.
translations.idiomatic: Han Anbao sent twelve envoys led by Han Xing'an to Gaochang, and Ma Ru again dispatched Guli with his heir Yishu to welcome him.

sentences.zh: 至白棘城，去高昌百六十里。

translations.literal: Reaching Bojie City, one hundred sixty li from Gaochang.
translations.idiomatic: They reached Bojie City, one hundred sixty li from Gaochang.

sentences.zh: 而高昌舊人情戀本土，不願東遷，相與殺儒而立麴嘉為王。

translations.literal: But the old residents of Gaochang, whose feelings clung to their native land, did not wish to move east; together they killed Ru and installed Qu Jia as king.
translations.idiomatic: But Gaochang's old families clung to their homeland and refused to move east; they joined together, killed Ma Ru, and made Qu Jia king.

sentences.zh: 嘉字靈鳳，金城榆中人。

translations.literal: Jia, courtesy name Lingfeng, was a man of Yuzhong in Jincheng.
translations.idiomatic: Qu Jia, courtesy name Lingfeng, was a native of Yuzhong in Jincheng.

sentences.zh: 既立，又臣於蠕蠕那蓋。

translations.literal: Once installed, he again submitted to Rouran's Nagai.
translations.idiomatic: Once enthroned, he again submitted to the Rouran khan Nagai.

sentences.zh: 顧禮與義舒隨安保至洛陽。

translations.literal: Guli and Yishu followed Anbao to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Guli and Yishu accompanied Han Anbao to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 及蠕蠕主伏圖為高車所殺，嘉又臣高車。

translations.literal: When the Rouran ruler Futu was killed by the Gaoche, Jia again submitted to the Gaoche.
translations.idiomatic: After the Rouran ruler Futu was killed by the Gaoche, Qu Jia submitted to the Gaoche in turn.

sentences.zh: 初，前部胡人悉為高車所徙，入於焉耆，又為嚈噠所破滅，國人分散，眾不自立，請主於嘉。

translations.literal: At first, all the Hu people of the Former Kingdom were moved by the Gaoche into Yanqi; they were again destroyed by the Hephthalites, the state's people scattered, the multitude unable to establish themselves on their own, and they requested Jia as lord.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the Gaoche had moved all the Hu of the Former Kingdom into Yanqi; the Hephthalites then destroyed them, scattering the people until they could no longer sustain themselves and asked Qu Jia to rule them.

sentences.zh: 嘉遣第二子為焉耆王以主之。

translations.literal: Jia sent his second son to be king of Yanqi to govern them.
translations.idiomatic: Qu Jia sent his second son to reign as king of Yanqi and govern them.

sentences.zh: 永平元年，嘉遣兄子私署左衛將軍、田地太守孝亮朝京師，仍求內徙，乞軍迎援。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongping, Jia sent his elder brother's son, who had self-appointed the Left Guard General and Governor of Tiandi Xiaoliang, to court at the capital, still requesting inward migration and begging for troops to welcome and assist.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongping 1, Qu Jia sent his nephew Xiaoliang—who had taken the titles Left Guard General and Governor of Tiandi—to the capital, again asking to move inward and begging for troops to escort them.

sentences.zh: 於是遣龍驤將軍孟威發涼州兵三千人迎之，至伊吾，失期而反。

translations.literal: Thereupon they sent the Dragon Cavalry General Meng Wei to dispatch three thousand Liang province troops to welcome them; reaching Yiwu, he missed the deadline and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The court then sent Dragon Cavalry General Meng Wei with three thousand Liang troops to meet them, but he reached only Yiwu, missed the rendezvous, and turned back.

sentences.zh: 于後十餘遣使獻珠像、白黑貂裘、名馬、鹽枕等，款誠備至。

translations.literal: For the next ten-plus years he repeatedly sent envoys presenting pearl images, white and black sable fur coats, famous horses, salt pillows, and the like, with utmost sincerity and devotion.
translations.idiomatic: For more than ten years afterward he sent envoys bearing pearl images, white and black sable coats, prized horses, salt pillows, and the like, with unwavering sincerity.

sentences.zh: 唯賜優旨，卒不重迎。

translations.literal: Only gracious edicts were bestowed; in the end he was not again welcomed inward.
translations.idiomatic: The court replied only with gracious edicts and never again sent troops to receive them.

sentences.zh: 三年，嘉遣使朝貢，宣武又遣孟威使詔勞之。

translations.literal: In the third year, Jia sent envoys with tribute; Emperor Xuanwu again sent Meng Wei with an edict to console him.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Qu Jia sent tribute envoys, and Emperor Xuanwu again dispatched Meng Wei with an edict of consolation.

sentences.zh: 延昌中，以嘉為持節、平西將軍、瓜州刺史、泰臨縣開國伯，私署王如故。

translations.literal: In the Yanchang period he was made Holder of the Staff, Pacifier of the West General, Governor of Guazhou, and Baron of Tailin County with founding nobility, while his self-assumed title of king remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: During Yanchang, Qu Jia was appointed Holder of the Staff, Pacifier of the West General, Governor of Guazhou, and founding Baron of Tailin County, while retaining his self-assumed royal title.

sentences.zh: 熙平初，遣使朝獻。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiping, he sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xiping era he sent envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「卿地隔關山，境接荒漠，頻請朝援，徙國內遷。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Your territory is cut off by passes and mountains; your border adjoins the wilderness. You have repeatedly requested audiences and aid, asking to move the state inward.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said: "Your land lies beyond the passes, your border touches the desert, and you have repeatedly asked for imperial aid to move your kingdom inward.

sentences.zh: 雖來誠可嘉，即於理未帖。

translations.literal: Although your coming sincerity is commendable, as a matter of principle it is not fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Your loyalty is admirable, but the request itself is impracticable.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 彼之颧庶，是漢、魏遺黎，自晉氏不綱，因難播越，成家立國，世積已久。

translations.literal: The common people there are remnants of Han and Wei; since the Jin dynasty lost its restraint, through hardships they scattered abroad, established families and a state, and this has accumulated for generations.
translations.idiomatic: Your people are descendants of Han and Wei who, after the Jin lost control, fled hardship, settled there, and built a kingdom that has stood for generations.

sentences.zh: 惡徙重遷，人懷戀舊。

translations.literal: They loathe migration and heavy relocations; people cherish their old homeland.
translations.idiomatic: They hate uprooting and cherish their old home.

sentences.zh: 今若動之，恐異同之變，爰在肘腋，不得便如來表也。」

translations.literal: If we move them now, I fear mutiny and discord would arise right at our flank; we cannot conveniently act as your memorial requests.
translations.idiomatic: If we forced them to move now, rebellion might erupt at our very side; we cannot do as your memorial asks.

sentences.zh: 神龜元年冬，孝亮復表求援內徙，朝廷不許。

translations.literal: In winter of the first year of Shengui, Xiaoliang again memorialized begging aid to move inward; the court did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of Shengui 1, Xiaoliang again petitioned for aid to move inward, and the court refused.

sentences.zh: 正光元年，明帝遺假員外將軍趙義等使於嘉。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenguang, Emperor Ming sent the acting Exterior Affairs General Zhao Yi and others as envoys to Jia.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguang 1, Emperor Ming sent Acting Exterior Affairs General Zhao Yi and others as envoys to Qu Jia.

sentences.zh: 嘉朝貢不絕，又遣使奉表，自以邊遐，不習典誥，求借《五經》、諸史，並請國子助教劉燮以為博士，明帝許之。

translations.literal: Jia's tribute missions never ceased; he again sent envoys with a memorial, considering himself remote on the frontier and unskilled in court regulations, requesting to borrow the Five Classics and various histories, and also requesting the National University assistant instructor Liu Xie to serve as Erudite; Emperor Ming granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Qu Jia's tribute never ceased; he sent another memorial saying that, remote on the frontier, he was unversed in court ritual and asked to borrow the Five Classics and standard histories, and also requested National University assistant instructor Liu Xie as his Erudite. Emperor Ming agreed.

sentences.zh: 嘉死，贈鎮西將軍、涼州刺史。

translations.literal: When Jia died, he was posthumously granted General Who Pacifies the West and Governor of Liang province.
translations.idiomatic: When Qu Jia died, he was posthumously made General Who Pacifies the West and Governor of Liang Province.

sentences.zh: 其國，周時，城有一十六。

translations.literal: As for the state—in Zhou times there were sixteen cities.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhou times the kingdom had sixteen cities.

sentences.zh: 後至隋時，城有十八。

translations.literal: Later, by Sui times there were eighteen cities.
translations.idiomatic: By Sui times there were eighteen.

sentences.zh: 其都城周回一千八百四十步，於坐室畫魯哀公問政於孔子之像。

translations.literal: Its capital city measured one thousand eight hundred forty paces in circumference; in the audience hall they painted the image of Duke Ai of Lu inquiring about government from Confucius.
translations.idiomatic: The capital measured eighteen hundred forty paces around its walls; in the hall they painted Duke Ai of Lu asking Confucius about government.

sentences.zh: 官有令尹一人，比中夏相國；

translations.literal: In office there was one Chief Minister, comparable to the Chancellor of State in central China;
translations.idiomatic: There was one Chief Minister, equivalent to a Chancellor of State in China;

sentences.zh: 次有公二人，皆王子也，一為交河公，一為田地公；

translations.literal: next were two dukes, both princes of the royal house—one the Duke of Jiaohe, one the Duke of Tiandi;
translations.idiomatic: next two dukes, both royal princes—the Duke of Jiaohe and the Duke of Tiandi;

sentences.zh: 次有左右衛；

translations.literal: next were the Left and Right Guards;
translations.idiomatic: then the Left and Right Guards;

sentences.zh: 次有八長史，曰吏部、祠部、庫部、倉部、主客、禮部、戶部、兵部等長史也；

translations.literal: next were eight chief secretaries—the Chief Secretaries of Personnel, Sacrificial Affairs, Treasury, Granary, Reception of Guests, Rites, Households, and Military Affairs;
translations.idiomatic: then eight chief secretaries—for Personnel, Sacrificial Affairs, Treasury, Granary, Reception of Guests, Rites, Households, and Military Affairs;

sentences.zh: 次有五將軍，曰建武、威遠、陵江、殿中、伏波等將軍也；

translations.literal: next were five generals—the Generals of Establishing Martial Prowess, Awesome Reach, River-towering, Palace Guard, and Wave-quelling;
translations.idiomatic: then five generals—Establishing Martial Prowess, Awesome Reach, River-towering, Palace Guard, and Wave-quelling;

sentences.zh: 次有八司馬，長史之副也；

translations.literal: next were eight marshals, deputies to the chief secretaries;
translations.idiomatic: then eight marshals, deputies to the chief secretaries;

sentences.zh: 次有侍郎、校郎、主簿、從事，階位相次，分掌諸事。

translations.literal: next were Attendants, Reviewing Clerks, Chief Clerks, and Staff Officers, ranks succeeding one another, each administering various affairs.
translations.idiomatic: then Attendants, Reviewing Clerks, Chief Clerks, and Staff Officers in descending rank, each handling assigned duties.

sentences.zh: 次有省事，專掌導引。

translations.literal: next were attendants-in-service who specialized exclusively in ushering and protocol.
translations.idiomatic: Next came attendants-in-service who handled ushering and protocol.

sentences.zh: 其大事決之于王，小事則世子及二公隨狀斷決。

translations.literal: Great affairs were decided by the king; minor affairs were adjudicated as circumstances warranted by the heir and the two dukes.
translations.idiomatic: Major matters were decided by the king; minor ones were judged as circumstances required by the heir apparent and the two dukes.

sentences.zh: 評章錄記，事訖即除，籍書之外，無久掌文案。

translations.literal: They deliberated, recorded, and once a matter was finished removed the record—apart from the registers there were no long-held case files.
translations.idiomatic: Cases were reviewed, recorded, and the record discarded once finished; apart from the registers, no documents were kept on file.

sentences.zh: 官人雖有列位，並無曹府，唯有每早集於牙門，評議眾事。

translations.literal: Although officials had ranked positions, there were no departmental offices; they merely assembled each morning at the court gate to discuss the multitude of affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Officials held rank but had no separate offices; each morning they gathered at the court gate to discuss business.

sentences.zh: 諸城各有戶曹、水曹、田曹。

translations.literal: Each city had Household, Water, and Field bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: Each city had bureaus for households, water, and fields.

sentences.zh: 城遣司馬、侍郎相監檢校，名為令。

translations.literal: The city sent a Marshal and Attendant to supervise and inspect jointly, titled "Magistrate."
translations.idiomatic: Each city sent a marshal and an attendant to supervise and inspect together, styled "Magistrate."

sentences.zh: 服飾，丈夫從胡法，婦人裙襦，頭上作髻。

translations.literal: In dress and adornment, men followed Hu custom; women wore skirts and short jackets with hair done up in buns on the head.
translations.idiomatic: In dress, men followed steppe custom; women wore skirts and jackets with their hair bound in topknots.

sentences.zh: 其風俗政令，與華夏略同，兵器有弓、刀、箭、楯、甲、槊。

translations.literal: Its customs, government, and ordinances were roughly the same as Huaxia; weapons included bows, swords, arrows, shields, armor, and spears.
translations.idiomatic: Customs and government resembled Huaxia; weapons included bows, swords, arrows, shields, armor, and spears.

sentences.zh: 文字亦同華夏，兼用胡書。

translations.literal: Writing too was the same as Huaxia, together with use of Hu script.
translations.idiomatic: Writing followed Huaxia norms as well, though Hu script was also used.

sentences.zh: 有《毛詩》、《論語》、《孝經》，置學官弟子，以相教授。

translations.literal: They had the Mao Odes, Analects, and Classic of Filial Piety; they established academicians and disciples to instruct one another.
translations.idiomatic: They possessed the Mao Odes, Analects, and Classic of Filial Piety, with academicians and disciples teaching one another.

sentences.zh: 雖習讀之，而皆為胡語。

translations.literal: Although they practiced reading them, all were in Hu speech.
translations.idiomatic: Although they studied them, they read them all in the local tongue.

sentences.zh: 賦稅則計田輸銀錢，無者輸麻布。

translations.literal: For taxes and levies they reckoned fields and paid in silver coin; those without it paid hemp cloth.
translations.idiomatic: Taxes were assessed by field and paid in silver; those without silver paid in hemp cloth.

sentences.zh: 其刑法、風俗、昏姻、喪葬與華夏小異而大同。

translations.literal: Its penal code, customs, marriage, and funerals differed slightly from Huaxia but were largely the same.
translations.idiomatic: Penal law, customs, marriage, and burial differed slightly from Huaxia but were largely the same.

sentences.zh: 自敦煌向其國，多沙磧，茫然無有蹊徑，欲往者，尋其人畜骸骨而去。

translations.literal: From Dunhuang toward their state the route was mostly shifting sands; blankly there were no paths or tracks—those who wished to go sought human and livestock bones to find their way.
translations.idiomatic: From Dunhuang to Gaochang the route crossed mostly desert with no clear track; travelers had to follow the bones of men and beasts to find their way.

sentences.zh: 路中或聞歌哭聲，行人尋之，多致亡失，蓋魑魅魍魎也。

translations.literal: On the road one might hear songs and weeping; travelers who went to seek them often came to loss—it was the work of evil spirits and demons.
translations.idiomatic: Travelers sometimes heard singing and weeping along the way; those who went to investigate often vanished—work, it was said, of demons and goblins.

sentences.zh: 故商客往來，多取伊吾路。

translations.literal: Therefore merchants traveling back and forth mostly took the Yiwu route.
translations.idiomatic: Merchants therefore usually took the Yiwu route instead.

sentences.zh: 開皇十年，突厥破其四城，有二千人來歸中國。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Kaihuang, the Turks destroyed four of its cities; two thousand people came to submit to China.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaihuang 10 the Turks captured four of its cities, and two thousand people fled to China.

sentences.zh: 堅死，子伯雅立。

translations.literal: When Jian died, his son Boya succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When Qu Jian died, his son Boya succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 其大母本突厥可汗女，其父死，突厥令依其俗。

translations.literal: His grandmother was originally a daughter of a Turk khan; when his father died, the Turks ordered him to follow their custom.
translations.idiomatic: His grandmother had been a Turk khan's daughter; when his father died, the Turks ordered Boya to observe their levirate custom.

sentences.zh: 伯雅不從者久之。

translations.literal: Boya refused for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: Boya refused for a long time.

sentences.zh: 突厥逼之，不得已而從。

translations.literal: The Turks pressed him; having no alternative, he complied.
translations.idiomatic: The Turks pressed him until he had no choice but to comply.

sentences.zh: 煬帝即位，引致諸蕃。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded, he summoned the various barbarian states.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang took the throne, he summoned the frontier states to court.

sentences.zh: 大業四年，遣使貢獻，帝待其使甚厚。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Daye, they sent envoys with tribute; the emperor treated their envoys very generously.
translations.idiomatic: In Daye 4 he sent tribute envoys, and the emperor treated them with great generosity.

sentences.zh: 明年伯雅來朝，因從擊高麗。

translations.literal: The next year Boya came to court and joined the campaign against Goguryeo.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Boya came to court and joined the campaign against Goguryeo.

sentences.zh: 還，尚宗室女華容公主。

translations.literal: Returning, he married the imperial clanswoman Princess Huarong.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he married Princess Huarong, a clanswoman of the imperial house.

sentences.zh: 八年冬，歸蕃，下令國中曰：「先者，以國處邊荒境，被髮左衽。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, winter, returning to his state, he issued an order within the state, saying: "Formerly, because the state lay in a remote borderland, we wore our hair loose and buttoned to the left.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the eighth year, back in his kingdom, he issued a proclamation: "Formerly, because our state lay in a remote borderland, we wore our hair loose and buttoned our coats to the left.

sentences.zh: 今大隋統御，宇宙平一。

translations.literal: Now Great Sui unifies and pacifies; the universe is united as one.
translations.idiomatic: Now Great Sui rules all under Heaven and the realm is united.

sentences.zh: 孤既沐浴和風，庶均大化。

translations.literal: I, having bathed in harmonious winds, wish to share equally in great transformation.
translations.idiomatic: I have bathed in its civilizing breeze and wish to share fully in its great transformation.

sentences.zh: 其庶人以上，皆宜解辮削衽。」

translations.literal: All common people and above should undo their braids and cut their lapel to the right.
translations.idiomatic: All commoners and above should undo their braids and cut their lapels to the right.

sentences.zh: 帝聞而善之，下詔曰：「光祿大夫、弁國公、高昌王伯雅，本自諸華，世祚西壤，昔因多難，翦為胡服。

translations.literal: The emperor heard and approved; he issued an edict saying: "Grand Master of Splendid Merit, Duke of Bianguo, King of Gaochang Boya—he was originally of the various Hua; for generations he has held the western frontier. Formerly, through many hardships, he was clipped into Hu dress.
