translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved and issued an edict: "Grand Master of Splendid Merit, Duke of Bianguo, King of Gaochang Boya is descended from the Chinese lineages that have long held the western frontier; through many hardships he was reduced to barbarian dress.

sentences.zh: 自我皇隋，平一宇宙，伯雅逾沙忘阻，奉貢來庭，削衽曳裾，變夷從夏，可賜衣冠，仍班製造之式。」

translations.literal: Since our august Sui pacified the universe as one, Boya crossed the sands forgetting barriers, came to court bearing tribute, cut his lapel and trailed his robe-skirt, changed from barbarian to follow Xia—he may be granted caps and gowns, and the patterns for their manufacture shall still be distributed.
translations.idiomatic: Since our Sui united the realm, Boya has crossed the desert, forgotten its barriers, come to court with tribute, cut his lapel, and trailed his robe in Chinese fashion—changing from barbarian ways to follow Xia. Let caps and gowns be granted him, together with patterns for their manufacture.

sentences.zh: 然伯雅先臣鐵勒，恆遣重臣在高昌國，有商胡往來者則稅之，送於鐵勒。

translations.literal: Yet Boya had earlier submitted to the Tiele; he constantly sent high ministers in the state of Gaochang, and when merchant Hu came and went they were taxed and sent to the Tiele.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Boya had long submitted to the Tiele and kept senior ministers in Gaochang to tax passing merchant caravans and send the proceeds to the Tiele.

sentences.zh: 雖有此令取悅中華，然竟畏鐵勒，不敢改也。

translations.literal: Although he had this order to please China, in the end he feared the Tiele and did not dare change.
translations.idiomatic: Although he issued this order to please China, he still feared the Tiele and did not dare actually change.

sentences.zh: 自是歲令貢方物。

translations.literal: From then on tribute of regional products was sent every year.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he sent regional tribute every year.

sentences.zh: 且彌國，都天山東于大谷，在車師北，去代一萬五百七十里。

translations.literal: The state of Qiemi had its capital east of the Tianshan in Dayu valley, north of Cheshi, ten thousand five hundred seventy li from Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Qiemi, capital east of the Tianshan in Dayu valley, north of Cheshi, lay ten thousand five hundred seventy li from the Wei capital.

sentences.zh: 本役屬車師。

translations.literal: Originally it was subordinate to Cheshi.
translations.idiomatic: It had originally been subject to Cheshi.

sentences.zh: 焉耆國，在車師南都員渠城，白山南七十里，漢時舊國也，去代一萬二百里。

translations.literal: The state of Yanqi was at Yuanqu city, the southern capital of Cheshi, seventy li south of White Mountain; it was the old state of Han times, ten thousand two hundred li from Dai.
translations.idiomatic: The state of Yanqi lay at Yuanqu, the southern capital of Cheshi, seventy li south of White Mountain; an old Han-era kingdom, it was ten thousand two hundred li from Dai.

sentences.zh: 其王姓龍，名鳩屍畢那，即前涼張軌所討龍熙之胤。

translations.literal: Its king bore the surname Long and the name Jushibina—the descendant of Long Xi whom Zhang Gui of Former Liang had campaigned against.
translations.idiomatic: Its king, surname Long and personal name Jushibina, was a descendant of Long Xi, whom Zhang Gui of Former Liang had campaigned against.

sentences.zh: 所都城方二里。

translations.literal: The city they held as capital was two li square.
translations.idiomatic: The capital city was two li square.

sentences.zh: 國內凡有九城。

translations.literal: Within the state there were nine cities in all.
translations.idiomatic: Within the kingdom there were nine cities in all.

sentences.zh: 國小人貧，無綱紀法令。

translations.literal: The state was small and the people poor; there were no statutes or ordinances.
translations.idiomatic: The state was small and poor and had no formal laws or regulations.

sentences.zh: 兵有弓、刀、甲、槊。

translations.literal: In arms there were bows, swords, armor, and spears.
translations.idiomatic: Its arms included bows, swords, armor, and spears.

sentences.zh: 婚姻略同華夏。

translations.literal: Marriage was roughly the same as Huaxia.
translations.idiomatic: Marriage customs resembled those of Huaxia.

sentences.zh: 死亡者，皆焚而後葬，其服制滿七日則除之。

translations.literal: When people died, all were burned and then buried; mourning dress was removed after a full seven days.
translations.idiomatic: The dead were cremated before burial, and mourning dress was cast off after seven days.

sentences.zh: 丈夫並翦髮以為首飾。

translations.literal: Men all cut their hair to serve as head ornament.
translations.idiomatic: Men all cut their hair short as a form of adornment.

sentences.zh: 文字與婆羅門同。

translations.literal: Writing was the same as Brahmin script.
translations.idiomatic: Writing followed the Brahmin script.

sentences.zh: 俗事天神，並崇信佛法也。

translations.literal: In custom they served the Heavenly Spirit and also widely believed in the Buddhist Law.
translations.idiomatic: They worshipped the Heavenly Spirit and also devoutly followed Buddhism.

sentences.zh: 尤重二月八日、四月八日。

translations.literal: They especially honored the eighth day of the second month and the eighth day of the fourth month.
translations.idiomatic: They especially observed the eighth day of the second month and the eighth day of the fourth month.

sentences.zh: 是日也，其國咸依釋教，齋戒行道焉。

translations.literal: On those days the whole state observed the Buddhist teaching, fasting and practicing the Way.
translations.idiomatic: On those days the whole kingdom observed Buddhist rites, fasting and performing religious devotions.

sentences.zh: 氣候寒，土田良沃，穀有稻、粟、菽、麥，畜有駝、馬。

translations.literal: The climate was cold; fields and soil were good and fertile; grains included rice, millet, beans, and wheat; livestock included camels and horses.
translations.idiomatic: The climate was cold and the soil fertile; grains included rice, millet, beans, and wheat, and livestock included camels and horses.

sentences.zh: 養蠶，不以為絲，唯充綿纊。

translations.literal: They raised silkworms but did not make them into silk, using them only for cotton wadding.
translations.idiomatic: They raised silkworms but did not reel silk, using the cocoons only for padding.

sentences.zh: 俗尚蒲桃酒，兼愛音樂。

translations.literal: Custom favored grape wine and also loved music.
translations.idiomatic: Grape wine was favored and music widely loved.

sentences.zh: 南去海十餘里，有魚鹽蒲葦之饒。

translations.literal: Ten-plus li south was the sea, rich in fish, salt, rushes, and reeds.
translations.idiomatic: A little more than ten li to the south lay a sea rich in fish, salt, rushes, and reeds.

sentences.zh: 東去高昌九百里，西去龜茲九百里，皆沙磧。

translations.literal: Nine hundred li east to Gaochang, nine hundred li west to Kucha—all shifting sands.
translations.idiomatic: It was nine hundred li east to Gaochang and nine hundred li west to Kucha, all desert.

sentences.zh: 東南去瓜州二千二百里。

translations.literal: Two thousand two hundred li southeast to Guazhou.
translations.idiomatic: It was twenty-two hundred li southeast of Guazhou.

sentences.zh: 恃地多險，頗剽劫中國使。

translations.literal: Relying on the land's many natural defenses, they frequently plundered and robbed Chinese envoys.
translations.idiomatic: Trusting in its rugged terrain, it frequently robbed Chinese envoys.

sentences.zh: 太武怒之，詔成周公萬度歸討之，約齎輕糧，取食路次。

translations.literal: Emperor Taiwu was enraged; he ordered the Prince of Chengdu Wanduigui to campaign against them, instructing him to carry light provisions and take food along the route.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taiwu was furious and ordered Prince of Chengdu Wanduigui to attack them, telling him to travel light and live off the land.

sentences.zh: 度歸入焉耆東界，擊其邊守左回、尉犁二城，拔之，進軍圍員渠。

translations.literal: Wanduigui entered Yanqi's eastern border, struck its frontier garrisons the two cities of Zuohui and Yuli, captured them, and advanced to besiege Yuanqu.
translations.idiomatic: Wanduigui entered Yanqi's eastern frontier, took the border towns of Zuohui and Yuli, and advanced to besiege Yuanqu.

sentences.zh: 鳩屍畢那以四五萬人出城，守險以距。

translations.literal: Jushibina led forty or fifty thousand men out of the city and held difficult terrain to resist.
translations.idiomatic: Jushibina marched out with forty or fifty thousand men and held the defiles to block them.

sentences.zh: 度歸募壯勇，短兵直往沖，鳩屍畢那眾大潰，盡虜之，單騎走入山中。

translations.literal: Duigui recruited brave warriors and charged straight in with close weapons; Jushibina's army collapsed in rout, all were captured, and he alone fled on horseback into the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Duigui rallied picked warriors and charged straight in at close quarters; Jushibina's force broke completely and was taken captive, while he alone escaped on horseback into the mountains.

sentences.zh: 度歸進屠其城，四鄙諸戎皆降服。

translations.literal: Duigui advanced and slaughtered the city; all the barbarian tribes on the four borders submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Duigui advanced, sacked the city, and all the frontier tribes submitted.

sentences.zh: 焉耆為國，鬥絕一隅，不亂日久，獲其珍奇異玩，殊方譎詭難識之物，橐駝、馬、牛、雜畜巨萬。

translations.literal: Yanqi as a state was isolated in a corner and had long been undisturbed; they seized its rare treasures and curios, objects from distant lands strange and hard to identify, and camels, horses, cattle, and miscellaneous livestock in vast numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Yanqi had long stood apart in peace; the victors seized rare treasures and exotic curios from distant lands, together with tens of thousands of camels, horses, cattle, and other livestock.

sentences.zh: 時太武幸陰山北宮，度歸破焉耆露板至，帝省訖，賜司徒崔浩書曰：「萬度歸以五千騎，經萬餘里，拔焉耆三城，獲其珍奇異物及諸委積不可勝數。

translations.literal: At the time Emperor Taiwu was at the Northern Palace on Mount Yinshan; when Duigui's report on the conquest of Yanqi arrived, the emperor finished reading it and sent a letter to Minister of State Cui Hao saying: "Wan Duigui with five thousand cavalry, traveling over ten thousand li, captured three cities of Yanqi and obtained rare treasures and accumulated stores beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taiwu was then at the Northern Palace on Mount Yinshan. When Duigui's victory report on Yanqi arrived, the emperor read it through and wrote to Minister of State Cui Hao: "Wan Duigui, with five thousand horsemen, crossed more than ten thousand li, took three Yanqi cities, and seized rare treasures and stored goods beyond numbering.

sentences.zh: 自古帝王，雖云即序西戎，有如指注，不能控引也。

translations.literal: Since ancient times, although emperors spoke of bringing the Western Rong into order, it was like pointing at them—they could not control and draw them in.
translations.idiomatic: Since antiquity, even when emperors spoke of bringing the Western Rong into order, it was like pointing at them from afar—they could not truly control them.

sentences.zh: 朕今手把而有之，如何？」

translations.literal: I now hold them in my hand and possess them—what do you think?"
translations.idiomatic: I now hold them in my hand—what do you think of that?"

sentences.zh: 浩上書稱美。

translations.literal: Cui Hao submitted a memorial praising this.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Hao submitted a memorial in praise.

sentences.zh: 遂命度歸鎮撫其人。

translations.literal: He then ordered Duigui to pacify and settle the people.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then ordered Duigui to pacify and govern the people.

sentences.zh: 初，鳩屍畢那走山中，猶覬城不拔，得還其國。

translations.literal: At first, Jushibina fled into the mountains, still hoping the city would not fall and he could return to his state.
translations.idiomatic: At first Jushibina fled into the mountains, still hoping the city would hold and he could return home.

sentences.zh: 既見盡為度歸所克，乃奔龜茲。

translations.literal: When he saw everything had been conquered by Duigui, he fled to Kucha.
translations.idiomatic: When he saw that Duigui had taken everything, he fled to Kucha.

sentences.zh: 龜茲以其婿，厚待之。

translations.literal: Kucha treated him generously as its son-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: Kucha welcomed him warmly as a son-in-law.

sentences.zh: 周保定四年，其王遣使獻名焉。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Baoding of Zhou, its king sent envoys presenting tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhou Baoding 4, its king sent envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 隋大業中，其王龍突騎支遣使貢方物。

translations.literal: During Sui Daye, its king Long Tuqizhi sent envoys presenting regional products.
translations.idiomatic: During the Sui Daye era, its king Long Tuqizhi sent envoys with regional tribute.

sentences.zh: 是時，其國勝兵千餘人而已。

translations.literal: At that time, its effective troops numbered only about a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: At that time it could field only about a thousand soldiers.

sentences.zh: 龜茲國，在尉犁西北，白山之南一百七十里，都延城，漢時舊國也，去代一萬二百八十里。

translations.literal: The state of Kucha lay northwest of Yuli, one hundred seventy li south of White Mountain, with its capital at Yancheng; it was the old state of Han times, ten thousand two hundred eighty li from Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Kucha lay northwest of Yuli, one hundred seventy li south of White Mountain, with its capital at Yancheng; an old Han-era kingdom, it was ten thousand two hundred eighty li from Dai.

sentences.zh: 其王姓白，即後涼呂光所立白震之後。

translations.literal: Its king bore the surname Bai—the descendant of Bai Zhen whom Lü Guang of Later Liang had installed.
translations.idiomatic: Its king, surname Bai, was a descendant of Bai Zhen, whom Lü Guang of Later Liang had installed.

sentences.zh: 其王頭系彩帶，垂之於後，坐金師子床。

translations.literal: The king tied a colored sash to his head, letting it hang behind, and sat on a golden lion couch.
translations.idiomatic: The king wore a colored sash tied about his head, trailing behind him, and sat on a golden lion throne.

sentences.zh: 所居城方五六里。

translations.literal: The city where he resided was five or six li square.
translations.idiomatic: The royal city was five or six li square.

sentences.zh: 其刑法，殺人者死，劫賊則斷其一臂，並刖一足。

translations.literal: Its penal code: murderers were put to death; robbers had one arm cut off and one foot amputated as well.
translations.idiomatic: Under its penal code, murderers were executed; robbers had one arm severed and one foot cut off.

sentences.zh: 賦稅，准地征租，無田者則稅銀。

translations.literal: For taxes and levies, rent was collected by land; those without fields paid a silver tax.
translations.idiomatic: Taxes were assessed by land; those without fields paid in silver.

sentences.zh: 風俗、婚姻、喪葬、物產與焉耆略同，唯氣候少溫為異。

translations.literal: Customs, marriage, funerals, and products were roughly the same as Yanqi, differing only in that the climate was somewhat warmer.
translations.idiomatic: Its customs, marriage, funerals, and products closely resembled those of Yanqi, except that the climate was somewhat warmer.

sentences.zh: 又出細氈、燒銅、鐵、鉛、麖皮、氍毹、鐃沙、鹽綠、雌黃、胡粉、安息香、良馬、犎牛等。

translations.literal: It also produced fine felt, refined copper, iron, lead, musk-deer hides, carpets, sal ammoniac, vitriol, orpiment, lead white, benzoin, fine horses, zebu cattle, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: It also exported fine felt, refined copper, iron, lead, musk-deer hides, carpets, sal ammoniac, vitriol, orpiment, lead white, benzoin, fine horses, zebu cattle, and the like.

sentences.zh: 東有輪台，即漢貳師將軍李廣利所屠者。

translations.literal: To the east was Luntai—the place Han General of the Second Division Li Guangli had slaughtered.
translations.idiomatic: To the east lay Luntai, the city Han General of the Second Division Li Guangli had destroyed.

sentences.zh: 其南三百里，有大河東流，號計戍水，即黃河也。

translations.literal: Three hundred li to its south was a great river flowing east, called Jishui—that is, the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: Three hundred li to the south was a great river flowing east, called Jishui—the text identifies it as the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 東去焉耆九百里，南去于闐一千四百里，西去疏勒一千五百里，北去突厥牙六百餘里，東南去瓜州三千一百里。

translations.literal: Nine hundred li east to Yanqi, fourteen hundred li south to Khotan, fifteen hundred li west to Kashgar, more than six hundred li north to the Turk headquarters, and thirty-one hundred li southeast to Guazhou.
translations.idiomatic: It was nine hundred li east of Yanqi, fourteen hundred li south of Khotan, fifteen hundred li west of Kashgar, more than six hundred li north of the Turk headquarters, and thirty-one hundred li southeast of Guazhou.

sentences.zh: 其東關城戍，寇竊非一，太武詔萬度歸率騎一千以擊之。

translations.literal: Its eastern border fortresses frequently raided and plundered; Emperor Taiwu ordered Wan Duigui to lead a thousand cavalry to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: Its eastern border forts had raided repeatedly; Emperor Taiwu ordered Wan Duigui to strike them with a thousand horsemen.

sentences.zh: 龜茲遣烏羯目提等領兵三千距戰，度歸擊走之，斬二百餘級，大獲駝馬而還。

translations.literal: Kucha sent Wujiemuti and others leading three thousand troops to resist; Duigui routed them, beheaded more than two hundred, and returned with great captures of camels and horses.
translations.idiomatic: Kucha sent Wujiemuti and others with three thousand men to resist; Duigui drove them off, took more than two hundred heads, and returned with a great haul of camels and horses.

sentences.zh: 俗性多淫，置女市，收男子錢以入官。

translations.literal: By custom the people were very licentious; they established a women's market, collecting money from men for the state treasury.
translations.idiomatic: The people were licentious by custom; they maintained a women's market and collected men's payments for the state.

sentences.zh: 土多孔雀，群飛山谷間，人取而食之，孳乳如雞鶩，其王家恆有千餘隻云。

translations.literal: The land had many peacocks flocking in mountain valleys; people caught and ate them; they bred like chickens and ducks; the royal house constantly had over a thousand, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Peacocks were abundant, flocking through the valleys; people caught and ate them, and they bred like chickens and ducks—the royal house, it is said, always kept more than a thousand.

sentences.zh: 其國西北大山中有如膏者，流出成川，行數里入地，狀如䬾糊，甚臭。

translations.literal: In the great mountains northwest of the state there was something like grease that flowed out forming a stream, traveled several li then entered the ground, resembling porridge paste, very foul-smelling.
translations.idiomatic: In the great mountains northwest of the kingdom flowed a greasy substance that formed a stream, ran several li, then sank into the earth; it looked like porridge paste and smelled foul.

sentences.zh: 服之，發齒已落者，能令更生，癘人服之，皆愈。

translations.literal: Taken internally, it could make hair and teeth that had fallen grow again; lepers who took it were all cured.
translations.idiomatic: Taken internally, it could restore hair and teeth that had fallen out; lepers who consumed it were all cured.

sentences.zh: 自後每使朝貢。

translations.literal: From then on, on each mission they presented tribute at court.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter they sent tribute with every envoy mission.

sentences.zh: 周保定元年，其王遣使來獻。

translations.literal: In the first year of Baoding of Zhou, its king sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhou Baoding 1, its king sent envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 隋大業中，其王白蘇尼栎巫遣使朝，貢方物。

translations.literal: During Sui Daye, its king Bai Sunilüwu sent envoys to court presenting regional products.
translations.idiomatic: During the Sui Daye era, its king Bai Sunilüwu sent envoys to court with regional tribute.

sentences.zh: 是時，其國勝兵可數千人。

translations.literal: At that time, its effective troops numbered several thousand.
translations.idiomatic: At that time it could field several thousand soldiers.

sentences.zh: 姑默國，居南城，在龜茲西，去代一萬五百里。

translations.literal: The state of Gumo had its seat at Nancheng, west of Kucha, ten thousand five hundred li from Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Gumo, seat at Nancheng, west of Kucha, lay ten thousand five hundred li from Dai.

sentences.zh: 役屬龜茲。

translations.literal: It was subject to Kucha.
translations.idiomatic: It was subject to Kucha.

sentences.zh: 溫宿國，居溫宿城，在姑默西北，去代一萬五百五十里。

translations.literal: The state of Wensu had its seat at Wensu city, northwest of Gumo, ten thousand five hundred fifty li from Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Wensu, capital at Wensu city, northwest of Gumo, lay ten thousand five hundred fifty li from Dai.

sentences.zh: 役屬龜茲。

translations.literal: It was subject to Kucha.
translations.idiomatic: It was subject to Kucha.

sentences.zh: 尉頭國，居尉頭城，在溫宿北，去代一萬六百五十里。

translations.literal: The state of Weitou had its seat at Weitou city, north of Wensu, ten thousand six hundred fifty li from Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Weitou, capital at Weitou city, north of Wensu, lay ten thousand six hundred fifty li from Dai.

sentences.zh: 役屬龜茲。

translations.literal: It was subject to Kucha.
translations.idiomatic: It was subject to Kucha.

sentences.zh: 烏孫國，居赤穀城，在龜茲西北，去代一萬八十里。

translations.literal: The state of Wusun had its seat at Chigu city, northwest of Kucha, ten thousand eighty li from Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Wusun, capital at Chigu city, northwest of Kucha, lay ten thousand eighty li from Dai.

sentences.zh: 其國數為蠕蠕所侵，西徙蔥嶺山中。

translations.literal: Its state was frequently invaded by the Rouran and moved west into the Pamir mountains.
translations.idiomatic: The state was repeatedly invaded by the Rouran and moved west into the Pamirs.

sentences.zh: 無城郭，隨畜牧逐水草。

translations.literal: It had no walled cities and followed pastoral life, pursuing water and grass.
translations.idiomatic: It had no walled cities and lived by herding, moving after pasture and water.

sentences.zh: 太延三年，遣使者董琬等使其國，後每使朝貢。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taiyan, envoys Dong Wan and others were dispatched to their state; afterward tribute was sent every year.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiyan 3, the court sent envoys led by Dong Wan to their state; thereafter it sent tribute every year.

sentences.zh: 疏勒國，在姑默西，白山南百餘里，漢時舊國也。

translations.literal: The state of Kashgar lay west of Gumo, more than a hundred li south of White Mountain; it was the old state of Han times.
translations.idiomatic: Kashgar lay west of Gumo, south of White Mountain by more than a hundred li; it was an old Han-era kingdom.

sentences.zh: 去代一萬一千二百五十里。

translations.literal: Eleven thousand two hundred fifty li from Dai.
translations.idiomatic: It lay eleven thousand two hundred fifty li from Dai.

sentences.zh: 文成末，其王遣使送釋迦牟尼佛袈裟一，長二丈餘。

translations.literal: Near the end of Emperor Wencheng's reign, its king sent envoys presenting one kāṣāya of Śākyamuni Buddha, more than two zhang long.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of Emperor Wencheng's reign, its king sent envoys with a kāṣāya said to belong to Śākyamuni Buddha, more than two zhang in length.

sentences.zh: 帝以審是佛衣，應有靈異，遂燒之以驗虛實，置於猛火之上，經日不然，觀者莫不悚駭，心形俱肅。

translations.literal: The emperor, believing it was truly the Buddha's robe and ought to have supernatural properties, burned it to test truth and falsehood; placed on fierce fire, after a full day it did not burn; viewers were all shocked, hearts and bearing alike solemn.
translations.idiomatic: Convinced it was the Buddha's robe and ought to show miraculous power, the emperor burned it to test its authenticity; though placed in fierce flames for a full day, it did not burn, and every onlooker was awestruck into reverent silence.

sentences.zh: 其王戴金師子冠。

translations.literal: Its king wore a golden lion crown.
translations.idiomatic: Its king wore a golden lion crown.

sentences.zh: 土多稻、粟、麻、麥、銅、鐵、錫、雌黃，每歲常供送於突厥。

translations.literal: The land was rich in rice, millet, hemp, wheat, copper, iron, tin, and orpiment; every year supplies were regularly sent to the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: The land produced rice, millet, hemp, wheat, copper, iron, tin, and orpiment, which it sent annually to the Turks.

sentences.zh: 其都城方五里。

translations.literal: Its capital city was five li square.
translations.idiomatic: Its capital was five li square.

sentences.zh: 國內有大城十二，小城數十。

translations.literal: Within the state were twelve large cities and several dozen small ones.
translations.idiomatic: Within the kingdom were twelve great cities and several dozen smaller ones.

sentences.zh: 人手足皆六指，產子非六指者即不育。

translations.literal: People's hands and feet all had six fingers; children born without six fingers were not reared.
translations.idiomatic: People's hands and feet all had six fingers; infants born without six fingers were not kept.

sentences.zh: 勝兵者二千人。

translations.literal: Effective troops numbered two thousand.
translations.idiomatic: It could field two thousand soldiers.

sentences.zh: 南有黃河，西帶蔥嶺，東去龜茲千五百里，西去吲汗國千里，南去硃俱波八九百里，東北至突厥牙千餘里，東南去瓜州四千六百里。

translations.literal: To the south was the Yellow River; to the west it bordered the Pamirs; fifteen hundred li east to Kucha, a thousand li west to Yinghan, eight or nine hundred li south to Zhujubo, more than a thousand li northeast to the Turk headquarters, and forty-six hundred li southeast to Guazhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow River lay to the south and the Pamirs to the west; it was fifteen hundred li east of Kucha, a thousand li west of Yinghan, eight or nine hundred li south of Zhujubo, more than a thousand li northeast of the Turk headquarters, and forty-six hundred li southeast of Guazhou.

sentences.zh: 悅般國，在烏孫西北，去代一萬九百三十里。

translations.literal: The state of Yueban lay northwest of Wusun, ten thousand nine hundred thirty li from Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Yueban, northwest of Wusun, lay ten thousand nine hundred thirty li from Dai.

sentences.zh: 其先，匈奴北單于之部落也。

translations.literal: In origin it was a tribe of the Northern Chanyu of the Xiongnu.
translations.idiomatic: Its people were originally a tribe of the Xiongnu Northern Chanyu.

sentences.zh: 為漢車騎將軍竇憲所逐，北單于度金微山西走康居，其羸弱不能去者，住龜茲北。

translations.literal: Pursued by Han General of the Chariots and Cavalry Dou Xian, the Northern Chanyu crossed west of Mount Jinwei into Kangju; those too weak to go remained north of Kucha.
translations.idiomatic: When Han General of the Chariots and Cavalry Dou Xian drove them out, the Northern Chanyu fled west of Mount Jinwei into Kangju; those too weak to follow remained north of Kucha.

sentences.zh: 地方數千里，眾可二十餘萬，涼州人猶謂之單于王。

translations.literal: Their territory was several thousand li square; their population could reach more than two hundred thousand; people of Liang province still called them the Chanyu kings.
translations.idiomatic: Their territory covered several thousand li; their population reached more than two hundred thousand; people of Liang province still called them the Chanyu kings.

sentences.zh: 其風俗言語與高車同，而其人清潔于胡。

translations.literal: Their customs and language were the same as the Gaoche, but the people were cleaner than the Hu.
translations.idiomatic: Their customs and language matched those of the Gaoche, but the people were cleaner than other Hu.

sentences.zh: 俗翦發齊眉，以䬾糊塗之，昱昱然光澤。

translations.literal: By custom they cut their hair level with the eyebrows and smeared it with porridge paste until it gleamed brightly.
translations.idiomatic: By custom they cut their hair level with their eyebrows and coated it with porridge paste until it shone.

sentences.zh: 日三澡漱，然後飲食。

translations.literal: They bathed and rinsed the mouth three times a day before eating and drinking.
translations.idiomatic: They washed and rinsed their mouths three times daily before eating.

sentences.zh: 其國南界有火山，山傍石皆燋鎔，流地數十里乃凝堅，人取以為藥，即石流黃也。

translations.literal: On their state's southern border was a volcano; the stones beside the mountain were scorched and melted, flowing over the ground for several tens of li before hardening; people took it for medicine—that is, flowing yellow stone.
translations.idiomatic: On the southern border stood a volcano whose stones were scorched and melted; the molten rock ran for several tens of li before hardening, and people collected it as medicine—native sulfur.

sentences.zh: 與蠕蠕結好，其王嘗將數千人入蠕蠕國，欲與大檀相見。

translations.literal: They were on friendly terms with the Rouran; their king once led several thousand men into Rouran territory, wishing to meet Datan.
translations.idiomatic: They were allied with the Rouran; their king once led several thousand men into Rouran lands to meet Datan.

sentences.zh: 入其界百餘里，見其部人不浣衣，不絆發，不洗手，婦人口舐器物。

translations.literal: After entering their border more than a hundred li, he saw their tribesmen not washing clothes, not binding hair, not washing hands, and women licking vessels with their mouths.
translations.idiomatic: A hundred li inside their border he saw tribesmen who did not wash clothes, bind their hair, or wash their hands, and women who licked vessels with their mouths.

sentences.zh: 王謂其從臣曰：「汝曹誑我，將我入此狗國中。」

translations.literal: The king said to his followers: "You deceived me and brought me into this dog country."
translations.idiomatic: The king told his attendants, "You lied to me and led me into this dog country."

sentences.zh: 乃馳還。

translations.literal: He then galloped back.
translations.idiomatic: Then he galloped away.

sentences.zh: 大檀遣騎追之，不及。

translations.literal: Datan sent cavalry in pursuit but could not overtake him.
translations.idiomatic: Datan sent horsemen in pursuit but failed to catch him.

sentences.zh: 自是相仇讎，數相征討。

translations.literal: From then on they were mutual enemies and frequently campaigned against each other.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter they became bitter enemies and raided one another repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 真君九年，遣使朝獻。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Zhenjun, they sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenjun 9 they sent tribute envoys.

sentences.zh: 並送幻人，稱能割人喉脈令斷，擊人頭令骨陷，皆血出或數升或盈鬥，以草藥內其口中，令嚼咽之，須臾血止，養瘡一月復常，又無痕瘢。

translations.literal: They also sent illusionists who claimed they could cut a man's throat and pulse so they broke, strike a man's head so the bone sank in—blood flowing out in several sheng or filling a dou—then put herbs in the mouth, have him chew and swallow, and within moments the bleeding stopped; after a month of tending the wound he returned to normal, with no scar.
translations.idiomatic: They also sent illusionists who claimed to sever the throat and pulse, or strike the skull until it sank and blood poured out by the sheng or filled a bushel; then, putting herbs in the victim's mouth to chew, they stopped the bleeding within moments, and after a month of healing the man was whole again, without a scar.

sentences.zh: 世疑其虛，乃取死罪囚試之，皆驗。

translations.literal: The world doubted it was false, so condemned prisoners were taken to test it—all proved true.
translations.idiomatic: Skeptics tested the act on condemned prisoners—and each time it worked.

sentences.zh: 雲中國諸名山皆有此草，乃使人受其術而厚遇之。

translations.literal: They also said that all the famous mountains of Yunzhong had this herb, so men were sent to learn their technique and they were treated generously.
translations.idiomatic: They said the famous mountains of Yunzhong held the same herb, so the court sent men to learn the technique and treated the visitors generously.

sentences.zh: 又言：其國有大術者，蠕蠕來抄掠，術人能作霖雨、盲風、大雪及行潦，蠕蠕凍死漂亡者十二三。

translations.literal: They also said that in their state there was a great adept: when the Rouran came raiding, the adept could summon drenching rain, blinding gales, heavy snow, and rushing floods; one or two tenths of the Rouran froze or drowned.
translations.idiomatic: They also claimed a great adept in their land who, when the Rouran raided, could raise torrential rain, blinding storms, heavy snow, and floods until one or two tenths of the Rouran froze or drowned.

sentences.zh: 是歲，再遣使朝貢，求與官軍東西齊契討蠕蠕。

translations.literal: That year they again sent envoys with tribute, requesting a joint pledge with imperial armies to strike the Rouran from east and west.
translations.idiomatic: That year they sent tribute again, asking for a coordinated campaign with imperial forces against the Rouran from east and west.

sentences.zh: 太武嘉其意，命中外諸軍戒嚴，以淮南王佗為前鋒，襲蠕蠕。

translations.literal: Emperor Taiwu approved their intent and ordered all armies within and without to stand ready; Prince of Huainan Tuo was made vanguard and struck the Rouran.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taiwu welcomed the proposal, put all armies on alert, and sent Prince of Huainan Tuo as vanguard against the Rouran.

sentences.zh: 仍詔有司，以其鼓舞之節，施於樂府。

translations.literal: He also ordered the relevant offices to adopt their drum-and-dance rhythms for the Music Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered the court to adopt their drum-and-dance rhythms for the Music Bureau.

sentences.zh: 自後每使朝貢。

translations.literal: From then on, on each mission they presented tribute at court.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter they sent tribute with every envoy mission.

sentences.zh: 者至拔國，都者至拔城，在疏勒西，去代一萬一千六百二十里。

translations.literal: The state of Jizhibo had its capital at Jizhibo city, west of Kashgar, eleven thousand six hundred twenty li from Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Jizhibo, capital at Jizhibo city, west of Kashgar, lay eleven thousand six hundred twenty li from Dai.

sentences.zh: 其國東有潘賀那山，出美鐵及師子。

translations.literal: East of its state was Mount Panhena, which produced fine iron and lions.
translations.idiomatic: East of the kingdom stood Mount Panhena, source of fine iron and lions.

sentences.zh: 迷密國，都迷密城，在者至拔西，去代一萬二千一百里。

translations.literal: The state of Mimi had its capital at Mimi city, west of Jizhibo, twelve thousand one hundred li from Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Mimi, capital at Mimi city, west of Jizhibo, lay twelve thousand one hundred li from Dai.

sentences.zh: 正平元年，遣使獻一峰黑橐駝。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhengping, they sent envoys presenting one black Bactrian camel.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengping 1 they sent envoys with a single-humped black camel.

sentences.zh: 其國東有山名郁悉滿山，出金、玉，亦多鐵。

translations.literal: East of its state was a mountain called Mount Yuximan, which produced gold, jade, and also much iron.
translations.idiomatic: East of the kingdom stood Mount Yuximan, yielding gold, jade, and abundant iron.

sentences.zh: 悉萬斤國，都悉萬斤城，在迷密西，去代一萬二千七百二十里。

translations.literal: The state of Samarkand had its capital at Samarkand city, west of Mimi, twelve thousand seven hundred twenty li from Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Samarkand, capital at Samarkand city, west of Mimi, lay twelve thousand seven hundred twenty li from Dai.

sentences.zh: 其國南有山名伽色那山，出師子。

translations.literal: South of its state was a mountain called Mount Gaseina, which produced lions.
translations.idiomatic: South of the kingdom stood Mount Gaseina, home to lions.

sentences.zh: 每使朝貢。

translations.literal: Tribute envoys were sent every year.
translations.idiomatic: It sent tribute envoys every year.

sentences.zh: 忸密國，都忸密城，在悉萬斤西，去代二萬二千八百二十八里。

translations.literal: The state of Wumi had its capital at Wumi city, west of Samarkand, twenty-two thousand eight hundred twenty-eight li from Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Wumi, capital at Wumi city, west of Samarkand, lay twenty-two thousand eight hundred twenty-eight li from Dai.

sentences.zh: 破洛那國，故大宛國也。

translations.literal: The state of Bactria was formerly the state of Dayuan.
translations.idiomatic: Bactria was the old kingdom of Dayuan.

sentences.zh: 都貴山城，在疏勒西北，去代萬四千四百五十里。

translations.literal: Its capital was Guishan city, northwest of Kashgar, fourteen thousand four hundred fifty li from Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Its capital was Guishan city, northwest of Kashgar, fourteen thousand four hundred fifty li from Dai.

sentences.zh: 太和三年，遣使獻汗血馬，自此每使朝貢。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taihe, they sent envoys presenting blood-sweating horses; from then on tribute was sent every year.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe 3 they sent envoys with blood-sweating horses; thereafter they sent tribute every year.

sentences.zh: 粟特國，在蔥嶺之西，古之奄蔡，一名溫那沙，居於大澤，在康居西北，去代一萬六千里。

translations.literal: The state of Sogdiana lay west of the Pamirs; it was ancient Yancai, also called Wunasha, dwelling in a great marsh northwest of Kangju, sixteen thousand li from Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Sogdiana lay west of the Pamirs; ancient Yancai, also called Wunasha, it dwelt in a great marsh northwest of Kangju, sixteen thousand li from Dai.

sentences.zh: 先是，匈奴殺其王而有其國，至王忽倪，已三世矣。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Xiongnu had killed its king and seized the state; by King Huní, this had already lasted three generations.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Xiongnu had killed its king and taken the kingdom; by the reign of King Huní, this had already lasted three generations.

sentences.zh: 其國商人先多詣涼土販貨，及魏克姑臧，悉見虜。

translations.literal: Its merchants had formerly gone in great numbers to Liang territory to trade, and when Wei captured Guzang they were all taken captive.
translations.idiomatic: Its merchants had long traded in Liang territory, and when Wei captured Guzang they were all taken captive.

sentences.zh: 文成初，粟特王遣使請贖之，詔聽焉。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Wencheng's reign, the king of Sogdiana sent envoys requesting their ransom; an edict granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Wencheng's reign, the Sogdian king sent envoys to ransom them, and the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 自後無使朝獻。

translations.literal: After that no envoys came with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: After that no tribute envoys came.

sentences.zh: 周保定四年，其王遣使貢方物。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Baoding of Zhou, its king sent envoys presenting regional products.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhou Baoding 4 its king sent envoys with regional tribute.

sentences.zh: 波斯國，都宿利城，在忸密西，古條支國也。

translations.literal: The state of Persia had its capital at Suli city, west of Wumi; it was the ancient state of Taoxi.
translations.idiomatic: Persia, capital at Suli city, west of Wumi, was the ancient kingdom of Taoxi.

sentences.zh: 去代二萬四千二百二十八里。

translations.literal: Twenty-four thousand two hundred twenty-eight li from Dai.
translations.idiomatic: It lay twenty-four thousand two hundred twenty-eight li from Dai.

sentences.zh: 城方十里，戶十餘萬，河經其城中南流。

translations.literal: The city was ten li square, with more than one hundred thousand households; a river passed through the city flowing south.
translations.idiomatic: The capital measured ten li square and held over one hundred thousand households; a river ran through it southward.

sentences.zh: 土地平正，出金、銀、鍮石、珊瑚、琥珀、車渠、馬腦，多大真珠、頗梨、琉璃、水精、瑟瑟、金剛、火齊、鑌鐵、銅、錫、硃砂、水銀、綾、錦、疊、毼、氍毹、毾◄、赤麞皮、及薰六、郁金、蘇合、青木等香，胡椒、蓽撥、石蜜、千年棗、香附子、訶梨勒、無食子、鹽綠、雌黃等物。

translations.literal: The land was level, producing gold, silver, yu stone, coral, amber, tridacna, agate, and much fine pearl, crystal glass, lapis lazuli, rock crystal, sapphires, diamond, carnelian, wootz steel, copper, tin, cinnabar, mercury, gauze, brocade, layered silk, felt, rugs, carpets, red deer hide, and aromatics such as asafetida, turmeric, storax, and eaglewood, plus pepper, long pepper, rock sugar, millennial jujubes, cyperus, myrobalan, gallnut, salt green, and orpiment.
translations.idiomatic: Level ground yielded gold, silver, coral, amber, pearls, glass, lapis, crystal, sapphires, diamonds, wootz steel, copper, tin, cinnabar, mercury, silks, brocades, rugs, hides, and spices from asafetida and pepper to myrobalan and orpiment—goods almost without number.

sentences.zh: 氣候暑熱，家自藏冰。

translations.literal: The climate was sweltering; households kept ice in store.
translations.idiomatic: The climate was fiercely hot; families stored their own ice.

sentences.zh: 地多沙磧，引水溉灌。

translations.literal: Much of the land was sandy; water was led in for irrigation.
translations.idiomatic: Much of the soil was gravelly; irrigation depended on diverted water.

sentences.zh: 其五穀及鳥獸等與中夏略同，唯無稻及黍、稷。

translations.literal: Its five grains and birds and beasts were roughly the same as in Central China, except that it had no rice, glutinous millet, or millet.
translations.idiomatic: Its grains and wildlife resembled those of the Middle Kingdom, though it lacked rice, glutinous millet, and millet.

sentences.zh: 土出名馬、大驢及駝，往往有一日能行七百里者，富室至有數千頭。

translations.literal: The region produced famed horses, great donkeys, and camels; some could travel seven hundred li in a day, and wealthy households might own several thousand head.
translations.idiomatic: It bred famed horses, great donkeys, and camels—some covering seven hundred li in a day; rich households might own thousands.

sentences.zh: 又出白象、師子、大鳥卵。

translations.literal: It also produced white elephants, lions, and great birds' eggs.
translations.idiomatic: It also had white elephants, lions, and ostrich eggs.

sentences.zh: 有鳥形如橐駝，有兩翼，飛而不能高，食草與肉，亦能栎敢火。

translations.literal: There was a bird shaped like a Bactrian camel, with two wings; it could fly but not high, ate grass and meat, and was unafraid even of fire.
translations.idiomatic: There was a winged bird shaped like a camel that could fly only low, ate plants and meat, and was not afraid even of fire.

sentences.zh: 其王姓波氏名斯，坐金羊床，戴金花冠，衣錦袍、織成帔，飾以真珠寶物。

translations.literal: Its king, of the Bo clan named Si, sat on a golden ram throne, wore a golden floral crown, brocade robes and woven mantles, and was adorned with pearls and jewels.
translations.idiomatic: The king, surnamed Bo and named Si, sat on a golden ram throne, wore a golden floral crown, brocade robes and woven mantles, and was decked in pearls and jewels.

sentences.zh: 其俗：丈夫翦發，戴白皮帽，貫頭衫，兩箱近下開之，亦有巾帔，緣以織成；

translations.literal: Their custom: men cropped their hair, wore white felt caps and pull-over tunics open below the waist; some also wore scarves edged with woven trim;
translations.idiomatic: Custom: men cropped their hair, wore white felt caps and pull-over tunics slit low at the sides; some also wore scarves edged with woven trim;

sentences.zh: 婦女服大衫，披大帔，其發前為髻，後披之，飾以金銀花，仍貫五色珠，絡之於膊。

translations.literal: Women wore long gowns and great mantles; they looped the hair before into a bun and let it fall behind, adorned it with gold and silver flowers, and strung five-colored beads looped on the arms.
translations.idiomatic: Women wore long gowns and great mantles, hair looped before and loose behind, adorned with gold and silver flowers and strings of five-colored beads on the arms.

sentences.zh: 王於其國內別有小牙十餘所，猶中國之離宮也。

translations.literal: Within the kingdom the king maintained more than ten separate minor palaces, like the detached palaces of China.
translations.idiomatic: The king kept more than ten minor palaces within the realm, like the detached palaces of China.

sentences.zh: 每年四月出遊處之，十月仍還。

translations.literal: Each year in the fourth month he went out to tour them, returning in the tenth month.
translations.idiomatic: Each year in the fourth month he toured them, returning in the tenth month.

sentences.zh: 王即位以後，擇諸子內賢者，密書其名，封之于庫，諸子及大臣莫之知也。

translations.literal: After his accession the king would secretly write the name of whichever son he judged worthy, seal it in the treasury, and neither the princes nor the ministers knew of it.
translations.idiomatic: After accession the king secretly wrote the name of the worthiest son, sealed it in the treasury, and kept princes and ministers alike in ignorance.

sentences.zh: 王死，眾乃共發書視之，其封內有名者，即立以為王。

translations.literal: When the king died, the seal was opened; whichever name was inside was immediately established as king.
translations.idiomatic: When the king died the seal was opened, and whoever was named inside became king at once.

sentences.zh: 余子出各就邊任，兄弟更不相見也。

translations.literal: The remaining sons were sent out to frontier posts, and the brothers never saw one another again.
translations.idiomatic: The other sons were posted to the frontiers and never met again.

sentences.zh: 國人號王曰醫栎贊，妃曰防步率，王之諸子曰殺野。

translations.literal: The people called the king Yilizan, the queen Fangbulü, and the princes Shaye.
translations.idiomatic: The people called the king Yilizan, the queen Fangbulü, and the princes Shaye.

sentences.zh: 大官有摸胡壇，掌國內獄訟；

translations.literal: Among high officials was Mokhutan, who managed domestic lawsuits and punishments;
translations.idiomatic: High officials included Mokhutan, who oversaw lawsuits and punishments within the realm;

sentences.zh: 泥忽汗，掌庫藏、關禁；

translations.literal: Nihouhan managed the treasuries and frontier passes;
translations.idiomatic: Nihouhan managed treasuries and frontier passes;

sentences.zh: 地卑，掌文書及眾務。

translations.literal: Dibei managed documents and general affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Dibei managed documents and general affairs.

sentences.zh: 次有遏羅訶地，掌王之內事；

translations.literal: Next was Elagandi, who managed the king's inner household;
translations.idiomatic: Next came Elagandi, overseer of the king's inner household;

sentences.zh: 薛波勃，掌四方兵馬，其下皆有屬官，分統其事。

translations.literal: Xuebopo managed armies in the four directions; beneath them were subordinate officials who divided and governed the tasks.
translations.idiomatic: Xuebopo commanded armies in the four directions, with subordinate officials under each to divide the work.

sentences.zh: 兵有甲、槊、圓排、劍、弩、弓、箭。

translations.literal: Their troops had armor, spears, round shields, swords, crossbows, bows, and arrows.
translations.idiomatic: Their forces used armor, spears, round shields, swords, crossbows, bows, and arrows.

sentences.zh: 戰兼乘象，百人隨之。

translations.literal: In battle they also mounted elephants, each followed by a hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: In battle they also fought from elephants, each attended by a hundred men.

sentences.zh: 其刑法：重罪懸諸竿上，射殺之；

translations.literal: Their penal code: for grave crimes the offender was hung on a pole and shot to death;
translations.idiomatic: Penal law: for grave crimes the offender was hung on a pole and shot dead;

sentences.zh: 次則系獄，新王立，乃釋之；

translations.literal: lesser ones were imprisoned, and when a new king acceded they were released;
translations.idiomatic: lesser offenders were imprisoned and released when a new king acceded;

sentences.zh: 輕罪則劓、刖若髡，或翦半鬢及系牌于項，以為恥辱；

translations.literal: light crimes were punished by nose-cutting, foot-cutting, or head-shaving, or by clipping half the side-whiskers or hanging a placard on the neck as shame;
translations.idiomatic: light crimes brought nose-cutting, foot-cutting, head-shaving, clipping half the side-whiskers, or a placard hung on the neck as disgrace;

sentences.zh: 犯強盜，系之終身；

translations.literal: robbers were bound for life;
translations.idiomatic: robbers were bound for life;

sentences.zh: 奸貴人妻者，男子流，婦人割其耳鼻。

translations.literal: a man who seduced a noblewoman's wife was exiled, and the woman had her nose and ears cut off.
translations.idiomatic: a man who seduced a noblewoman's wife was exiled, and the woman had her nose and ears cut off.

sentences.zh: 賦稅，則准地輸銀錢。

translations.literal: Taxes were levied in silver coin according to land held.
translations.idiomatic: Taxes were paid in silver according to land.

sentences.zh: 俗事火神天神。

translations.literal: Their custom was to serve the fire god and the heavenly god.
translations.idiomatic: They worshipped the fire god and the heavenly god.

sentences.zh: 文字與胡書異。

translations.literal: Their writing differed from the scripts of the northern peoples.
translations.idiomatic: Their script differed from the writing of the northern peoples.

sentences.zh: 多以姊妹為妻妾，自餘婚合，亦不擇尊卑，諸夷之中最為醜穢矣。

translations.literal: Many took their sisters as wives and concubines; in other marriages too they paid no heed to rank—it was the most revolting custom among the western peoples.
translations.idiomatic: Men often married their sisters; other unions ignored rank as well—the most revolting custom among the western peoples.

sentences.zh: 百姓女年十歲以上有姿貌者，王收養之，有功勳人，即以分賜。

translations.literal: Common girls over ten who were comely were taken into the king's household; men of merit were then granted them as rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Comely common girls over ten were raised in the royal household and bestowed on men of merit.

sentences.zh: 死者，多棄屍於山，一月著服。

translations.literal: The dead were usually abandoned on the mountains; mourners wore funeral dress for one month.
translations.idiomatic: The dead were usually left on the mountains, and mourners wore funeral dress for one month.

sentences.zh: 城外有人別居，唯知喪葬之事，號為不淨人。

translations.literal: Outside the walls lived people set apart who handled funerals alone—they were called the Unclean.
translations.idiomatic: Outside the walls lived people set apart for funerals alone—they were called the Unclean.

sentences.zh: 若入城市，搖鈴自別。

translations.literal: When they entered the city they rang bells to announce themselves.
translations.idiomatic: When they entered the city they rang bells to distinguish themselves.

sentences.zh: 以六月為歲首，尤重七月七日、十二月一日。

translations.literal: They took the sixth month as New Year and especially observed the seventh day of the seventh month and the first day of the twelfth month.
translations.idiomatic: They began the year in the sixth month and especially observed the seventh day of the seventh month and the first day of the twelfth month.

sentences.zh: 其日，人庶以上，各相命召，設會作樂，以極歡娛。

translations.literal: On those days commoners and nobles summoned one another to feasts and music, reveling to the full.
translations.idiomatic: On those days nobles and commoners summoned one another to feasts and music, reveling to the utmost.

sentences.zh: 又每年正月二十日，各祭其先死者。

translations.literal: Each year on the twentieth day of the first month they sacrificed to their ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: Each year on the twentieth day of the first month they sacrificed to their ancestors.

sentences.zh: 神龜中，其國遣使上書貢物，云：「大國天子，天之所生，願日出處常為漢中天子。

translations.literal: In the Shengui era the kingdom sent envoys with tribute and a letter saying, "Son of Heaven of the great state, born of Heaven—we pray that he at the place where the sun rises may forever be Son of Heaven of Han China.
translations.idiomatic: In the Shengui era the kingdom sent envoys with tribute and a letter saying, "Son of Heaven of the great state, born of Heaven—we pray that he where the sun rises may forever be Son of Heaven of Han China.

sentences.zh: 波斯國王居和多千萬敬拜。」

translations.literal: The king of Persia, Jvheduo Qianwan, pays reverent homage.
translations.idiomatic: The king of Persia, Jvheduo Qianwan, pays reverent homage.

sentences.zh: 朝廷嘉納之。

translations.literal: The court graciously accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: The court graciously accepted the tribute.

sentences.zh: 自此，每使朝獻。

translations.literal: From then on tribute envoys came every year.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter tribute envoys came every year.

sentences.zh: 恭帝二年，其王又遣使獻方物。

translations.literal: In the second year of Emperor Gong its king again sent envoys with regional tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Gong 2 its king again sent envoys with regional tribute.

sentences.zh: 隋煬帝時，遣雲騎尉李昱使通波斯。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Yang of Sui, Cloud Cavalry Commandant Li Yu was sent as envoy to Persia.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Yang of Sui, Cloud Cavalry Commandant Li Yu was dispatched to Persia.

sentences.zh: 尋使隨昱貢方物。

translations.literal: Persian envoys soon followed Yu with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Persian envoys soon followed Yu with regional tribute.

sentences.zh: 伏盧尼國，都伏盧尼城，在波斯國北，去代二萬七千三百二十里。

translations.literal: The state of Volunni had its capital at Volunni city, north of Persia, twenty-seven thousand three hundred twenty li from Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Volunni, capital at Volunni city, north of Persia, lay twenty-seven thousand three hundred twenty li from Dai.

sentences.zh: 累石為城，東有大河南流，中有鳥，其形似人，亦有如橐駝、馬者，皆有翼，常居水中，出水便死。

translations.literal: Its walls were piled stone; east of it a great river flowed south. In the river were birds shaped like men, and also like camels and horses; all had wings, dwelt in the water, and died as soon as they left it.
translations.idiomatic: Its walls were piled stone; east of it a great river flowed south. In the river were winged birds shaped like men, camels, and horses that lived in the water and died once they left it.

sentences.zh: 城北有雲尼山，出銀、珊瑚、琥珀，多師子。

translations.literal: North of the city was Mount Yunni, which produced silver, coral, and amber, and had many lions.
translations.idiomatic: North of the city stood Mount Yunni, source of silver, coral, and amber and home to many lions.

sentences.zh: 色知顯國，都色知顯城，在悉萬斤西北，去代一萬二千九百四十里。

translations.literal: The state of Sezhixian had its capital at Sezhixian city, northwest of Samarkand, twelve thousand nine hundred forty li from Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Sezhixian, capital at Sezhixian city, northwest of Samarkand, lay twelve thousand nine hundred forty li from Dai.

sentences.zh: 土平，多五果。

translations.literal: The land was level and produced many fruits.
translations.idiomatic: The land was level and rich in fruit.

sentences.zh: 伽色尼國，都伽色尼城，在悉萬斤南，去代一萬二千九百里。

translations.literal: The state of Gaseini had its capital at Gaseini city, south of Samarkand, twelve thousand nine hundred li from Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Gaseini, capital at Gaseini city, south of Samarkand, lay twelve thousand nine hundred li from Dai.

sentences.zh: 土出赤鹽，多五果。

translations.literal: The soil produced red salt and many fruits.
translations.idiomatic: The soil yielded red salt and abundant fruit.

sentences.zh: 薄知國，都薄知城，在伽色尼國南，去代一萬三千三百二十里。

translations.literal: The state of Bozhi had its capital at Bozhi city, south of Gaseini, thirteen thousand three hundred twenty li from Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Bozhi, capital at Bozhi city, south of Gaseini, lay thirteen thousand three hundred twenty li from Dai.

sentences.zh: 多五果。

translations.literal: It had many fruits.
translations.idiomatic: It had abundant fruit.

sentences.zh: 牟知國，都牟知城，在忸密西南，去代二萬二千九百二十里。

translations.literal: The state of Mouzhi had its capital at Mouzhi city, southwest of Wumi, twenty-two thousand nine hundred twenty li from Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Mouzhi, capital at Mouzhi city, southwest of Wumi, lay twenty-two thousand nine hundred twenty li from Dai.

sentences.zh: 土平，禽獸草木類中國。

translations.literal: The land was level; its birds, beasts, and plants resembled those of China.
translations.idiomatic: The land was level; birds, beasts, and plants resembled those of China.

sentences.zh: 阿弗太汗國，都阿弗太汗城，在忸密西，去代二萬三千七百二十里。

translations.literal: The state of Afutaihan had its capital at Afutaihan city, west of Wumi, twenty-three thousand seven hundred twenty li from Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Afutaihan, capital at Afutaihan city, west of Wumi, lay twenty-three thousand seven hundred twenty li from Dai.

sentences.zh: 土平，多五果。

translations.literal: The land was level and produced many fruits.
translations.idiomatic: The land was level and rich in fruit.

sentences.zh: 呼似密國，都呼似密城，在阿弗太汗西，去代二萬四千七百里。

translations.literal: The state of Husimi had its capital at Husimi city, west of Afutaihan, twenty-four thousand seven hundred li from Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Husimi, capital at Husimi city, west of Afutaihan, lay twenty-four thousand seven hundred li from Dai.

sentences.zh: 土平，出銀、琥珀，有師子，多五果。

translations.literal: The land was level, producing silver and amber; it had lions and many fruits.
translations.idiomatic: The land was level, yielding silver and amber; it had lions and abundant fruit.

sentences.zh: 諾色波羅國，都波羅城，在忸密南，去代二萬三千四百二十八里。

translations.literal: The state of Nuoseboluo had its capital at Boluo city, south of Wumi, twenty-three thousand four hundred twenty-eight li from Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Nuoseboluo, capital at Boluo city, south of Wumi, lay twenty-three thousand four hundred twenty-eight li from Dai.

sentences.zh: 土平，宜稻、麥，多五果。

translations.literal: The land was level, suited to rice and wheat, and had many fruits.
translations.idiomatic: The land was level, suited to rice and wheat, and rich in fruit.

sentences.zh: 早伽至國，都早伽至成，在忸密西，去代二萬三千七百二十八里。

translations.literal: The state of Zaogazhi had its capital at Zaogazhi Cheng, west of Wumi, twenty-three thousand seven hundred twenty-eight li from Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Zaogazhi, capital at Zaogazhi Cheng, west of Wumi, lay twenty-three thousand seven hundred twenty-eight li from Dai.

sentences.zh: 土平，少田殖，取稻、麥於鄰國，有五果。

translations.literal: The land was level, with little cultivation; it obtained rice and wheat from neighboring states and had five kinds of fruit.
translations.idiomatic: The land was level but poorly cultivated; rice and wheat came from neighboring states, and it had five kinds of fruit.

sentences.zh: 伽不單國，都伽不單城，在悉萬斤西北，去代一萬二千七百八十里。

translations.literal: The state of Jiabudan had its capital at Jiabudan city, northwest of Samarkand, twelve thousand seven hundred eighty li from Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Jiabudan, capital at Jiabudan city, northwest of Samarkand, lay twelve thousand seven hundred eighty li from Dai.

sentences.zh: 土平，宜稻、麥，有五果。

translations.literal: The land was level, suited to rice and wheat, and had five kinds of fruit.
translations.idiomatic: The land was level, suited to rice and wheat, and had five kinds of fruit.

sentences.zh: 者舌國，故康居國，在破洛那西北，去代一萬五千四百五十里。

translations.literal: The state of Zheshe was the old state of Kangju, northwest of Bactria, fifteen thousand four hundred fifty li from Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Zheshe, the old kingdom of Kangju, northwest of Bactria, lay fifteen thousand four hundred fifty li from Dai.

sentences.zh: 太延三年，遣使朝貢，不絕。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taiyan envoys came with tribute, and this did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiyan 3 envoys came with tribute, and the missions did not cease.

sentences.zh: 伽倍國，故休密翕侯，都和墨城，在莎車西，去代一萬三千里。

translations.literal: The state of Jiabei was the old Xiumi xihou; its capital was Hemocheng, west of Yarkand, thirteen thousand li from Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Jiabei, the old Xiumi xihou, capital at Hemocheng west of Yarkand, lay thirteen thousand li from Dai.

sentences.zh: 人居山谷間。

translations.literal: The people dwelt among mountain valleys.
translations.idiomatic: Its people lived in mountain valleys.

sentences.zh: 折薛莫孫國，故雙靡翕侯，都雙靡城，在伽倍西，去代一萬三千五百里。

translations.literal: The state of Zhexiesun was the old Shuangmi xihou; its capital was Shuangmi city, west of Jiabei, thirteen thousand five hundred li from Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Zhexiesun, the old Shuangmi xihou, capital at Shuangmi city west of Jiabei, lay thirteen thousand five hundred li from Dai.

sentences.zh: 居山谷間。

translations.literal: They dwelt among mountain valleys.
translations.idiomatic: They lived in mountain valleys.

sentences.zh: 鉗敦國，故貴霜翕侯，都護澡城，在折薛莫孫西，去代一萬三千五百六十里，居山谷間。

translations.literal: The state of Qiandun was the old Guishuang xihou; its capital was Huzao city, west of Zhexiesun, thirteen thousand five hundred sixty li from Dai; they dwelt among mountain valleys.
translations.idiomatic: Qiandun, the old Guishuang xihou, capital at Huzao city west of Zhexiesun, thirteen thousand five hundred sixty li from Dai, lived in mountain valleys.

sentences.zh: 弗敵沙國，故肹頓翕侯，都薄茅城，在鉗敦西，去代一萬三千六百六十里。

translations.literal: The state of Fudisha was the old Xidun xihou; its capital was Baomao city, west of Qiandun, thirteen thousand six hundred sixty li from Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Fudisha, the old Xidun xihou, capital at Baomao city west of Qiandun, lay thirteen thousand six hundred sixty li from Dai.

sentences.zh: 居山谷間。

translations.literal: They dwelt among mountain valleys.
translations.idiomatic: They lived in mountain valleys.

sentences.zh: 閻浮謁國，故高附翕侯，都高附城，在弗敵沙南，去代一萬三千七百六十里。

translations.literal: The state of Yanfuye was the old Gaofu xihou; its capital was Gaofu city, south of Fudisha, thirteen thousand seven hundred sixty li from Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Yanfuye, the old Gaofu xihou, capital at Gaofu city south of Fudisha, lay thirteen thousand seven hundred sixty li from Dai.

sentences.zh: 居山谷間。

translations.literal: They dwelt among mountain valleys.
translations.idiomatic: They lived in mountain valleys.

sentences.zh: 大月氏國，都剩鹽氏城，在弗敵沙西，去代一萬四千五百里。

translations.literal: The state of the Great Yuezhi had its capital at Shengyanshi city, west of Fudisha, fourteen thousand five hundred li from Dai.
translations.idiomatic: The Great Yuezhi, capital at Shengyanshi city west of Fudisha, lay fourteen thousand five hundred li from Dai.

sentences.zh: 北與蠕蠕接，數為所侵，遂西徙都薄羅城，去弗敵沙二千一百里。

translations.literal: It bordered the Rouran on the north and was repeatedly invaded by them; it therefore moved west and established its capital at Boluo city, two thousand one hundred li from Fudisha.
translations.idiomatic: Bordering the Rouran on the north, it was repeatedly invaded and moved west to Boluo city, two thousand one hundred li from Fudisha.

sentences.zh: 其王寄多羅勇武，遂興師越大山，南侵北天竺。

translations.literal: Its king Jiduoluo was brave and martial; he raised an army, crossed the great mountains, and invaded northern India to the south.
translations.idiomatic: King Jiduoluo, brave and martial, marched over the great mountains and invaded northern India.

sentences.zh: 自乾陀羅以北五國，盡役屬之。

translations.literal: From Gandhara northward, five states were wholly brought under his service and submission.
translations.idiomatic: From Gandhara northward, five states were wholly subjugated.

sentences.zh: 太武時，其國人商販京師，自雲能鑄石為五色琉璃。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Taiwu, merchants of that country in the capital said they could cast stone into five-colored glass.
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Taiwu's reign, its merchants at the capital claimed they could cast stone into five-colored glass.

sentences.zh: 於是採礦山中，于京師鑄之，既成，光澤乃美於西方來者。

translations.literal: Ore was taken from the mountains and cast in the capital; when finished, its luster was finer than glass brought from the west.
translations.idiomatic: Ore was mined in the mountains and cast at the capital; the finished glass outshone western imports.

sentences.zh: 乃詔為行殿，容百餘人，光色映徹，觀者見之，莫不驚駭，以為神明所作。

translations.literal: An edict then made it into a traveling hall holding more than a hundred men; its light shone through, and viewers were all astonished, thinking it the work of spirits.
translations.idiomatic: An edict had it made into a traveling hall for more than a hundred men; light streamed through it, and onlookers were awestruck, deeming it divine work.

sentences.zh: 自此，國中琉璃遂賤，人不復珍之。

translations.literal: From then on glass in the realm became cheap, and people no longer prized it.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter glass in the realm grew cheap and was no longer prized.

sentences.zh: 安息國，在蔥嶺西，都蔚搜城。

translations.literal: The state of Parthia lay west of the Pamirs, with its capital at Weisou city.
translations.idiomatic: Parthia lay west of the Pamirs, capital at Weisou city.

sentences.zh: 北與康居，西與波斯相接，在大月氏西北，去代二萬一千五百里。

translations.literal: It bordered Kangju on the north and Persia on the west, northwest of the Great Yuezhi, twenty-one thousand five hundred li from Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Bordering Kangju on the north and Persia on the west, northwest of the Great Yuezhi, it lay twenty-one thousand five hundred li from Dai.

sentences.zh: 周天和二年，其王遣使朝獻。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianhe of Zhou its king sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhou Tianhe 2 its king sent envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 條支國，在安息西，去代二萬九千四百里。

translations.literal: The state of Taoxi lay west of Parthia, twenty-nine thousand four hundred li from Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Taoxi lay west of Parthia, twenty-nine thousand four hundred li from Dai.

sentences.zh: 大秦國，一名黎軒，都安都城，從條支西渡海曲一萬里，去代三萬九千四百里。

translations.literal: The state of Daqin, also called Lixuan, had its capital at Andu city; from Taoxi one crossed the sea's bend ten thousand li westward, thirty-nine thousand four hundred li from Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Daqin, also called Lixuan, capital at Andu city, lay ten thousand li west across the sea's bend from Taoxi, thirty-nine thousand four hundred li from Dai.

sentences.zh: 其海滂出，猶渤海也，而東西與渤海相望，蓋自然之理。

translations.literal: Its sea swelled outward, like the Bohai Sea, yet east and west it faced the Bohai—as though by nature's own design.
translations.idiomatic: Its sea swelled outward like the Bohai, yet faced the Bohai east and west—as though by nature's design.

sentences.zh: 地方六千里，居兩海之間。

translations.literal: Its territory was six thousand li square, lying between two seas.
translations.idiomatic: Its territory measured six thousand li square, between two seas.

sentences.zh: 其地平正，人居星布。

translations.literal: The land was level; people's dwellings were scattered like stars.
translations.idiomatic: The land was level and settlements were scattered like stars.

sentences.zh: 其王都城分為五城，各方五里，周六十里。

translations.literal: The king's capital was divided into five cities, each five li square, sixty li in circumference.
translations.idiomatic: The royal capital was divided into five cities, each five li square, sixty li around.

sentences.zh: 王居中城，城置八臣，以主四方。

translations.literal: The king dwelt in the central city; eight ministers were placed in the city to govern the four directions.
translations.idiomatic: The king lived in the central city, with eight ministers placed there to govern the four directions.

sentences.zh: 而王城亦置八臣，分主四城。

translations.literal: The royal city also had eight ministers, each governing one of the four outer cities.
translations.idiomatic: The royal city also had eight ministers, each governing one outer city.

sentences.zh: 若謀國事及四方有不決者，則四城之臣，集議王所，王自聽之，然後施行。

translations.literal: When state affairs or matters in the four directions were unresolved, the ministers of the four cities assembled at the king's court; the king heard them himself and then carried out the decision.
translations.idiomatic: When state affairs or matters in the four directions were unresolved, ministers of the four cities met at court; the king heard them and then acted.

sentences.zh: 王三年一出觀風化。

translations.literal: Every three years the king went out to observe customs and transform the people.
translations.idiomatic: Every three years the king went out to observe the people's customs.

sentences.zh: 人有冤枉詣王訴訟者，當方之臣，小則讓責，大則黜退，令其舉賢人以代之。

translations.literal: When people had grievances and came before the king to plead their cases, the officials of that region, for minor matters received reprimand and blame, for major ones were dismissed and made to recommend worthy men to replace them.
translations.idiomatic: If anyone wronged came to the king to sue, the local officials, for lesser faults were reprimanded, for greater ones removed and told to recommend able men to take their place.

sentences.zh: 其人端正長大，衣服、車旗，擬儀中國，故外域謂之大秦。

translations.literal: Their people were upright and tall; clothing, chariots, and banners modeled the rites of China; hence the outer domains called them Great Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Their people were tall and well-formed; their dress, chariots, and banners mirrored Chinese ceremonial—and so the outer lands called them Daqin.

sentences.zh: 其土宜五穀、桑、麻，人務蠶、田。

translations.literal: Their soil suited the five grains, mulberry, and hemp; people devoted themselves to sericulture and fields.
translations.idiomatic: The land suited grain, mulberry, and hemp; the people worked at silkworms and farming.

sentences.zh: 多璆琳、琅玕、神龜、白馬硃鬣、明珠、夜光璧。

translations.literal: It had much fine jade, coral, divine tortoises, white horses with red manes, luminous pearls, and night-shining disks.
translations.idiomatic: It produced fine jades, coral, sacred tortoises, white horses with crimson manes, luminous pearls, and night-shining jade disks.

sentences.zh: 東南通交趾，又水道通益州永昌郡。

translations.literal: Southeast it linked to Jiaozhi; by water route it also reached Yongchang commandery in Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Southeast it connected with Jiaozhi; by waterways it also reached Yongchang commandery in Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 多出異物。

translations.literal: Many exotic goods came forth.
translations.idiomatic: Many exotic goods came from there.

sentences.zh: 大秦西海水之西有河，河西南流。

translations.literal: West of Daqin's Western Sea there was a river; the river flowed southwest.
translations.idiomatic: West of Daqin's Western Sea lay a river flowing southwest.

sentences.zh: 河西有南北山，山西有赤水，西有白玉山，玉山西有西王母山，玉為堂室云。

translations.literal: West of the river were north and south mountains; west of the mountains was Red Water; west was White Jade Mountain; west of White Jade Mountain was Queen Mother of the West Mountain—it is said jade formed halls and chambers.
translations.idiomatic: West of the river stood north and south mountains; beyond them lay the Red River, then White Jade Mountain, and beyond that Queen Mother of the West Mountain—where, it is said, jade formed halls and chambers.

sentences.zh: 從安息西界循海曲，亦至大秦，回萬餘里。

translations.literal: From Parthia's western border following the sea's curve, one also reached Daqin—a round trip of more than ten thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: From Parthia's western frontier, following the sea's curve, one could also reach Daqin—a journey of more than ten thousand li round trip.

sentences.zh: 于彼國觀日月星辰，無異中國，而前史云：條支西行百里，日入處，失之遠矣。

translations.literal: Observing sun, moon, and stars in that country, they were no different from China; yet earlier histories said: one hundred li west of Taoxi was where the sun sets—wide of the mark.
translations.idiomatic: Observed from that land, sun, moon, and stars were no different from China—yet earlier histories placed the sunset a hundred li west of Taoxi, far off the mark.

sentences.zh: 阿鉤羌國，在莎車西南，去代一萬三千里。

translations.literal: The state of Agou Qiang lay southwest of Shache, thirteen thousand li from Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Agou Qiang lay southwest of Shache, thirteen thousand li from Dai.

sentences.zh: 國西南有縣度山，其間四百里，中往往有棧道，下臨不測之深，人行以繩索相持而度，因以名之。

translations.literal: Southwest of the state was Mount Xiandu; four hundred li between them, and along the way there were often plank roads overhanging unfathomable depths; people crossed holding one another by rope—hence the name.
translations.idiomatic: Southwest of the state stood Mount Xiandu; across four hundred li between them plank roads often overhung unfathomable depths, and travelers crossed holding one another by rope—hence the name.

sentences.zh: 土有五穀、諸果。

translations.literal: The soil had the five grains and various fruits.
translations.idiomatic: The land yielded grain and many kinds of fruit.

sentences.zh: 市用錢為貨。

translations.literal: In markets they used coins as goods.
translations.idiomatic: Markets used coin as currency.

sentences.zh: 居止立宮室。

translations.literal: For dwelling they built palaces and chambers.
translations.idiomatic: They lived in built houses and palaces.

sentences.zh: 有兵器，土出金珠。

translations.literal: They had weapons; the soil produced gold and pearls.
translations.idiomatic: They had weapons; the land produced gold and pearls.

sentences.zh: 波路國，在阿鉤羌西北，去代一萬三千九百里。

translations.literal: The state of Bolu lay northwest of Agou Qiang, thirteen thousand nine hundred li from Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Bolu lay northwest of Agou Qiang, thirteen thousand nine hundred li from Dai.

sentences.zh: 其地濕熱，有蜀馬。

translations.literal: Its land was damp and hot; it had Shu horses.
translations.idiomatic: The land was humid and hot; it had Shu horses.

sentences.zh: 土平，物產國俗與阿鉤羌同類焉。

translations.literal: The land was level; products and national customs were of the same kind as Agou Qiang.
translations.idiomatic: The terrain was level; products and customs resembled those of Agou Qiang.

sentences.zh: 小月氏國，都富樓沙城，其王本大月氏王寄多羅子也。

translations.literal: The Lesser Yuezhi state had its capital at Fulusha city; its king was originally the son of the Great Yuezhi king Jiduoluo.
translations.idiomatic: The Lesser Yuezhi, capital at Fulusha, was ruled by a king who was originally the son of the Great Yuezhi king Jiduoluo.

sentences.zh: 寄多羅為匈奴所逐，西徙。

translations.literal: Jiduoluo was driven out by the Xiongnu and migrated west.
translations.idiomatic: Jiduoluo was driven out by the Xiongnu and moved west.

sentences.zh: 後令其子守此城，因號小月氏焉。

translations.literal: Later he had his son hold this city, and thus they were called Lesser Yuezhi.
translations.idiomatic: He later left his son to hold this city, and so they came to be called the Lesser Yuezhi.

sentences.zh: 在波路西南，去代一萬六千六百里。

translations.literal: It lay southwest of Bolu, sixteen thousand six hundred li from Dai.
translations.idiomatic: It lay southwest of Bolu, sixteen thousand six hundred li from Dai.

sentences.zh: 先居西平、張掖之間，被服頗與羌同。

translations.literal: They had earlier dwelt between Xiping and Zhangye; dress and adornment were quite like the Qiang.
translations.idiomatic: They had once lived between Xiping and Zhangye; their dress was much like the Qiang.

sentences.zh: 其俗以金銀錢為貨，隨畜牧移徙，亦類匈奴。

translations.literal: Their custom was to use gold and silver coins as currency; they moved with their herds, also resembling the Xiongnu.
translations.idiomatic: They used gold and silver coin as currency and moved with their herds, much like the Xiongnu.

sentences.zh: 其城東十里有佛塔，周三百五十步，高八十丈。

translations.literal: Ten li east of their city was a Buddhist pagoda, three hundred fifty paces in circumference, eighty zhang high.
translations.idiomatic: Ten li east of the city stood a Buddhist pagoda three hundred fifty paces around and eighty zhang high.

sentences.zh: 自佛塔初建計至武定八年，八百四十二年，年謂百丈佛圖也。

translations.literal: From the pagoda's first construction counted to the eighth year of Wuding, eight hundred forty-two years—they called it the hundred-zhang Buddhist stupa.
translations.idiomatic: From its first building to Wuding 8 was eight hundred forty-two years—they called it the hundred-zhang pagoda.

sentences.zh: 罽賓國，都善見城，在波路西南，去代一萬四千二百里。

translations.literal: The state of Jibin had its capital at Shanjian city, southwest of Bolu, fourteen thousand two hundred li from Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Jibin, capital at Shanjian, lay southwest of Bolu, fourteen thousand two hundred li from Dai.

sentences.zh: 居在四山中，其地東西八百里，南北三百里。

translations.literal: It lay among four mountains; its territory was eight hundred li east-west and three hundred li north-south.
translations.idiomatic: It sat among four mountains; its lands stretched eight hundred li east to west and three hundred li north to south.

sentences.zh: 地平，溫和，有苜蓿、雜草、奇木、檀、槐、梓、竹。

translations.literal: The land was level and mild; there were alfalfa, mixed grasses, rare trees, sandalwood, locust, catalpa, and bamboo.
translations.idiomatic: The terrain was level and mild, with alfalfa, mixed grasses, rare trees, sandalwood, locust, catalpa, and bamboo.

sentences.zh: 種五穀。

translations.literal: They planted the five grains.
translations.idiomatic: They cultivated grain.

sentences.zh: 糞園。

translations.literal: They manured gardens.
translations.idiomatic: They fertilized their gardens.

sentences.zh: 田地下濕，生稻。

translations.literal: The fields were low and damp; rice grew there.
translations.idiomatic: The fields were low and wet; rice grew there.

sentences.zh: 冬食生菜。

translations.literal: In winter they ate raw vegetables.
translations.idiomatic: In winter they ate fresh greens.

sentences.zh: 其人工巧，雕文刻鏤，織罽。

translations.literal: Their people were skilled and clever; they carved and inlaid designs and wove carpets.
translations.idiomatic: The people were clever with their hands, carving inlaid designs and weaving carpets.

sentences.zh: 有金、銀、銅、錫，以為器物。

translations.literal: They had gold, silver, copper, and tin, from which they made vessels.
translations.idiomatic: Gold, silver, copper, and tin were worked into utensils.

sentences.zh: 市用錢。

translations.literal: Markets used coins.
translations.idiomatic: Markets used coin.

sentences.zh: 他畜與諸國同。

translations.literal: Other livestock was the same as in other states.
translations.idiomatic: Other livestock resembled that of neighboring states.

sentences.zh: 每使朝獻。

translations.literal: They regularly sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: It sent tribute envoys regularly.

sentences.zh: 吐呼羅國，去代一萬二千里。

translations.literal: The state of Tuhuoluo was twelve thousand li from Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Tuhuoluo lay twelve thousand li from Dai.

sentences.zh: 東至范陽國，西至悉萬斤國，中間相去二千里；

translations.literal: East to Fanyang state, west to Xiwansijin state, two thousand li between them;
translations.idiomatic: East to Fanyang, west to Xiwansijin, two thousand li apart;

sentences.zh: 南至連山，不知名，北至波斯國，中間相去一萬里。

translations.literal: south to linked mountains of unknown name, north to Persia, ten thousand li between them.
translations.idiomatic: south to unnamed mountain ranges, north to Persia, ten thousand li apart.

sentences.zh: 薄提城周匝六十里，城南有西流大水，名漢樓河。

translations.literal: Boti city circled sixty li; south of the city was a great west-flowing river called the Hanlou River.
translations.idiomatic: Boti city ran sixty li around; south of it flowed a great river westward, the Hanlou River.

sentences.zh: 土宜五穀，有好馬、駝、騾。

translations.literal: The soil suited the five grains; it had good horses, camels, and mules.
translations.idiomatic: The land suited grain; it had fine horses, camels, and mules.

sentences.zh: 其王曾遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: Its king once sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Its king once sent tribute envoys.

sentences.zh: 副貨國，去代一萬七千里。

translations.literal: The state of Fuhe was seventeen thousand li from Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Fuhe lay seventeen thousand li from Dai.

sentences.zh: 東至阿富使且國，西至沒誰國，中間相去一千里；

translations.literal: East to Afushiqie state, west to Meishui state, one thousand li between them;
translations.idiomatic: East to Afushiqie, west to Meishui, one thousand li apart;

sentences.zh: 南有連山，不知名，北至奇沙國，相去一干五百里。

translations.literal: south were linked mountains of unknown name, north to Qisha state, fifteen hundred li apart.
translations.idiomatic: south lay unnamed mountain ranges, north to Qisha, fifteen hundred li apart.

sentences.zh: 國中有副貨城，周匝七十里。

translations.literal: In the state was Fuhe city, seventy li in circumference.
translations.idiomatic: Its capital, Fuhe city, ran seventy li around.

sentences.zh: 宜五穀、蒲桃，唯有馬、駝、騾。

translations.literal: Suited the five grains and grapes; it had only horses, camels, and mules.
translations.idiomatic: The land suited grain and grapes; livestock was limited to horses, camels, and mules.

sentences.zh: 國王有黃金殿，殿下有金駝七頭，各高三尺。

translations.literal: The king had a golden hall; beneath the hall were seven golden camels, each three chi high.
translations.idiomatic: The king had a golden hall with seven golden camels beneath it, each three chi high.

sentences.zh: 其王遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: Its king sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Its king sent tribute envoys.

sentences.zh: 南天竺國，去代三萬一千五百里。

translations.literal: South Tianzhu was thirty-one thousand five hundred li from Dai.
translations.idiomatic: South India lay thirty-one thousand five hundred li from Dai.

sentences.zh: 有伏醜城，周匝十里。

translations.literal: It had Fuchou city, ten li in circumference.
translations.idiomatic: It had Fuchou city, ten li around.

sentences.zh: 城中出摩尼珠、珊瑚。

translations.literal: The city produced mani pearls and coral.
translations.idiomatic: The city produced mani pearls and coral.

sentences.zh: 城東三百里有拔賴城，城中出黃金、白真檀、石蜜、蒲桃。

translations.literal: Three hundred li east of the city was Balai city; the city produced gold, white sandalwood, rock honey, and grapes.
translations.idiomatic: Three hundred li east stood Balai city, producing gold, white sandalwood, rock honey, and grapes.

sentences.zh: 土宜五穀。

translations.literal: The soil suited the five grains.
translations.idiomatic: The land suited grain.

sentences.zh: 宣武時，其國王婆羅化遣使獻駿馬、金、銀。

translations.literal: In Emperor Xuanwu's reign, King Poluohua sent envoys offering fine horses, gold, and silver.
