translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xuanwu, King Poluohua sent envoys with fine horses, gold, and silver.

sentences.zh: 自此，每使朝貢。

translations.literal: From then on, they regularly sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: From then on tribute envoys came regularly.

sentences.zh: 疊伏羅國，去代三萬一千里。

translations.literal: The state of Diefuluo was thirty-one thousand li from Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Diefuluo lay thirty-one thousand li from Dai.

sentences.zh: 國中有勿悉城，城北有鹽奇水，西流。

translations.literal: In the state was Wuxi city; north of the city was Yanqi water flowing west.
translations.idiomatic: It had Wuxi city; north of the city the Yanqi River flowed west.

sentences.zh: 有白象。

translations.literal: It had white elephants.
translations.idiomatic: It had white elephants.

sentences.zh: 並有阿末黎木，皮中織作布。

translations.literal: It also had amoli wood; from its bark they wove cloth in the middle layer.
translations.idiomatic: It also had amoli trees; cloth was woven from the bark.

sentences.zh: 土宜五穀。

translations.literal: The soil suited the five grains.
translations.idiomatic: The land suited grain.

sentences.zh: 宣武時，其國王伏陀末多遣使獻方物。

translations.literal: In Emperor Xuanwu's reign, King Fotuomoduo sent envoys offering local products.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xuanwu, King Fotuomoduo sent envoys with regional goods.

sentences.zh: 自是，每使朝貢。

translations.literal: From then on, they regularly sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter tribute envoys came regularly.

sentences.zh: 拔豆國，去代五萬一千里。

translations.literal: The state of Badou was fifty-one thousand li from Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Badou lay fifty-one thousand li from Dai.

sentences.zh: 東至多勿當國，西至旃那國，中間相去七百五十里；

translations.literal: East to Duowudang state, west to Zhana state, seven hundred fifty li between them;
translations.idiomatic: East to Duowudang, west to Zhana, seven hundred fifty li apart;

sentences.zh: 南至罽陵伽國，北至弗那伏且國，中間相去九百里。

translations.literal: south to Jilingjia state, north to Funafuqie state, nine hundred li between them.
translations.idiomatic: south to Jilingjia, north to Funafuqie, nine hundred li apart.

sentences.zh: 國中出金、銀、雜寶、白象、水牛、犛牛、蒲桃、五果，土宜五穀。

translations.literal: The state produced gold, silver, miscellaneous treasures, white elephants, water buffalo, yaks, grapes, and the five fruits; the soil suited the five grains.
translations.idiomatic: It produced gold, silver, assorted treasures, white elephants, water buffalo, yaks, grapes, and many fruits; the land also suited grain.

sentences.zh: 嚈噠國，大月氏之種類也，亦曰高車之別種。

translations.literal: The Yeda were of the Great Yuezhi kind; also called a separate branch of the Gaoche.
translations.idiomatic: The Yeda were kin to the Great Yuezhi, also reckoned a separate branch of the Gaoche.

sentences.zh: 其原出於塞北。

translations.literal: Their origin lay in the northern frontier beyond the passes.
translations.idiomatic: They originated north of the frontier passes.

sentences.zh: 自金山而南，在于闐之西，都烏滸水南二百餘里，去長安一萬一百里。

translations.literal: From Jin Mountain southward, west of Khotan, their capital stood two hundred-plus li south of Wuhu water, ten thousand one hundred li from Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: South from Jin Mountain, west of Khotan, their capital lay two hundred-odd li south of the Wuhu River, ten thousand one hundred li from Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 其王都拔底延城，蓋王舍城也。

translations.literal: The king's capital was Badiyan city—likely Rajagriha.
translations.idiomatic: The royal seat was Badiyan city—probably the old Wangshe (Rajagriha).

sentences.zh: 其城方十里餘，多寺塔，皆飾以金。

translations.literal: The city was slightly more than ten li square; many temples and pagodas, all adorned with gold.
translations.idiomatic: The city was a little over ten li square, with many temples and pagodas all gilded.

sentences.zh: 風俗與突厥略同。

translations.literal: Customs resembled the Turks somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: Customs roughly matched those of the Turks.

sentences.zh: 其俗，兄弟共一妻，夫無兄弟者，妻戴一角帽，若有兄弟者，依其多少之數更加帽角焉。

translations.literal: Their custom: brothers shared one wife; if a husband had no brothers, his wife wore a one-horned cap; if he had brothers, horns were added to the cap according to their number.
translations.idiomatic: Brothers shared one wife; a wife whose husband had no brothers wore a one-horned cap, and for each brother an additional horn was added.

sentences.zh: 衣服類加以纓絡，頭皆翦發。

translations.literal: Clothes were adorned with tassels and cords; all cut their hair short.
translations.idiomatic: Garments were trimmed with tassels and cords; hair was cut short.

sentences.zh: 其語與蠕蠕、高車及諸胡不同。

translations.literal: Their language differed from Rouran, Gaoche, and the various Hu peoples.
translations.idiomatic: Their language differed from Rouran, Gaoche, and the other Hu peoples.

sentences.zh: 眾可有十萬，無城邑，依隨水草，以氈為屋，夏遷涼土，冬逐暖處，分其諸妻，各在別所，相去或二百、三百里。

translations.literal: Their multitude could reach one hundred thousand; they had no walled towns, followed water and pasture, used felt for dwellings; in summer they moved to cool soil, in winter to warm places; their many wives were distributed, each at a separate place, sometimes two or three hundred li apart.
translations.idiomatic: They numbered perhaps one hundred thousand, with no walled towns; they followed pasture and water, lived in felt tents, moved to cool lands in summer and warm ones in winter, and kept their wives at separate camps sometimes two or three hundred li apart.

sentences.zh: 其王巡曆而行，每月一處。

translations.literal: The king traveled in circuit, one place each month.
translations.idiomatic: The king moved in circuit, one camp each month.

sentences.zh: 冬寒之時，三月不徙。

translations.literal: In the cold of winter, three months without moving.
translations.idiomatic: In the depth of winter they did not move for three months.

sentences.zh: 王位不必傳子，子弟堪者，死便受之。

translations.literal: Kingship need not pass to a son; whichever kinsman was capable received it when the ruler died.
translations.idiomatic: The throne did not have to pass to a son; when the ruler died, whichever kinsman was fit took it.

sentences.zh: 其國無車，有輿，多駝、馬。

translations.literal: The state had no chariots; it had litters; many camels and horses.
translations.idiomatic: They had no chariots, only litters, and many camels and horses.

sentences.zh: 用刑嚴急，偷盜無多少，皆腰斬，盜一責十。

translations.literal: Punishments were harsh and swift; theft regardless of amount—all cut at the waist; steal one, repay ten.
translations.idiomatic: Justice was severe: any theft, however small, meant execution by cutting at the waist; steal one, repay ten.

sentences.zh: 死者，富家累石為藏，貧者掘地而埋，隨身諸物，皆置塚內。

translations.literal: For the dead, the rich piled stones for a tomb; the poor dug earth to bury; all personal goods were placed inside the mound.
translations.idiomatic: The wealthy piled stone tombs; the poor dug earth graves; all belongings went into the mound with the dead.

sentences.zh: 其人凶悍，能鬥戰，西域康居、于闐、沙勒、安息及諸小國三十許，皆役屬之，號為大國。

translations.literal: Their people were fierce and able in battle; Kangju, Khotan, Shule, Parthia, and some thirty small states of the Western Regions all served them—they were called a great power.
translations.idiomatic: They were fierce fighters; Kangju, Khotan, Shule, Parthia, and some thirty small Western Region states all served them—their realm was reckoned a great power.

sentences.zh: 與蠕蠕婚姻。

translations.literal: They intermarried with the Rouran.
translations.idiomatic: They intermarried with the Rouran.

sentences.zh: 自太安以後，每遣使朝貢，正光末，遣貢師子一，至高平，遇万俟醜奴反，因留之。

translations.literal: From Tai'an onward they regularly sent tribute envoys; at the end of Zhenguang they sent a lion as tribute; reaching Gaoping they met Moqi Chounu's rebellion and it was detained there.
translations.idiomatic: From Tai'an they sent tribute envoys regularly; at the end of Zhenguang they sent a lion as tribute, but at Gaoping it was detained when Moqi Chounu rebelled.

sentences.zh: 醜奴平，送京師。

translations.literal: When Chounu was pacified, it was sent to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: After Chounu was subdued, the lion was sent to the capital.

sentences.zh: 永熙以後，朝獻遂絕。

translations.literal: After Yongxi, tribute missions ceased.
translations.idiomatic: After Yongxi, tribute ceased.

sentences.zh: 至大統十二年，遣使獻其方物。

translations.literal: By the twelfth year of Datong, they sent envoys offering local products.
translations.idiomatic: In Datong 12 they sent envoys with regional goods.

sentences.zh: 廢帝二年、周明帝二年，並遣使來獻。

translations.literal: In Feidi year 2 and Zhou Mingdi year 2, both sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In Feidi 2 and Zhou Mingdi 2 they both sent tribute envoys.

sentences.zh: 後為突厥所破，部落分散，職貢遂絕。

translations.literal: Later broken by the Turks, tribes scattered, official tribute ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Turks broke them; the tribes scattered and formal tribute stopped.

sentences.zh: 至隋大業中，又遣使朝貢方物。

translations.literal: By the Sui Daye period, they again sent envoys with tribute goods.
translations.idiomatic: In the Sui Daye reign they again sent tribute envoys.

sentences.zh: 其國去漕國千五百里，東去瓜州六千五百里。

translations.literal: Their state was fifteen hundred li from Caoguo, sixty-five hundred li east from Guazhou.
translations.idiomatic: The realm lay fifteen hundred li from Caoguo and sixty-five hundred li east of Guazhou.

sentences.zh: 初，熙平中，明帝遣剩伏子統宋雲、沙門法力等使西域，訪求佛經，時有沙門慧生者，亦與俱行。

translations.literal: Initially, in the Xiping era, Emperor Ming sent the Shengfuzi Song Yun, the monk Fali, and others as envoys to the Western Regions seeking Buddhist scriptures; at the time the monk Hu Sheng also went along.
translations.idiomatic: At first, in the Xiping era, Emperor Ming sent Song Yun, bearer of the shengfu credential, the monk Fali, and others to the Western Regions to seek Buddhist scriptures; the monk Hu Sheng traveled with them.

sentences.zh: 正光中，還。

translations.literal: In the Zhenguang era, they returned.
translations.idiomatic: They returned in the Zhenguang era.

sentences.zh: 慧生所經諸國，不能知其本末及山川里數，獸舉其略云。

translations.literal: As for the states Hu Sheng passed through, one cannot know their origins or the measures of mountains and rivers; only a summary is set forth below.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Sheng could not determine the origins or distances of the lands he crossed; what follows is only a brief account.

sentences.zh: 硃居國，在于闐西。

translations.literal: The state of Zhuju lay west of Khotan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuju lay west of Khotan.

sentences.zh: 其人山居，有麥，多林果。

translations.literal: Their people lived in the mountains; they had wheat and many forest fruits.
translations.idiomatic: The people lived in the mountains; they had wheat and abundant orchard fruit.

sentences.zh: 咸事佛，語與于闐相類，役屬嚈噠。

translations.literal: They all served the Buddha; their language was much like Khotan's, and they were subject to the Yeda.
translations.idiomatic: They all followed Buddhism; their speech resembled Khotan's, and they were subject to the Yeda.

sentences.zh: 渴盤陀國，在蔥嶺東，硃駒波西。

translations.literal: The state of Kepantuo lay east of the Onion Range, west of Zhujubo.
translations.idiomatic: Kepantuo lay east of the Pamirs, west of Zhujubo.

sentences.zh: 河經其國東北流，有高山，夏積霜雪。

translations.literal: A river passed northeast through their land; there were high mountains where frost and snow accumulated even in summer.
translations.idiomatic: A river ran northeast through their country; high mountains there kept frost and snow even in summer.

sentences.zh: 亦事佛道，附於嚈噠。

translations.literal: They also served the Buddha and were attached to the Yeda.
translations.idiomatic: They too followed Buddhism and were subject to the Yeda.

sentences.zh: 缽和國，在渴盤陀西。

translations.literal: The state of Bohe lay west of Kepantuo.
translations.idiomatic: Bohe lay west of Kepantuo.

sentences.zh: 其土尤寒，人畜同居，穴地而處。

translations.literal: Its land was extremely cold; people and livestock lived together, dwelling in excavated underground chambers.
translations.idiomatic: The land was bitterly cold; people and livestock shared dwellings, living in dug-out chambers.

sentences.zh: 又有大雪山，望若銀峰。

translations.literal: There was also a great snow mountain that looked like a silver peak.
translations.idiomatic: There was also a great snow mountain that appeared like a silver peak.

sentences.zh: 其人唯食餅面，飲麥酒，服氈裘。

translations.literal: The people ate only flatbread and noodles and drank wheat ale; they wore felt cloaks.
translations.idiomatic: The people ate only flatbread and noodles, drank wheat ale, and wore felt cloaks.

sentences.zh: 有二道，一道西行向嚈噠，一道西南趣烏萇。

translations.literal: There were two routes: one west toward the Yeda, one southwest toward Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: Two roads led out: one west toward the Yeda, one southwest toward Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 亦為嚈噠所統。

translations.literal: They too were ruled by the Yeda.
translations.idiomatic: They too were subject to the Yeda.

sentences.zh: 波知國，在缽和西南。

translations.literal: The state of Bozhi lay southwest of Bohe.
translations.idiomatic: Bozhi lay southwest of Bohe.

sentences.zh: 土狹人貧，依託山谷，其王不能總攝。

translations.literal: The land was narrow and the people poor; relying on mountain valleys, their king could not hold full authority.
translations.idiomatic: The land was cramped and the people poor; clinging to mountain valleys, their king could not govern effectively.

sentences.zh: 有三池，傳云大池有龍，次者有龍婦，小者有龍子，行人經之，設祭乃得過，不祭，多遇風雪之困。

translations.literal: There were three pools; tradition said the great pool had a dragon, the next a dragon's mate, and the smallest a dragon's son. Travelers who passed offered sacrifice and then could cross; if they did not, they often met with wind and snow hardship.
translations.idiomatic: There were three pools; tradition held that the largest held a dragon, the next a dragon's mate, and the smallest a dragon's son. Travelers who passed made offerings and then could cross; without offerings, they often met wind and snow hardship.

sentences.zh: 賒彌國，在波知之南。

translations.literal: The state of Shemi lay south of Bozhi.
translations.idiomatic: Shemi lay south of Bozhi.

sentences.zh: 山居，不信佛法，專事諸神。

translations.literal: Mountain-dwellers, they did not believe in the Buddhist Law but devoted themselves exclusively to various spirits.
translations.idiomatic: They lived in the mountains, rejected Buddhism, and served various spirits exclusively.

sentences.zh: 亦附嚈噠。

translations.literal: They too were attached to the Yeda.
translations.idiomatic: They too were subject to the Yeda.

sentences.zh: 東有缽盧勒國，路險，緣鐵鎖而度，不下見底。

translations.literal: East was the state of Bolule; the road was perilous, and one crossed by iron chains without seeing the bottom below.
translations.idiomatic: To the east lay Bolule; the route was perilous, crossed by iron chains with the depths invisible below.

sentences.zh: 熙平中，宋雲等竟不能達。

translations.literal: In the Xiping era, Song Yun and the others ultimately could not reach it.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xiping era, Song Yun and his party could not reach it at all.

sentences.zh: 烏萇國，在賒彌南。

translations.literal: The state of Wuchang lay south of Shemi.
translations.idiomatic: Wuchang lay south of Shemi.

sentences.zh: 北有蔥嶺，南至天竺。

translations.literal: North was the Onion Range; south reached India.
translations.idiomatic: North lay the Pamirs; south reached India.

sentences.zh: 婆羅門胡為其上族。

translations.literal: Brahmin foreigners formed the upper stratum.
translations.idiomatic: Brahmin foreigners formed the ruling elite.

sentences.zh: 婆羅門多解天文吉凶之數，其王動則訪決焉。

translations.literal: Many Brahmins understood the reckoning of celestial signs and fortune and misfortune; when the king acted, he consulted them for decisions.
translations.idiomatic: Many Brahmins understood astronomy and the calculation of fortune and misfortune; when the king acted, he consulted them.

sentences.zh: 土多林果，引水灌田，豐稻、麥。

translations.literal: The land had many forest fruits; they channeled water to irrigate fields and had abundant rice and wheat.
translations.idiomatic: The land had many orchard fruits; they irrigated the fields and had abundant rice and wheat.

sentences.zh: 事佛，多諸寺塔，極華麗。

translations.literal: They served the Buddha; there were many monasteries and pagodas, extremely splendid.
translations.idiomatic: They followed Buddhism; monasteries and pagodas were numerous and exceedingly splendid.

sentences.zh: 人有爭訴，服之以藥，曲者發狂，直者無恙。

translations.literal: When people had disputes, they were made to take medicine: the guilty went mad, the innocent were unharmed.
translations.idiomatic: In disputes, both parties took medicine: the guilty went mad, the innocent suffered no harm.

sentences.zh: 為法不殺，犯死罪唯徙於靈山。

translations.literal: By law they did not kill; those guilty of capital crimes were only exiled to Spirit Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Their law forbade killing; capital offenders were merely exiled to Spirit Mountain.

sentences.zh: 西南有檀特山，山上立寺，以驢數頭運食山下，無人控禦，自知往來也。

translations.literal: Southwest was Mount Tante; a monastery stood on the mountain, and several donkeys carried food down the mountain with no one driving them—they came and went of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Southwest stood Mount Tante, with a monastery on its summit; donkeys carried food down the slope with no driver—they moved of their own accord.

sentences.zh: 乾陀國，在烏萇西。

translations.literal: The state of Gandhara lay west of Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: Gandhara lay west of Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 本名業波，為嚈噠所破，因改焉。

translations.literal: Originally named Yabo, it was broken by the Yeda and therefore renamed.
translations.idiomatic: Originally called Yabo, it was broken by the Yeda and renamed accordingly.

sentences.zh: 其王本是敕勒，臨國已二世矣。

translations.literal: Its king was originally of the Chile; he had already ruled the state for two generations.
translations.idiomatic: Its king was originally of the Chile people and had already ruled for two generations.

sentences.zh: 好征戰，與罽賓鬥，三年不罷，人怨苦之。

translations.literal: Fond of campaigning, he fought with Jibin for three years without cease, and the people resented and suffered from it.
translations.idiomatic: He loved warfare and fought Jibin for three years without pause; the people resented and suffered for it.

sentences.zh: 有鬥象七百頭，十人乘一象，皆執兵仗，象鼻縛刀以戰。

translations.literal: There were seven hundred war elephants; ten men rode each elephant, all bearing weapons, and knives were bound to the elephants' trunks for battle.
translations.idiomatic: He had seven hundred war elephants; ten men rode each, all armed, with blades bound to the elephants' trunks for combat.

sentences.zh: 所都城東南七里有佛塔，高七十丈，周三百步，即所謂雀離佛圖也。

translations.literal: Seven li southeast of the capital city was a Buddhist pagoda, seventy zhang high and three hundred paces around—the so-called Sparrow-Perch Buddha Stupa.
translations.idiomatic: Seven li southeast of the capital stood a Buddhist pagoda seventy zhang high and three hundred paces around—the so-called Sparrow-Perch Buddha Stupa.

sentences.zh: 康國者，康居之後也，遷徙無常，不恆故地，自漢以來，相承不絕。

translations.literal: Kang was the successor state of Kangju; they moved without fixed abode and did not long remain in one place—from Han times onward the line was unbroken.
translations.idiomatic: Kang was the successor to Kangju; they moved without fixed abode and seldom stayed in one place—from Han times the line continued unbroken.

sentences.zh: 其王本姓溫，月氏人也，舊居祁連山北昭武城，因被匈奴所破，西逾蔥嶺，遂有國。

translations.literal: The king's original surname was Wen; he was a Yuezhi man, formerly dwelling at Zhaowu city north of the Qilian Mountains; broken by the Xiongnu, he crossed west beyond the Onion Range and then had a state.
translations.idiomatic: The king's original surname was Wen; he was Yuezhi, formerly dwelling at Zhaowu city north of the Qilian Mountains; driven out by the Xiongnu, he crossed west beyond the Pamirs and founded a state.

sentences.zh: 枝庶各分王，故康國左右諸國並以昭武為姓，示不忘本也。

translations.literal: Cadet branches each ruled as kings in turn, so the states around Kang all took Zhaowu as surname, showing they did not forget their origins.
translations.idiomatic: Cadet branches each ruled in turn, so the states around Kang all bore the surname Zhaowu, showing they did not forget their origins.

sentences.zh: 王字世夫畢，為人寬厚，甚得眾心。

translations.literal: The king's personal name was Shifubi; as a man he was generous and greatly won the people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: The king, styled Shifubi, was generous and greatly won the people's hearts.

sentences.zh: 其妻，突厥達度可汗女也。

translations.literal: His wife was the daughter of the Turkic Tardu qaghan.
translations.idiomatic: His wife was a daughter of the Turkic qaghan Tardu.

sentences.zh: 都于薩寶水上阿祿迪城。

translations.literal: The capital was Aludi city on the Saba River.
translations.idiomatic: The capital was Aludi city on the Saba River.

sentences.zh: 多人居，大臣三人，共掌國事。

translations.literal: Many people lived there; three great ministers jointly governed state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The population was large; three great ministers jointly governed state affairs.

sentences.zh: 其王素冠七寶花，衣綾、羅、錦、繡、白疊。

translations.literal: The king customarily wore a crown of seven-jewel flowers and robes of gauze, silk, brocade, embroidery, and white layered cloth.
translations.idiomatic: The king customarily wore a seven-jewel flower crown and robes of gauze, silk, brocade, embroidery, and white layered cloth.

sentences.zh: 其妻有髮，幪以皁巾。

translations.literal: His wife had hair and covered it with a black kerchief.
translations.idiomatic: His wife wore her hair long and covered it with a black kerchief.

sentences.zh: 丈夫翦髮，錦袍。

translations.literal: Husbands cut their hair and wore brocade robes.
translations.idiomatic: Men cut their hair short and wore brocade robes.

sentences.zh: 名為強國，西域諸國多歸之。

translations.literal: It was called a powerful state, and many states of the Western Regions submitted to it.
translations.idiomatic: It was reckoned a powerful state, and many Western Region states submitted to it.

sentences.zh: 米國、史國、曹國、何國、安國、小安國、那色波國、烏那曷國、穆國皆歸附之。

translations.literal: Mi, Shi, Cao, He, An, Lesser An, Nashebo, Wunahe, and Mu all submitted to it.
translations.idiomatic: Mi, Shi, Cao, He, An, Lesser An, Nashebo, Wunahe, and Mu all submitted to it.

sentences.zh: 有胡律，置於祅祠，將決罰，則取而斷之。

translations.literal: There was a Hu code of law kept in the fire temple; when punishments were to be decided, it was taken out and judgment rendered by it.
translations.idiomatic: They had a Hu legal code kept in the fire temple; when punishments were to be decided, it was taken out and judgment rendered accordingly.

sentences.zh: 重者族，次罪者死，賊盜截其足。

translations.literal: For grave offenses the whole clan was punished; for lesser crimes death; thieves had their feet cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Grave offenses brought punishment on the whole clan; lesser crimes brought death; thieves had their feet cut off.

sentences.zh: 人皆深目、高鼻、多髯。

translations.literal: The people all had deep-set eyes, high noses, and many beards.
translations.idiomatic: The people had deep-set eyes, high noses, and heavy beards.

sentences.zh: 善商賈，諸夷交易，多湊其國。

translations.literal: Skilled in trade, many barbarian merchants gathered in their state for transactions.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled in commerce, many foreign merchants gathered there to trade.

sentences.zh: 有大小鼓、琵琶、五弦、箜篌。

translations.literal: They had large and small drums, pipa, five-string lutes, and konghou harps.
translations.idiomatic: They had large and small drums, pipa, five-string lutes, and konghou harps.

sentences.zh: 婚姻喪制與突厥同。

translations.literal: Marriage and mourning rites were the same as the Turks'.
translations.idiomatic: Marriage and mourning customs matched those of the Turks.

sentences.zh: 國立祖廟，以六月祭之，諸國皆助祭。

translations.literal: The state maintained an ancestral temple; in the sixth month they sacrificed to it, and all the states assisted in the rites.
translations.idiomatic: The state maintained an ancestral temple and sacrificed in the sixth month, with all the subject states assisting.

sentences.zh: 奉佛，為胡書。

translations.literal: They served the Buddha and used Hu script.
translations.idiomatic: They followed Buddhism and wrote in Hu script.

sentences.zh: 氣候溫，宜五穀，勤修園蔬，樹木滋茂。

translations.literal: The climate was mild; the five grains suited the land; they diligently tended gardens and vegetables, and trees flourished.
translations.idiomatic: The climate was mild; grain thrived; they diligently tended gardens and vegetables, and trees flourished.

sentences.zh: 出馬、駝、驢、犎牛、黃金、硇沙、<貝甘>香、阿薩那香、瑟瑟、麞皮、氍<叟毛>、錦、疊。

translations.literal: They produced horses, camels, donkeys, zebu, gold, sal ammoniac, Beigan incense, asana incense, sese, deer hide, soumao, brocade, and layered cloth.
translations.idiomatic: They produced horses, camels, donkeys, zebu, gold, sal ammoniac, Beigan incense, asana incense, sese, deerskin, soumao, brocade, and layered cloth.

sentences.zh: 多蒲桃酒，富家或致千石，連年不敗。

translations.literal: Grape wine was abundant; the wealthy sometimes stored a thousand shi, keeping it for years without spoiling.
translations.idiomatic: Grape wine was plentiful; wealthy households sometimes stored a thousand shi, keeping it for years without spoiling.

sentences.zh: 大業中，始遣使貢方物，後遂絕焉。

translations.literal: In the Daye reign they first sent envoys offering local products; afterward tribute ceased.
translations.idiomatic: In the Daye reign they first sent envoys with regional goods; afterward tribute ceased.

sentences.zh: 安國，漢時安息國也。

translations.literal: An was the Parthian state of Han times.
translations.idiomatic: An was the Parthian state known in Han times.

sentences.zh: 王姓昭武氏，與康國王同族，字設力；

translations.literal: The king's surname was Zhaowu, of the same clan as the king of Kang; his personal name was Sheli;
translations.idiomatic: The king bore the surname Zhaowu, of the same clan as the king of Kang; his personal name was Sheli;

sentences.zh: 妻，康國王女也。

translations.literal: his wife was the daughter of the king of Kang.
translations.idiomatic: his wife was the king of Kang's daughter.

sentences.zh: 都在那密水南，城有五重，環以流水，宮殿皆平頭。

translations.literal: The capital stood south of the Nami River; the city had five enclosures ringed by flowing water, and the palaces all had flat roofs.
translations.idiomatic: The capital stood south of the Nami River; the city had five enclosures ringed by flowing water, and the palaces all had flat roofs.

sentences.zh: 王坐金駝座，高七八尺，每聽政，與妻相對，大臣三人，評理國事。

translations.literal: The king sat on a golden camel throne seven or eight chi high; whenever he heard cases, he faced his wife; three great ministers assessed and settled state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The king sat on a golden camel throne seven or eight chi high; when he held court he faced his wife, while three great ministers assessed state affairs.

sentences.zh: 風俗同于康居，唯妻其姊妹及母子遞相禽獸，此為異也。

translations.literal: Customs were like Kangju's, except that they took their sisters as wives and mothers and sons in succession behaved like beasts toward one another—this was the difference.
translations.idiomatic: Customs resembled those of Kangju, save that they wed their sisters and practiced successive union between mothers and sons like beasts—this was the exceptional feature.

sentences.zh: 隋煬帝即位，遣司隸從事杜行滿使西域，至其國，得五色鹽而返。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang of Sui took the throne, he sent Director of Retainers Attendant Du Xingman as envoy to the Western Regions; reaching this state, he obtained five-colored salt and returned.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang of Sui ascended the throne, he sent Du Xingman of the Director of Retainers' staff as envoy to the Western Regions; reaching this state, he obtained five-colored salt and returned.

sentences.zh: 國西百餘里有畢國，可千餘家。

translations.literal: More than a hundred li west of the state was Bi, with perhaps a thousand-odd households.
translations.idiomatic: More than a hundred li west lay Bi, with perhaps a thousand-odd households.

sentences.zh: 其國無君長，安國統之。

translations.literal: That state had no ruler; An governed it.
translations.idiomatic: That state had no ruler of its own; An governed it.

sentences.zh: 大業五年，遣使貢獻。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Daye they sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In Daye 5 they sent tribute envoys.

sentences.zh: 石國，居於藥殺水，都城方十餘里。

translations.literal: The state of Shi dwelt on the Yaosha River; its capital was a little more than ten li square.
translations.idiomatic: Shi dwelt on the Yaosha River; its capital was a little more than ten li square.

sentences.zh: 其王姓石名涅。

translations.literal: Its king's surname was Shi and his personal name Nie.
translations.idiomatic: Its king bore the surname Shi and the personal name Nie.

sentences.zh: 國城東南立屋，置座於中。

translations.literal: Southeast of the capital city a hall was built with a seat placed within.
translations.idiomatic: Southeast of the capital they built a hall with a seat placed within.

sentences.zh: 正月六日，以王父母燒余之骨，金甕盛置床上，巡繞而行，散以花香雜果，王率臣下設祭焉。

translations.literal: On the sixth day of the first month they took the burnt bones of the king's parents, placed them in a golden urn on a couch, and walked around scattering flowers and mixed fruits; the king led his ministers in offering sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: On the first month's sixth day they placed the burnt bones of the king's parents in a golden urn on a couch, walked around scattering flowers and mixed fruits, and the king led his ministers in sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 禮終，王與夫人出就別帳，臣下以次列坐，享宴而罷。

translations.literal: When the rites ended, the king and his consort went to a separate tent while the ministers sat in order below, feasting before dispersing.
translations.idiomatic: When the rites ended, the king and his consort withdrew to a separate tent while the ministers sat in order and feasted before dispersing.

sentences.zh: 有粟、麥，多良馬。

translations.literal: There were millet and wheat, and many fine horses.
translations.idiomatic: They had millet and wheat and many fine horses.

sentences.zh: 其俗善戰。

translations.literal: Their custom favored warfare.
translations.idiomatic: They were warlike by custom.

sentences.zh: 曾貳於突厥，射匱可汗滅之，令特勤甸職攝其國事。

translations.literal: They had once sided with the Turks; Shekui qaghan destroyed them and had the special prince Tegin Dianzhi administer their state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: They had once sided with the Turks; qaghan Shekui destroyed them and had special prince Tegin Dianzhi administer their state affairs.

sentences.zh: 南去吲汗六百里，東南去瓜州六千里。

translations.literal: Six hundred li south to Yinhan, six thousand li southeast to Guazhou.
translations.idiomatic: It lay six hundred li south of Yinhan and six thousand li southeast of Guazhou.

sentences.zh: 甸職以隋大業五年遣使朝貢，後不復至。

translations.literal: Dianzhi sent envoys with tribute in Sui Daye 5; afterward they did not come again.
translations.idiomatic: Dianzhi sent tribute envoys in Sui Daye 5; afterward they came no more.

sentences.zh: 女國，在蔥嶺南。

translations.literal: The Women's State lay south of the Onion Range.
translations.idiomatic: The Women's State lay south of the Pamirs.

sentences.zh: 其國世以女為王，姓蘇毗，字末羯，在位二十年，女王夫號曰金聚，不知政事。

translations.literal: That state through the generations took a woman as king; the surname was Subi and the personal name Mojie; she reigned twenty years. The queen's husband was styled Jinjui and did not know state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: That state through the generations had a woman as king; the surname was Subi and the personal name Mojie; she reigned twenty years. The queen's husband was styled Jinjui and did not handle state affairs.

sentences.zh: 國內丈夫，唯以征伐為務。

translations.literal: Within the state the men devoted themselves only to campaigning.
translations.idiomatic: Within the state the men devoted themselves only to warfare.

sentences.zh: 山下為城，方五六里，人有萬家。

translations.literal: Below the mountain they had a city four or five li square, with ten thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Below the mountain stood a city four or five li square, with ten thousand households.

sentences.zh: 王居九層之樓，侍女數百人，五日一聽朝，復有小女王共知國政。

translations.literal: The queen lived in a nine-story tower; several hundred attendant women served her. Every five days she held court once, and a lesser queen jointly managed state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The queen lived in a nine-story tower attended by several hundred women; every five days she held court once, and a lesser queen jointly managed state affairs.

sentences.zh: 其俗婦人輕丈夫，而性不妒忌。

translations.literal: Their custom was for women to look down on husbands, yet they were not jealous by nature.
translations.idiomatic: By custom women looked down on their husbands, yet they were not jealous by nature.

sentences.zh: 男女皆以彩色塗面，而一日中或數度變改之。

translations.literal: Men and women all painted their faces in colors and might change them several times in a single day.
translations.idiomatic: Men and women all painted their faces in colors and might change the designs several times in a single day.

sentences.zh: 人皆被髮，以皮為鞋。

translations.literal: Everyone wore their hair loose and used hide for shoes.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone wore loose hair and made shoes of hide.

sentences.zh: 課稅無常。

translations.literal: Taxes were levied without fixed rule.
translations.idiomatic: Taxation had no fixed rule.

sentences.zh: 氣候多寒，以射獵為業。

translations.literal: The climate was mostly cold; hunting was their occupation.
translations.idiomatic: The climate was mostly cold; they lived by hunting.

sentences.zh: 出鍮石、硃砂、麝香、ＢＸ牛、駿馬、蜀馬。

translations.literal: They produced lead ore, cinnabar, musk, yak, fine horses, and Shu horses.
translations.idiomatic: They produced lead ore, cinnabar, musk, yaks, fine horses, and Shu horses.

sentences.zh: 尤多鹽，恆將鹽向天竺興販，其利數倍。

translations.literal: Salt was especially abundant; they constantly carried salt to trade in India, reaping several times the profit.
translations.idiomatic: Salt was especially abundant; they constantly carried it to trade in India for several times the profit.

sentences.zh: 亦數與天竺、党項戰爭。

translations.literal: They also frequently warred with India and the Tangut.
translations.idiomatic: They also frequently warred with India and the Tangut.

sentences.zh: 其女王死，國中厚斂金錢，求死者族中之賢女二人，一為女王，次為小王。

translations.literal: When their queen died, the state heavily collected gold and money and sought two worthy women from the dead woman's clan—one to be queen, the other lesser queen.
translations.idiomatic: When their queen died, the state collected gold heavily and sought two worthy women from the dead queen's clan—one as queen, one as lesser queen.

sentences.zh: 貴人死剝皮，以金屑和骨肉置瓶中，埋之。

translations.literal: When a noble died they flayed the skin, mixed the flesh and bones with gold dust, placed them in a jar, and buried them.
translations.idiomatic: When a noble died they flayed the skin, mixed flesh and bones with gold dust, placed them in a jar, and buried them.

sentences.zh: 經一年，又以其皮納鐵器埋之。

translations.literal: After a year they again placed the skin in an iron vessel and buried it.
translations.idiomatic: After a year they placed the skin in an iron vessel and buried it again.

sentences.zh: 俗事阿修羅神，又有樹神，歲初以人祭，或用獼猴。

translations.literal: By custom they served the Asura god; there was also a tree god, and at the year's start they sacrificed people—or sometimes gibbons.
translations.idiomatic: By custom they served the Asura god; they also had a tree god, and at the year's start sacrificed people—or sometimes gibbons.

sentences.zh: 祭畢，入山祝之，有一鳥如雌雉，來集掌上，破腹其視之，有眾粟則年豐，沙石則有災，謂之鳥卜。

translations.literal: When the sacrifice was finished they entered the mountains to pray; a bird like a hen pheasant came and alighted on the palm; they opened its belly and looked—if there was much millet the year would be abundant, if sand and stones there would be disaster; this was called bird divination.
translations.idiomatic: When the sacrifice ended they entered the mountains to pray; a bird like a hen pheasant alighted on the palm; they opened its belly and looked—much millet meant a plentiful year, sand and stones meant disaster; this was called bird divination.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇六年，遣使朝貢，後遂絕。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Sui Kaihuang they sent envoys with tribute; afterward tribute ceased.
translations.idiomatic: In Sui Kaihuang 6 they sent tribute envoys; afterward tribute ceased.

sentences.zh: 吲汗國，都蔥嶺之西五百餘里，古渠搜國也。

translations.literal: The state of Yinhan had its capital more than five hundred li west of the Onion Range; it was the ancient state of Qusou.
translations.idiomatic: Yinhan had its capital more than five hundred li west of the Pamirs; it was the ancient state of Qusou.

sentences.zh: 王姓昭武，字阿利柒。

translations.literal: The king's surname was Zhaowu; his personal name was Aliqi.
translations.idiomatic: The king bore the surname Zhaowu; his personal name was Aliqi.

sentences.zh: 都城方四里，勝兵數千人。

translations.literal: The capital was four li square; effective troops numbered several thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The capital was four li square; effective troops numbered several thousand.

sentences.zh: 王坐金羊床，妻戴金花。

translations.literal: The king sat on a golden ram couch; his wife wore golden flowers.
translations.idiomatic: The king sat on a golden ram throne; his consort wore golden flowers in her hair.

sentences.zh: 俗多硃砂、金、鐵。

translations.literal: Their customs included much cinnabar, gold, and iron.
translations.idiomatic: The region produced much cinnabar, gold, and iron.

sentences.zh: 東去疏勒千里，西去蘇對沙那國五百里，西北去石國五百里，東北去突厥可汗二千餘里，東去瓜州五千五百里。

translations.literal: One thousand li east to Kashgar, five hundred li west to Sogdiana, five hundred li northwest to Shi, more than two thousand li northeast to the Turk qaghan, five thousand five hundred li east to Guazhou.
translations.idiomatic: It lay a thousand li east of Kashgar, five hundred li west of Sogdiana, five hundred li northwest of Shi, more than two thousand li northeast of the Turk qaghan, and five thousand five hundred li east of Guazhou.

sentences.zh: 隋大業中，遣使貢方物。

translations.literal: During Sui Daye, they sent envoys presenting regional products.
translations.idiomatic: During the Sui Daye era, they sent envoys with regional tribute.

sentences.zh: 吐火羅國，都蔥嶺西五百里，與挹怛雜居。

translations.literal: The state of Tokhara had its capital five hundred li west of the Onion Range and lived intermixed with the Hephthalites.
translations.idiomatic: Tokhara had its capital five hundred li west of the Pamirs and lived intermixed with the Hephthalites.

sentences.zh: 都城方二里，勝兵者十萬人，皆善戰。

translations.literal: The capital was two li square; effective troops numbered one hundred thousand, all skilled in battle.
translations.idiomatic: The capital was two li square; effective troops numbered one hundred thousand, all skilled fighters.

sentences.zh: 其俗奉佛。

translations.literal: Their custom was to serve the Buddha.
translations.idiomatic: They followed Buddhism.

sentences.zh: 兄弟同一妻，迭寢焉，每一人入房，戶外掛其衣以為志，生子屬其長兄。

translations.literal: Brothers shared one wife and took turns sleeping with her; when one entered the chamber he hung his garment outside as a sign, and any child born belonged to the eldest brother.
translations.idiomatic: Brothers shared one wife and slept with her in turn; when one entered the room he hung his garment outside as a sign, and any child born belonged to the eldest brother.

sentences.zh: 其山穴中有神馬，每歲牧馬於穴所，必產名駒。

translations.literal: In a mountain cave there was a divine horse; each year they pastured horses at the cave and always produced famous colts.
translations.idiomatic: A mountain cave held a divine horse; each year they pastured horses there and always produced famous colts.

sentences.zh: 南去漕國千七百里，東去瓜州五千八百里。

translations.literal: One thousand seven hundred li south to Caoguo, five thousand eight hundred li east to Guazhou.
translations.idiomatic: It lay seventeen hundred li south of Caoguo and fifty-eight hundred li east of Guazhou.

sentences.zh: 大業中，遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: In the Daye reign they sent envoys to court with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the Daye reign they sent tribute envoys to court.

sentences.zh: 米國，都那密水西，舊康居之地。

translations.literal: The state of Mi had its capital west of the Nami River; it was old Kangju territory.
translations.idiomatic: Mi had its capital west of the Nami River, on the old Kangju lands.

sentences.zh: 無王，其城主姓昭武，康國王之支庶，字閉拙。

translations.literal: There was no king; the city lord bore the surname Zhaowu, a cadet of the king of Kang, with the personal name Bizhuo.
translations.idiomatic: It had no king; the city lord bore the surname Zhaowu, a cadet branch of the king of Kang, with the personal name Bizhuo.

sentences.zh: 都城方二里，勝兵數百人。

translations.literal: The capital was two li square; effective troops numbered several hundred.
translations.idiomatic: The capital was two li square; effective troops numbered several hundred.

sentences.zh: 西北去蘇對沙那國五百里，西南去史國二百里，東去瓜州六千四百里。

translations.literal: Five hundred li northwest to Sogdiana, two hundred li southwest to Shi, six thousand four hundred li east to Guazhou.
translations.idiomatic: It lay five hundred li northwest of Sogdiana, two hundred li southwest of Shi, and sixty-four hundred li east of Guazhou.

sentences.zh: 大業中，頻貢方物。

translations.literal: In the Daye reign they frequently offered regional products.
translations.idiomatic: In the Daye reign they frequently sent regional tribute.

sentences.zh: 史國，都獨莫水南十里，舊康居之地也。

translations.literal: The state of Shi had its capital ten li south of the Duemo River; it was old Kangju territory.
translations.idiomatic: Shi had its capital ten li south of the Duemo River, on the old Kangju lands.

sentences.zh: 其王姓照昭武，字狄遮，亦康國王之支庶也。

translations.literal: Its king bore the surname Zhaowu; his personal name was Dizhe; he too was a cadet of the king of Kang.
translations.idiomatic: Its king bore the surname Zhaowu; his personal name was Dizhe; he too was a cadet branch of the king of Kang.

sentences.zh: 都城方二里，勝兵千餘人。

translations.literal: The capital was two li square; effective troops numbered more than a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The capital was two li square; effective troops numbered more than a thousand.

sentences.zh: 俗同康國。

translations.literal: Customs were the same as Kang.
translations.idiomatic: Its customs matched those of Kang.

sentences.zh: 北去康國二百四十里，南吐火羅五百里，西去那色波國二百里，東北去米國二百里，東去瓜州六千五百里。

translations.literal: Two hundred forty li north to Kang, five hundred li south to Tokhara, two hundred li west to Nashebo, two hundred li northeast to Mi, six thousand five hundred li east to Guazhou.
translations.idiomatic: It lay two hundred forty li north of Kang, five hundred li south of Tokhara, two hundred li west of Nashebo, two hundred li northeast of Mi, and sixty-five hundred li east of Guazhou.

sentences.zh: 大業中，遣使貢方物。

translations.literal: In the Daye reign they sent envoys presenting regional products.
translations.idiomatic: In the Daye reign they sent envoys with regional tribute.

sentences.zh: 曹國，都那密水南數里，舊是康居之地也。

translations.literal: The state of Cao had its capital several li south of the Nami River; it was old Kangju territory.
translations.idiomatic: Cao had its capital several li south of the Nami River, on the old Kangju lands.

sentences.zh: 國無主，康國王令子烏建領之。

translations.literal: The state had no ruler; the king of Kang had his son Wujian administer it.
translations.idiomatic: The state had no ruler of its own; the king of Kang put his son Wujian in charge.

sentences.zh: 都城方三里，勝兵千餘人。

translations.literal: The capital was three li square; effective troops numbered more than a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The capital was three li square; effective troops numbered more than a thousand.

sentences.zh: 國中有得悉神，自西海以東諸國並敬事之，其神有金人，破羅闊丈有五尺，高下相稱，每日以駝五頭、馬十匹、羊一百口祭之，常有數千人，食之不盡。

translations.literal: In the state there was the god Dexi; from the Western Sea eastward all states alike revered him. The god had a golden image one zhang and five chi wide, proportionate in height and breadth; each day they sacrificed five camels, ten horses, and a hundred sheep to it, and several thousand people always attended—yet the food was never exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: The state worshipped the god Nana, revered from the Western Sea eastward by every realm. The deity had a golden image a zhang and five chi across, proportionate in height and width; each day they sacrificed five camels, ten horses, and a hundred sheep, and several thousand people feasted—yet the food never ran out.

sentences.zh: 東南去康國百里，西去何國百五十里，東去瓜州六千六百里。

translations.literal: One hundred li southeast to Kang, one hundred fifty li west to He, six thousand six hundred li east to Guazhou.
translations.idiomatic: It lay a hundred li southeast of Kang, a hundred fifty li west of He, and sixty-six hundred li east of Guazhou.

sentences.zh: 大業中，遣使貢方物。

translations.literal: In the Daye reign they sent envoys presenting regional products.
translations.idiomatic: In the Daye reign they sent envoys with regional tribute.

sentences.zh: 何國，都那密水南數里，舊是康居地也。

translations.literal: The state of He had its capital several li south of the Nami River; it was old Kangju territory.
translations.idiomatic: He had its capital several li south of the Nami River, on the old Kangju lands.

sentences.zh: 其王姓昭武，亦康國王之族類，字敦。

translations.literal: Its king bore the surname Zhaowu, of the same clan as the king of Kang; his personal name was Dun.
translations.idiomatic: Its king bore the surname Zhaowu, kin to the king of Kang; his personal name was Dun.

sentences.zh: 都城方二里，勝兵者千人。

translations.literal: The capital was two li square; effective troops numbered a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The capital was two li square; effective troops numbered a thousand.

sentences.zh: 其王坐金羊座。

translations.literal: Its king sat on a golden ram throne.
translations.idiomatic: Its king sat on a golden ram throne.

sentences.zh: 東去曹國百五十里，西去小安國三百里，東去瓜州六千七百五十里。

translations.literal: One hundred fifty li east to Cao, three hundred li west to Lesser An, six thousand seven hundred fifty li east to Guazhou.
translations.idiomatic: It lay a hundred fifty li east of Cao, three hundred li west of Lesser An, and sixty-seven hundred fifty li east of Guazhou.

sentences.zh: 大業中，遣使貢方物。

translations.literal: In the Daye reign they sent envoys presenting regional products.
translations.idiomatic: In the Daye reign they sent envoys with regional tribute.

sentences.zh: 烏那遏國，都烏滸水西，舊安息之地也。

translations.literal: The state of Wunahe had its capital west of the Wuhu River; it was old Parthian territory.
translations.idiomatic: Wunahe had its capital west of the Wuhu River, on the old Parthian lands.

sentences.zh: 王姓昭武，亦康國王種類，字佛食。

translations.literal: The king bore the surname Zhaowu, of the same stock as the king of Kang; his personal name was Foshi.
translations.idiomatic: The king bore the surname Zhaowu, of the same line as the king of Kang; his personal name was Foshi.

sentences.zh: 都城方二里，勝兵數百人。

translations.literal: The capital was two li square; effective troops numbered several hundred.
translations.idiomatic: The capital was two li square; effective troops numbered several hundred.

sentences.zh: 王坐金羊座。

translations.literal: The king sat on a golden ram throne.
translations.idiomatic: The king sat on a golden ram throne.

sentences.zh: 東北去安國四百里，西北去穆國二百餘里，東去瓜州七千五百里。

translations.literal: Four hundred li northeast to An, more than two hundred li northwest to Mu, seven thousand five hundred li east to Guazhou.
translations.idiomatic: It lay four hundred li northeast of An, more than two hundred li northwest of Mu, and seventy-five hundred li east of Guazhou.

sentences.zh: 大業中，遣使貢方物。

translations.literal: In the Daye reign they sent envoys presenting regional products.
translations.idiomatic: In the Daye reign they sent envoys with regional tribute.

sentences.zh: 穆國，都烏滸河之西，亦安息之故地，與烏那遏為鄰。

translations.literal: The state of Mu had its capital west of the Wuhu River; it too was old Parthian territory and bordered Wunahe.
translations.idiomatic: Mu had its capital west of the Wuhu River, on the old Parthian lands, and bordered Wunahe.

sentences.zh: 其王姓昭武，亦康國王之種類也，字阿濫密。

translations.literal: Its king bore the surname Zhaowu, of the same stock as the king of Kang; his personal name was Alanmi.
translations.idiomatic: Its king bore the surname Zhaowu, of the same line as the king of Kang; his personal name was Alanmi.

sentences.zh: 都城方三里，勝兵二千人。

translations.literal: The capital was three li square; effective troops numbered two thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The capital was three li square; effective troops numbered two thousand.

sentences.zh: 東北去安國五百里，東去烏那遏二百餘里，西去波斯國四千餘里，東去瓜州七千七百里。

translations.literal: Five hundred li northeast to An, more than two hundred li east to Wunahe, more than four thousand li west to Persia, seven thousand seven hundred li east to Guazhou.
translations.idiomatic: It lay five hundred li northeast of An, more than two hundred li east of Wunahe, more than four thousand li west of Persia, and seventy-seven hundred li east of Guazhou.

sentences.zh: 大業中，遣使貢方物。

translations.literal: In the Daye reign they sent envoys presenting regional products.
translations.idiomatic: In the Daye reign they sent envoys with regional tribute.

sentences.zh: 漕國，在蔥嶺之北，漢時罽賓國也。

translations.literal: Caoguo lay north of the Onion Range; it was the Jibin state of Han times.
translations.idiomatic: Caoguo lay north of the Pamirs; it was the Jibin state known in Han times.

sentences.zh: 其王姓昭武，字順達，康國王之宗族也。

translations.literal: Its king bore the surname Zhaowu; his personal name was Shunda; he was of the king of Kang's clan.
translations.idiomatic: Its king bore the surname Zhaowu; his personal name was Shunda; he belonged to the king of Kang's clan.

sentences.zh: 都城方四里，勝兵者萬餘人。

translations.literal: The capital was four li square; effective troops numbered more than ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The capital was four li square; effective troops numbered more than ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 國法嚴，殺人及賊盜皆死。

translations.literal: State law was strict; murderers and thieves all died.
translations.idiomatic: State law was strict: murderers and thieves were put to death.

sentences.zh: 其俗重淫祠，蔥嶺山有順天神者，儀制極華，金銀鍱為屋，以銀為地，祠者日有千餘人。

translations.literal: Their custom placed great weight on lavish shrines; on a Pamirs mountain there was the Shun Heaven god, whose rites were extremely splendid—gold and silver plates formed the roof, silver served as flooring, and more than a thousand worshippers came each day.
translations.idiomatic: They favored lavish cults; on a Pamir peak stood the Shun Heaven god, whose rites were magnificently appointed—gold and silver plates roofed the shrine, silver paved the floor, and more than a thousand worshippers came each day.

sentences.zh: 祠前有一魚脊骨，有孔，中通馬騎出入。

translations.literal: Before the shrine was a fish spine bone with a hole through it, large enough for horsemen to pass in and out.
translations.idiomatic: Before the shrine stood a fish spine with a hole through it wide enough for horsemen to ride through.

sentences.zh: 國王戴金牛頭冠，坐金馬座。

translations.literal: The king wore a golden ox-head crown and sat on a golden horse throne.
translations.idiomatic: The king wore a golden ox-head crown and sat on a golden horse throne.

sentences.zh: 多稻、粟、豆、麥，饒象、馬、犎牛、金、銀、鑌鐵、氍<叟毛>、硃沙、青黛、安息青木等香、石蜜、黑監、阿魏、沒藥、白附子。

translations.literal: There was much rice, millet, beans, and wheat; abundant elephants, horses, zebu, gold, silver, wootz steel, soumao, cinnabar, indigo, aromatics such as Parthian eaglewood, rock sugar, black salt, asafetida, myrrh, and white aconite.
translations.idiomatic: It produced rice, millet, beans, and wheat in abundance; elephants, horses, zebu, gold, silver, wootz steel, soumao, cinnabar, indigo, Parthian eaglewood and other aromatics, rock sugar, black salt, asafetida, myrrh, and white aconite.

sentences.zh: 去北帆延七百里，東去劫國六百里，東北去瓜州六千六百里。

translations.literal: Seven hundred li north to Fanyan, six hundred li east to Jie, six thousand six hundred li northeast to Guazhou.
translations.idiomatic: It lay seven hundred li north of Fanyan, six hundred li east of Jie, and sixty-six hundred li northeast of Guazhou.

sentences.zh: 大業中，遣使貢方物。

translations.literal: In the Daye reign they sent envoys presenting regional products.
translations.idiomatic: In the Daye reign they sent envoys with regional tribute.

sentences.zh: 論曰：自古開遠夷，通絕域，必因宏放之主，皆起好事之臣。

translations.literal: Commentary: From antiquity, opening distant barbarians and connecting cut-off realms has always required a magnanimous sovereign—and always produced officials eager for adventure.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: From antiquity, reaching distant peoples and opening cut-off realms has always depended on a magnanimous sovereign—and always summoned officials eager for grand ventures.

sentences.zh: 張騫鑿空于前，班超投筆於後，或結之以重寶，或懾之以利劍，投軀萬死之地，必要一旦之功，皆由主尚來遠之名，臣徇輕生之節。

translations.literal: Zhang Qian opened the blank west before them; Ban Chao laid down his brush after. Some were bound by heavy treasure, others awed by sharp swords; they cast themselves into lands of ten thousand deaths, demanding success in a single stroke—all because the ruler prized the fame of drawing the distant, and the minister pursued the honor of reckless valor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Qian opened the blank west; Ban Chao later laid down his brush. Some were won with heavy treasure, others cowed with sharp swords; they threw themselves into lands where death waited at every turn, bent on a single day's triumph—all because the ruler craved the fame of drawing the distant, and the minister sought the glory of throwing his life away.

sentences.zh: 是知上之所好，不必效焉。

translations.literal: From this we know that what the sovereign favors need not be imitated.
translations.idiomatic: From this we know that what the ruler favors is not necessarily worth imitating.

sentences.zh: 西域雖通于魏氏，于時中原始平，天子方以混一為心，未遑及此。

translations.literal: Though the Western Regions had contact with Wei, at the time the Central Plain was not yet pacified; the Son of Heaven had his heart set on unification and had no leisure for this.
translations.idiomatic: Though the Western Regions had contact with Wei, the Central Plain was not yet pacified; the Son of Heaven had his heart set on unification and had no leisure for distant affairs.

sentences.zh: 其信使往來，得羈縻勿絕之道。

translations.literal: Envoy exchanges sufficed to obtain the way of loose control without severing ties.
translations.idiomatic: Envoy exchanges alone sufficed to keep the ties of loose control from breaking.

sentences.zh: 及隋煬帝規摹宏侈，掩吞秦、漢，裴矩方進《西域圖記》以蕩其心，故萬乘親出玉門關，置伊吾、且末鎮，而關右暨於流沙，騷然無聊生矣。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang of Sui designed on a vast and extravagant scale, swallowing Qin and Han in ambition, Pei Ju presented "Records of the Western Regions" to inflame his heart; so the lord of ten thousand chariots went in person beyond Yumen Pass, established garrisons at Yiwu and Qiemo, and from Guanxi west to the shifting sands the people were in turmoil with nowhere to live in peace.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang of Sui planned on a vast and extravagant scale, ambition swallowing Qin and Han whole, Pei Ju presented "Records of the Western Regions" to stir his desires; so the ten-thousand-chariot lord went in person beyond Yumen Pass, established garrisons at Yiwu and Qiemo, and from Guanxi west to the shifting sands the people were in turmoil, with nowhere to live in peace.

sentences.zh: 若使北狄無虞，東夷告捷，必將修輪台之戍，築烏壘之城，求大秦之明珠，致條支之鳥卵，往來轉輸，將何以堪其弊哉！

translations.literal: Had the northern barbarians given no trouble and the eastern Yi reported victory, he would surely have restored the garrison at Luntai, built the fortress at Wulei, sought the bright pearls of Daqin, and brought the birds' eggs of Tiaozhi—constantly shipping goods back and forth; how could the realm have borne such ruin!
translations.idiomatic: Had the northern barbarians stayed quiet and the eastern Yi brought good news, he would surely have restored the Luntai garrison, built the fortress at Wulei, sought Daqin's bright pearls, and fetched Tiaozhi's birds' eggs—goods shuttling back and forth without end; how could the realm have borne such ruin!

sentences.zh: 古者哲王之制也，方五千里，務安諸夏，不事要荒。

translations.literal: The ancient wise kings' rule was a domain five thousand li square; they sought to secure the various Xia and did not serve the distant wastes.
translations.idiomatic: The ancient wise kings ruled a domain five thousand li square; they sought to secure the Central States and did not trouble themselves with the distant wastes.

sentences.zh: 豈威不能加，德不能被？

translations.literal: Was it that their might could not reach so far, or their virtue could not cover them?
translations.idiomatic: Was it that their might could not reach that far, or their virtue could not extend there?

sentences.zh: 蓋不以四夷勞中國，不以無用害有用也。

translations.literal: Rather, they would not wear out China for the four barbarians, nor let the useless harm the useful.
translations.idiomatic: Rather, they would not exhaust China for the four barbarians, nor let the useless drain the useful.

sentences.zh: 是以秦戍五嶺，漢事三邊，或道殣相望，或戶口減半。

translations.literal: Hence Qin garrisoned the Five Ridges and Han struggled on three frontiers; corpses lined the roads or households were halved.
translations.idiomatic: Hence Qin garrisoned the Five Ridges and Han fought on three frontiers—corpses lined the roads, or households were cut in half.

sentences.zh: 隋室恃其強盛，亦狼狽于青海。

translations.literal: The Sui house, trusting in its strength, also came to grief on the Qinghai.
translations.idiomatic: The Sui house, trusting in its strength, also came to grief on the Qinghai frontier.

sentences.zh: 此皆一人失其道，故億兆罹其苦。

translations.literal: All this because one man lost the Way, and the millions suffered for it.
translations.idiomatic: All because one man lost the Way, and the millions suffered for it.

sentences.zh: 載思即敘之義，固辭都護之請，返其千里之馬，不求白狼之貢，則七戎九夷，候風重譯，雖無遼東之捷，豈及江都之禍乎！

translations.literal: Remembering the principle of immediate order, firmly declining requests for protectors-general, returning the thousand-li horses, not seeking the tribute of the white wolf—then the seven Rong and nine Yi would wait on the wind and retranslate through many tongues; though without victory in Liaodong, would they have reached the disaster of Jiangdu!
translations.idiomatic: Had one borne in mind the principle of immediate order, firmly declined requests for protectors-general, returned the thousand-li horses, and not sought the white wolf's tribute, then the seven Rong and nine Yi would have waited on the wind and sent envoys through many interpreters—without victory in Liaodong, would disaster at Jiangdu ever have come!

sentences.zh: 案西域開於往漢，年世積久，雖離並多端，見聞殊說，此所以前書後史，踳駁不同，豈其好異，地遠故也。

translations.literal: The Western Regions were opened in former Han; years and generations piled up; though states split and merged in many ways and reports differed—this is why earlier histories and later records disagree. Is it love of novelty? It is because the land is far.
translations.idiomatic: The Western Regions were opened in former Han; ages piled up; states split and merged in many ways and eyewitness accounts diverged—this is why earlier histories and later records clash. Is it love of novelty? The land is simply far away.

sentences.zh: 人之所知，未若其所不知，信矣。

translations.literal: What people know is never equal to what they do not know—how true that is.
translations.idiomatic: What people know is never equal to what they do not know—truly so.

sentences.zh: 但可取其梗概，夫何是非其間哉？

translations.literal: One may take only the broad outline—why judge right and wrong among these?
translations.idiomatic: One may take only the broad outline—why quibble over right and wrong among these?
